llm.novelty_zh: 构建人类基底节8个区域的单细胞组蛋白修饰与转录组图谱，并用深度学习预测调控活性与变异效应。
llm.summary_zh: 作者建立人类基底节的单细胞多组学图谱，覆盖8个区域的活性与抑制性顺式调控元件，并解析基于同源框转录因子的细胞身份组合。结合MERFISH空间转录组，揭示区域异质性，并训练深度学习模型预测基因调控活性和非编码风险变异效应。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为解释神经精神疾病的非编码风险变异提供了参考框架，对人类脑细胞调控图谱研究有用。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及模型在未见细胞类型或扰动条件下的预测性能。

title: Circuit-aligned specialization of human basal ganglia astrocytes
abstract: Astrocytes shape synapses and circuits, yet their diversity within the human basal ganglia remains poorly defined. Integrating single-nucleus transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with spatial transcriptomics, we identify three anatomically organized astrocyte subgroups-striatal gray matter (GM), extra-striatal GM, and white matter (WM)-distinguished by neurotransmitter transporter expression and synapse-associated programs that reflect afferent input. These molecular distinctions generalize brain-wide, separating telencephalic from non-telencephalic astrocytes, with LHX2 marking telencephalic astrocyte identity across species. Within the striatum (STR), dorsal and ventral populations align with distinct microcircuits; a ventral population maps to the nucleus accumbens mediodorsal shell alongside specialized neuronal subtypes, a pattern conserved in nonhuman primates. A deep learning sequence model identifies subgroup-specific enhancer codes and recovers established transcription factor motif logic from published enhancer-AAV datasets, providing a foundation for targeted viral vector design. These findings define intersecting axes of human astrocyte specialization and offer a framework for cell-type-specific dissection of basal ganglia circuits.
affiliations: VIB-KU Leuven Center for Brain & Disease Research

llm.novelty_zh: 发现人类基底节星形胶质细胞按解剖与突触输入形成三类亚群，并给出跨物种保守性证据。
llm.summary_zh: 研究整合单核转录组、表观组与空间转录组，将基底节星形胶质细胞分为纹状体灰质、纹状体外灰质和白质三类。作者还用深度序列模型识别亚群特异性增强子编码，并在非人灵长类中观察到类似模式。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为人类基底节细胞类型分化和靶向病毒载体设计提供了细胞亚群与增强子层面的参考。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及深度模型的验证细节和样本来源的局限。

title: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and 3D genome atlas of the human basal ganglia
abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) underlie motor control, reward processing, and many neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet cell-type-resolved epigenomic and 3D genome maps of the human BG remain limited. Here, we present a multimodal single-cell atlas of DNA methylation (261,331 nuclei) and 3D chromatin conformation (229,286 nuclei) from eight subregions, harmonized under the BG consensus taxonomy and integrated with matched data across multiple regulatory layers. We identify millions of differentially methylated regions across cell types, enriched for distinct transcription factor motifs, and link them to disease-associated heritability. We characterize the POU6F2+ STR D2 SMYD2-HTR7 spiny projection neuron (SPN) subtype, with concordant signatures across multiple modalities, and reveal region-specific methylation and contact gradients. Integrative gene regulatory networks (GRNs) predict cell-type-resolved enhancer-promoter interactions, nominating candidate regulatory mechanisms for Parkinson's disease (PD) risk variants at SNCA. Finally, multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) profiling combined with cross-species Patch-seq identifies a neuronal subtype, STR FS PTHLH-PVALB GABA, with electrophysiological differences across the striatal matrix-striosome (MS) boundary.

llm.novelty_zh: 联合构建人类基底节单细胞DNA甲基化与三维染色质构象图谱，并与多层调控数据整合。
llm.summary_zh: 作者构建了人类基底节8个亚区的单细胞DNA甲基化（261,331个细胞核）和三维染色质构象（229,286个细胞核）图谱，并统一到基底节共识分类体系下。研究鉴定了POU6F2+ SPN亚型，并通过整合调控网络预测帕金森风险变异位点SNCA附近的增强子-启动子互作。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为理解基底节细胞类型特异的表观调控及帕金森风险机制提供了大规模资源。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及跨个体变异和功能验证的范围。

title: Stepping (hi)stones: Charting a single-cell multiomic path toward understanding the human brain
Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are interconnected subcortical nuclei with a complex topographical organization that orchestrate goal-directed behaviors and are implicated in neurodegenerative movement disorders. We generated a cellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics atlas of the BG in human, rhesus macaque, and common marmoset, sampling over one million cells in each species. By integrating spatial data with a cross-species consensus single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cell-type taxonomy, this atlas reveals principles of molecular organization within and across structures. Extensive spatial sampling across the rostral-caudal axis illuminates complex, yet highly stereotyped, multi-axis gene expression gradients superimposed onto discrete compartments of the striatum. Additionally, we identify core-shell organization of the internal globus pallidus. This unified, cross-species spatial transcriptomics atlas will be a foundational resource for characterizing the molecular and functional organization of the BG and their roles in health and disease.
affiliations: RIKEN Center for Biosystems Dynamics Research

new_dataset_names: cross-species basal ganglia spatial transcriptomics atlas
llm.novelty_zh: 构建人、恒河猴与普通狨基底神经节的跨物种细胞分辨率空间转录组图谱。
llm.summary_zh: 研究者在人、恒河猴和普通狨中生成了基底神经节的细胞分辨率空间转录组图谱，每个物种采样超过一百万个细胞，并与跨物种 snRNA-seq 细胞类型分类整合。结果揭示了纹状体内离散的分区、多轴基因表达梯度以及苍白球的核心-外壳结构。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该图谱为基底神经节的分子组织研究提供了跨物种基础资源，对神经退行性疾病研究有参考价值，但与虚拟细胞建模的关联较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Toward an integrated framework for a human and mammalian brain cell atlas
abstract: The NIH BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is developing a standardized, integrated reference framework for classifying and studying brain cell types across human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse. We present a cross-species, multimodal atlas of the basal ganglia, a group of subcortical nuclei central to motor control, adaptive behavior, and neurological disease. Built from large-scale single-cell transcriptomic classification and integrated with epigenomic, spatial genomic, multiomic, and developmental datasets, the atlas provides a curated, data-driven taxonomy with standardized nomenclature, extensive phenotypic characterization, and community-informed annotation. Cell types are mapped into species-specific anatomical reference frameworks and linked across species through structural ontologies. Realizing this resource required coordinated standards for tissue acquisition and processing, harmonized donor metadata, anatomical registration, sequencing pipelines, data infrastructure, visualization, mapping tools, and interoperable metadata. The BICAN basal ganglia atlas demonstrates how pipelines and standards can be implemented, validated, and scaled toward a whole-brain human and mammalian cell-type reference.

llm.novelty_zh: 建立跨物种基底节多模态细胞类型图谱，并给出标准化命名与解剖映射框架。
llm.summary_zh: 研究基于大规模单细胞转录组分类，整合表观基因组、空间基因组与多组学数据，构建基底节细胞类型分类体系。作者将细胞类型映射到人、猕猴、狨猴和小鼠的解剖框架，并讨论了实现该参考体系的标准化流程。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为全脑人类与哺乳动物细胞类型参考图谱建立了可扩展的标准和流程。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及各物种之间映射的不确定性。

title: NANOG and OCT4 dosage shapes non-monotonic gene expression responses during stem cell differentiation
abstract: Precise regulation of transcription factor (TF) expression is critical for maintaining cell identity, but studies on how graded expression levels affect cellular phenotypes are limited. To address this gap, we employed human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) as a dynamic model to study gene dosage effects and systematically titrated key TFs NANOG and OCT4 expression using CRISPR interference (CRISPRi). We then profiled transcriptomic changes in hESCs under self-renewal and definitive endoderm (DE) differentiation conditions using single-cell RNA-seq. Quantitative modeling of these Perturb-seq datasets uncovered distinct response patterns for different types of genes, including a striking non-monotonic up-regulation of on-target lineage genes during DE differentiation. This behavior extended to the ESC-to-neuroectoderm transition, suggesting non-monotonic responses of lineage genes to pluripotency regulator dosage are a recurring feature of lineage transitions. Together, these findings underscore the importance of characterizing TF function across a gradient of expression levels.

llm.novelty_zh: 系统滴定NANOG与OCT4表达剂量，揭示谱系基因的非单调响应是多次谱系转变的共性特征。
llm.summary_zh: 作者利用CRISPRi对hESC中的NANOG和OCT4进行表达滴定，并结合单细胞RNA测序分析自我更新与定型内胚层分化中的转录响应。定量建模显示，部分谱系基因在DE分化中呈现非单调上调，该现象也出现在ESC向神经外胚层转变中。

title: Transcription factor THAP1 regulates cell fate transition genes during embryonic gastrulation through METTL3
abstract: Early embryonic gastrulation requires precise cell fate decisions. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification regulates transcriptome dynamics during cell fate transitions but its upstream transcriptional regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify THAP1 as a direct transcriptional regulator of METTL3, the core m6A methyltransferase. THAP1 loss reduces METTL3 expression and global m6A levels, impairing the activation of genes involved in cell fate transition-associated signaling pathways in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) and rat embryos. Ectopic METTL3 expression in THAP1-knockout mESCs largely rescues transcriptional dysregulation and partially restores m6A modification, RNA stability, and translation. Single-cell RNA sequencing of rat embryos further reveals reduced METTL3 expression and impaired signaling associated with cell fate transitions upon THAP1 loss. Together, these findings establish a conserved THAP1-METTL3 regulatory axis that supports gene expression programs associated with early embryonic cell fate transitions and suggest that its disruption contributes, at least in part, to embryonic lethality following THAP1 deletion.
affiliations: Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics

llm.novelty_zh: 鉴定 THAP1 为 METTL3 的直接转录调控因子，建立了胚胎发育中的 THAP1-METTL3 调控轴。
llm.summary_zh: 研究鉴定 THAP1 为 m6A 甲基转移酶 METTL3 的直接转录调控因子。THAP1 缺失会降低 METTL3 表达与整体 m6A 水平，并削弱 mESC 与大鼠胚胎中细胞命运转换相关基因的激活。在 THAP1 敲除的 mESC 中外源表达 METTL3 可部分挽救转录与 RNA 稳定性的异常。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 阐明了 m6A 修饰在胚胎细胞命运转换中的上游转录调控机制。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Single hepatocellular carcinoma cells regenerate transcriptional and copy-number heterogeneity in patient-derived organoids
abstract: Intratumor heterogeneity is a hallmark of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that contributes to therapy resistance and poor clinical outcomes. Using patient-derived HCC organoids (HCCOs), we examine whether this diversity can be regenerated from single tumor cells. Across nine HCCO lines, a large proportion of individual cells give rise to new organoids, indicating that clonogenic capacity is broadly distributed rather than confined to a rare subset. Single-cell-derived HCCOs (scd-HCCOs) regenerate heterogeneous marker expression and display variable proliferation and drug responses. Single-cell RNA sequencing shows that parental and clonal organoids share a common repertoire of transcriptional states, with individual scd-HCCOs differing mainly in the relative abundance of these states. Serial single-cell cloning shows that functional traits diversify again in each generation, and whole-exome sequencing reveals few new point mutations but substantial copy-number variation. Single HCC cells therefore regenerate the marker, transcriptional, and functional diversity of the organoids they derive from.

llm.novelty_zh: 证明肝癌患者来源类器官的单个细胞可再生出原有的转录与功能异质性。
llm.summary_zh: 研究使用九条肝癌类器官系，发现多数单细胞能形成新的类器官。单细胞测序显示母本与克隆类器官的转录状态谱相似，但比例不同，多代克隆后功能性状仍会分化。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 说明肝癌异质性具有可再生性，有助于理解治疗耐药的来源。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要提到全外显子测序仅发现少量点突变，但拷贝数变异较为显著，未涉及更多机制解释。

title: Single-cell multiomics analysis reveals Cxcl12 enhancer inactivation in LepRhigh-MSCs driving niche dysfunction in murine myeloid malignancies
abstract: Blood cancers profoundly disrupt the bone marrow microenvironment, compromising its support for normal hematopoiesis. Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs), particularly Leptin receptor -high MSCs (LepR high -MSCs), are crucial niche components whose function is altered in diseases such as myeloid leukemia. Here, we employed single-cell multiomic RNA/ATAC-seq to comprehensively map changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility in MSCs from murine myeloid malignancy models. This unbiased analysis identified multiple regions of closed chromatin adjacent to niche-factor genes. Notably, we discovered a previously unrecognized enhancer downstream of Cxcl12 , exclusively accessible in healthy LepR high -MSCs and regulated by the transcription factor Foxc1, whose expression is downregulated in LepR high -MSCs of myeloid malignancies. These results are consistent with a trend observed in deconvolved patient sequence data, and disruption of the enhancer impairs Cxcl12 expression for normal hematopoiesis. Collectively, these findings reveal a critical transcription factor-chromatin-mRNA regulatory axis that maintains hematopoietic niche integrity, highlighting a hidden regulatory vulnerability underlying blood cancers.

llm.summary_zh: 研究利用单细胞RNA与ATAC联合测序绘制髓系恶性肿瘤小鼠模型中MSC的染色质与转录变化。作者发现一个仅在健康LepR-high MSC中开放的Cxcl12增强子，由Foxc1调控，其破坏会损害造血龛功能。

title: A Key Piece of the Whole-Cell Puzzle: Mechanistic signaling for interpretable whole-cell models
abstract: Cellular signaling orchestrates how cells sense and respond to their environment by coupling extracellular cues to gene regulation and metabolism. As efforts toward human whole-cell models accelerate, representing signaling at mechanistic resolution is increasingly important for integrating cellular processes into coherent models that explain and predict cellular behavior. At the same time, AI virtual cells are emerging as a promising direction, supported by progress in single-cell foundation models, perturbation-response prediction, and multimodal learning. Although these approaches can predict cell states and responses, they often do not explain which molecular mechanisms drive cellular phenotypes, hindering hypothesis prioritization for experimental testing and therapeutic targeting. Unifying learning-based approaches with causal models grounded in prior knowledge could bridge this interpretability gap by encoding established cellular mechanisms through molecular states, causal interactions, and biological constraints. A key aspect of such unification is representing signaling beyond pathway-level activity as mechanistic cascades that capture biochemical dependencies, crosstalk, alternative routing, and intervention points. In this Opinion, we discuss computational frameworks that reconstruct biochemical signaling networks using omics data and offer a basis for mechanistically linking extracellular stimuli to transcriptional regulation and metabolic control. Such frameworks could serve as scaffolds for future whole-cell models that also account for the dynamic, stochastic, spatial, physical, and multiscale realities of the living cell. Together, causal models of signaling and learning-based advances could support interpretable whole-cell models for mechanistic hypothesis generation and intervention design.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出以机理化信号网络为骨架、结合因果模型与学习方法的可解释全细胞模型观点。
llm.summary_zh: 这篇 Opinion 讨论了如何利用组学数据重建生化信号网络，把细胞外刺激与转录调控和代谢控制机械地联系起来，并主张将因果模型与基于先验知识的学习方法统一起来，作为可解释全细胞模型的基础。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为 AI 虚拟细胞与全细胞建模之间的衔接提供了机理层面的视角。
llm.limitations_zh: 作为观点性文章，摘要未给出实验验证或具体的定量结果。

title: scREFINE: Label-efficient refinement of frozen scGPT embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering.
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) clustering remains challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, technical noise, and limited cell annotations. Here, we propose scREFINE, a label-efficient semi-supervised clustering framework that adapts pretrained single-cell foundation-model embeddings for accurate cell clustering. scREFINE uses a lightweight refinement head to map cells into a task-specific clustering space using only 5% labeled cells, while treating the remaining cells as unlabeled during training. To exploit information from unlabeled cells, scREFINE introduces stability-aware soft structural regularization over local neighborhoods, which leverages reliable cell-cell relations as auxiliary guidance without relying on hard pseudo-label constraints. Experiments on five benchmark scRNA-seq datasets show that scREFINE achieves the best ARI on every dataset against every baseline under an identical, leakage-free protocol (mean ± SD over four seeds). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the five per-dataset means yields p=0.0625, above the conventional 0.05 threshold because only five datasets are available; we therefore interpret the consistent improvements as strong empirical evidence rather than a statistically conclusive demonstration. A common-embedding comparison confirms that these gains arise from task-specific refinement rather than the pretrained representation alone: adapted baselines receiving identical embeddings achieve 0.00-0.61 ARI, compared with 0.73-0.89 for scREFINE. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that task-specific embedding refinement is the primary driver of improvement, whereas soft structural regularization provides dataset-dependent auxiliary gains and degrades more gracefully than hard pseudo-labels when supervision is scarce. Biological marker-gene analysis confirms that the predicted clusters correspond to canonical cell populations.

title: An integrated single-cell and epigenomic resource for comparative analysis of the basal ganglia from BICAN
abstract: The basal ganglia regulate motor, cognitive, and affective behaviors, and their dysfunction underlies diverse neurological and psychiatric disorders. Comprehensive, accessible multi-omics resources are needed to understand the regulatory mechanisms governing basal ganglia cell types. Here, we present an open, interactive web-based platform for exploring single-cell multi-omics datasets from basal ganglia, generated using 10X Multiome, single-nucleus methylome and chromatin conformation sequencing (snm3C-seq), and Paired-Tag technologies by the BICAN (NIH BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network) consortium. The platform is available at https://basalganglia.epigenomes.net/and enables integrated visualization of gene expression, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, histone modifications, and chromatin conformation across cell types and human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse species, with direct genome browser support and comparative epigenomic functionality. Representative analyses demonstrate cell-type-specific regulatory landscapes, conserved and species-specific regulatory elements, and links between epigenomic regulation and transcription. This resource provides a scalable, community-oriented foundation for advancing basal ganglia biology and interpreting regulatory mechanisms relevant to brain function and disease.

title: MapMyCells: High-performance mapping of cell-by-gene data to reference brain taxonomies
abstract: Single-cell reference mapping is increasingly central to translating heterogeneous datasets into consistent representations of cell identity. As cell-type atlases expand in scale and complexity, mapping new data to shared references enables reproducible annotation, cross-study integration, and accumulation of biological knowledge. We present MapMyCells, an open-source, high-performance framework for mapping diverse single-cell omics datasets to hierarchical reference taxonomies with minimal preprocessing. MapMyCells currently supports six diverse brain references spanning whole mouse and human brain, Alzheimer's disease and aging cohorts, developing mouse cortex, and a cross-species basal ganglia taxonomy. Across these references, MapMyCells accurately recovers cell identities at broad and intermediate taxonomic levels, remains robust with reduced informative gene panels, and supports transcriptomic, epigenomic, and spatial datasets. Benchmarking shows competitive accuracy with substantially lower computational requirements, enabling datasets and taxonomies containing thousands of cell types to be analyzed on standard workstations. MapMyCells provides a scalable framework for unified, extensible brain cell atlases.

title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells
abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of gene expression data. Additionally, PIANO achieves robust integrations and trains 10× faster than previous methods. PIANO accurately integrates single-cell data across species and across single-cell and spatial transcriptomics modalities. As practical applications, PIANO models spatially resolved gene expression during Alzheimer's disease progression in human brains and integrates over 100 million cancer cells to model drug perturbations. In summary, PIANO's integration and generative modeling capabilities will empower novel insights for a wide range of future studies.

title: multiVIB: A unified probabilistic contrastive learning framework for atlas-scale integration of single-cell multi-omics data
abstract: Integrating heterogeneous single-cell datasets requires aligning shared biological features while preserving meaningful variation across modalities, studies, and species. Here, we present multiVIB, a unified framework combining the variational information bottleneck with probabilistic contrastive learning for horizontal, vertical, and mosaic integration of single-cell multi-omics data. Across diverse benchmarks, multiVIB achieves competitive integration performance while minimizing spurious alignments. Applied to BRAIN Initiative atlas-scale datasets, multiVIB enables incremental integration of nine molecular modalities in the mouse primary motor cortex and cross-species integration of primate basal ganglia transcriptomes, recovering conserved cell identities and species-specific molecular programs. Together, these results establish multiVIB as a versatile framework for scalable, biologically faithful construction and expansion of comprehensive brain cell atlases.

title: A connectome and transcriptome identity shift through a single transcription factor isoform.
abstract: The brain exhibits remarkable neuronal diversity. The sheer number of cell types emerging from extensive transcriptional, morphological, and connectome datasets provokes the question of how the brain is capable of generating so many unique identities. Proper neuronal specification and subsequent features of identity, such as wiring, are essential for normal cognitive and behavioral function. However, we still know little about how identity and wiring are encoded within developmental programs. Here, we turn to the visual system of Drosophila melanogaster. We use its unprecedented combination of single-synapse-resolution wiring diagrams from electron microscopy (EM) connectomes and developmental gene expression profiles from single-cell transcriptomic atlases to study the molecular basis of cell-type-specific terminal identity specification and downstream wiring patterns. We integrate analyses of neuronal anatomy, whole-cell electrophysiology, and single-cell RNA sequencing after perturbation (scRNA-Perturb-seq) to establish that the transcription factor broad functions to control terminal features of identity between two visual projection neuron cell types, LPLC1 and LPLC2. We demonstrate the first characterization in functional connectivity changes following changes in neuronal identity specification. We find broad acts through a single isoform (broad-z4) that is selectively expressed in LPLC1 and has the capacity to reprogram the morphology, functional connectivity, and transcriptional identity of postmitotic LPLC2 neurons into an LPLC1-like cell type. Our findings establish a single transcription factor isoform as the smallest unit required to differentiate neuronal identity, a strategy that may be conserved within developmental programs to expand the capacity for cell-type diversity across animal species.

title: Systematic evaluation of DINO-based self-supervised deep learning to decode cellular state heterogeneity
abstract: Characterising cellular phenotypic heterogeneity is central to understanding the morphological and molecular determinants of cellular state. Self-supervised vision transformers (ViTs) have emerged as powerful tools for this task, yet how architectural choices and successive advances in self-supervised learning shape their representations for high-content microscopy remains poorly understood. Here we systematically benchmark DINO-based self-supervised learning for single-cell immune phenotyping, comparing conventional feature-based image analysis, publicly available pretrained DINO-family ViTs, and custom-trained variants spanning the successive DINO, DINOv2, and DINOv3 training regimes and their associated architectural changes. Using a dataset of more than 1.3 million primary human immune cells across seven immune cell types, we find that custom DINOv2-trained ViTs, without seeing any labels during training, learn the most accurate representations reaching 91.84% kNN top-1 accuracy compared to 76.54% for conventional image analysis. These models further combine fast and scalable inference with data-efficient training, while extracting biologically meaningful features reflecting both lineage-specific protein expression and cell morphology. By making these approaches openly available within a unified framework, scDINOv2, we aim to lower the barrier for self-supervised phenotyping and support the unsupervised study of cellular state heterogeneity and de novo phenotype discovery in high-content imaging.

title: Artificial intelligence virtual patients
abstract: Translating fine-grained intracellular dynamics into predictable systemic clinical phenotypes remains a core challenge in biomedical research. This review explores the architectural continuum and translational value of artificial intelligence (AI) virtual patients (AIVPs) for bridging the gap between microscale biological mechanisms and macroscale clinical manifestations. We clarify the computational hierarchy of AIVPs, covering AI-based virtual cells, AI-based virtual extracellular vesicles, and AI virtual organoids. These modules jointly form the mechanistic basis of the integrated AIVP models. This review also clearly distinguishes between the epistemological connotations of AIVPs and digital twins (DTs). AIVPs act as population-level synthetic archetypes optimized for in silico clinical trials, whereas DTs serve as individualized longitudinal replicas updated by real-world data assimilation. Focusing on pharmaceutical research and development and regulatory science, we discuss the capacity of AIVP cohorts to reduce developmental risks in drug research. These in silico models can be used to construct synthetic control arms, optimize dynamic precision dosing, and accelerate regulatory progress via Model-Informed Drug Development. We further summarize the key obstacles restricting the clinical translation of AIVPs, including epistemological limitations, inadequate infrastructure, and complex socio-regulatory constraints. Resolving data fragmentation, reducing algorithmic bias, and unifying verification and validation standards are critical for transforming AIVPs from theoretical prototypes into credible regulatory and clinical tools (Graphical Abstract).

title: Integrative analysis of pooled CRISPR screens provide functional insights into AD GWAS risk genes.
abstract: Microglia pathways such as lipid transport and metabolism, phagocytosis, and lysosomal function are implicated Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, but the mechanisms underlying these pathways remain poorly understood. To map these pathways, custom CRISPR activation and interference (CRISPRa/i) libraries were constructed targeting 203 microglial and genome-wide association study (GWAS)-associated risk genes. Pooled CRISPRa/i screens in THP-1 cells identified core functional regulators of lipid metabolism and lysosomal function, a subset of which were validated in primary macrophages. We also captured transcriptomic changes caused by these genes by performing Perturb-seq in primary macrophages. Through non-negative matrix factorization, we identified five gene programs altered by our perturbation library. We then used an integrative analysis of functional screen data with Perturb-seq data that enabled us to uncover novel functions and genetic relationships between perturbations. This multidimensional resource links genetic perturbations to phenotypes and transcriptional programs, establishing a scalable framework for systematic gene discovery in neurodegeneration and beyond.

title: Cellular morphology emerges from polygenic, distributed transcriptional variation.
abstract: Height and disease risk are canonical polygenic traits, but whether an analogous architecture governs cellular phenotypes remains unclear. Here, we show that cellular morphology behaves as a polygenic systems phenotype by integrating cross-modal modeling, perturbation profiling, and human genetic variation. An adversarially aligned autoencoder trained on four perturbation datasets predicted morphology from gene expression and generalized without retraining to matched RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and cell painting profiles from 100 genetically diverse induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) donors. Seventeen morphological features were strongly predicted, particularly those capturing organelle distribution and cytoskeletal architecture. Predictive signal was broadly distributed across genes, with weak individual gene-morphology correlations. Independent CRISPR perturbations supported model-prioritized genes including TIAM1 , RAB31 , and ABCC5 , while genetic analyses identified variant-gene-morphology associations involving PDHX, SLC11A2 , and MAPKAPK5 . These findings extend polygenic models of complex traits to cellular architecture and provide a framework for interpreting cross-modal prediction in functional genomics.

title: LeakageHunter-SCFM: Evidence-bounded dataset-lineage auditing for single-cell foundation model benchmarks.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. Methods LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. Results The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Conclusion Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

title: Interpretable attention probing reveals model-specific perceptions of cell states in single-cell foundation models
abstract: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) are increasingly used for transcriptomic analysis, yet it remains unclear whether different models encode cell states according to the same biological principles. Here, we present scGeneLens, an interpretable probing framework for dissecting how Transformer-based scFMs organize gene-level information into cellular representations. scGeneLens combines structured sparse-attention probing, cross-layer gene influence propagation, and complementary attribution and representational-alignment analyses to expose the dominant biological signals prioritized by each model. Applying scGeneLens to scFoundation and scGPT, we found they exhibit pluralistic perceptions of cells: scFoundation emphasizes relations among cell-type marker genes, resulting in stronger cell-type separability, whereas scGPT focuses more on genes involved in shared cellular pathways and core biological activities. These results suggest that differences among scFMs reflect not only performance variation but also distinct biological abstractions of cell identity and state. scGeneLens provides a unified lens for probing what scFMs learn about cells and informing future model design.

title: CellPert: Graph-based variational learning with biological priors for cross-dataset perturbation prediction
abstract: Predicting single-cell perturbation responses across datasets is challenging due to differences in experimental platforms, biological contexts, and perturbation coverage. We developed CellPert, a graph-structured variational framework that integrates gene-gene interaction priors into a graph neural network-based autoencoder to learn biologically informed cellular representations. By modeling perturbation effects as transferable latent-space shifts, CellPert enables zero-shot prediction in unseen datasets without paired perturbation data in the target dataset. Benchmarked across LINCS L1000 and Mini Tahoe100M against eight methods, CellPert improved expression reconstruction, correlation with observed responses, differential gene recovery, and cross-platform consistency. In aspirin-treated cancer cells, CellPert recapitulated transcriptional and pathway changes, tumor-associated cell states, and regulatory programs involving microRNAs (miRNAs), RNA-binding proteins, transcription factors, and cell-cell communication. Its latent representations also captured drug-class relationships and prioritized cancer-associated regulatory genes. Together, CellPert provides an interpretable, biologically grounded approach for transferable single-cell perturbation prediction across heterogeneous datasets and experimental platforms.

title: Single-cell Morphological Mechanisms-of-Action Profiling using Nanowell Imaging Plates.
abstract: Mechanism-of-action (MoA) analysis is used in drug discovery to prioritize compounds that act through desired pathways while eliminating compounds associated with nonspecific or undesirable activity. Image cytometry provides a promising route for MoA inference by capturing high-dimensional cellular phenotypes at single-cell resolution, but conventional workflows remain limited by unreliable cell segmentation and dependence on human-engineered feature extraction. Here, we present a deep learning-based image cytometry workflow that confines single cells in nanowells to obtain uniformly framed, regularized single-cell images, enabling MoA inference directly from raw images without segmentation or human-engineered features. Using a nanowell-in-microwell platform, we treated cells with 21 chemotherapeutic compounds spanning 11 MoA classes across multiple doses and time points, generating more than 500,000 single-cell images for model training and validation. A ResNet-18 convolutional neural network trained on images annotated by known compound mechanism achieved 85% accuracy in MoA classification. When a second model was trained on compound identity rather than MoA, misclassification patterns frequently linked compounds with shared mechanisms, indicating that the model learned mechanism-level relationships directly from single-cell morphology, without those relationships being specified in advance. Together, these results establish regularized single-cell imaging in nanowells as a scalable and interpretable approach to image-based MoA classification that overcomes key limitations of segmentation-dependent feature analysis.

title: Population-scale integration of spatial omics networks for clinical prediction and biological discovery by SPIN
abstract: Spatial omics enables the integration of high-dimensional molecular organization with clinical outcomes, yet incorporating spatial single-cell information into predictive models at the population scale remains challenging. We introduce SPIN (spatial predictive integration network), which integrates subject-specific, cell-type level, spatially informed co-expression or co-abundance networks for population-scale clinical prediction. Current implementation of SPIN includes three key modules: network construction, molecular-to-clinical prediction by Bayesian scalar-on-network regression with manifold learning (BSNMani), and visualization & interpretation module. In the Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD) multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) transcriptomics cohort, SPIN achieved an accuracy of 0.81 for dementia-status prediction and revealed co-expression subnetworks with clear biological relevance. SPIN also achieved robust survival prediction in a breast cancer single-cell proteomics cohort (C-index = 0.78), identifying two survival-associated spatial proteomic subnetworks. In summary, SPIN is an interpretable tool for spatial-omics-based clinical outcome prediction at the population scale.

title: DECODER-SC: A single-cell algorithm for quantifying transcription factor–target regulatory discordance
abstract: Existing transcription factor (TF) activity inference methods quantify regulatory potential but do not evaluate whether inferred TF activity is concordant with downstream target-gene expression. To address this limitation, we present DECODER-SC, a single-cell algorithm that quantifies TF-target regulatory discordance from single-cell RNA-sequencing data. DECODER-SC integrates direction-aware regulatory logic using DoRothEA activation and repression annotations, weighted discordance scoring, and permutation-based statistical inference to compute TF-level, interaction-level, and cell-level discordance metrics. Benchmarking against AUCell, VIPER, and TF-target correlation baseline demonstrated that discordance profiles capture regulatory structure not explained by activity magnitude or simple expression co-variation. Ablation analysis supported the contribution of activator/repressor-aware modeling to discordance detection, while robustness analyses demonstrated highly stable TF rankings across multiple threshold settings. Orthogonal Perturb-seq validation demonstrated a reproducible IRF1 discordance signal across experimental units (effect = 0.0643, 95% CI = 0.0441-0.0845, BH-adjusted P = 0.0235). Leave-one-target-out and VIPER-based sensitivity analyses confirmed that discordance classifications are robust to target-level circularity and alternative TF-activity inference (97.76% and 73.42% agreement, respectively). Replicate-aware sample-level analysis further showed that cell-level proliferation and pathway associations were exploratory rather than statistically independent. Application of DECODER-SC across multiple single-cell transcriptomic datasets identified recurrent regulatory discordance patterns associated with malignant progression, stress-adaptive transcriptional programs, and transitional cellular states. DECODER-SC expands current single-cell regulatory analysis by enabling systematic quantification of TF-target discordance across heterogeneous cellular populations.

title: Spatial omics in cancer: a review of computational approaches and vision of AI-driven analysis
abstract: Predicting patient response to cancer treatments remains a challenge due to tumor heterogeneity and complex tumor microenvironments (TMEs). Modern spatial genomics technologies enable gene expression profiling alongside histological frameworks, but comprehensive analysis and clinical translation of these high-dimensionality datasets will benefit from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). This review synthesizes computational approaches that address challenges of spatial data by examining deep-learning architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for histological feature extraction and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for modeling cell-cell interactions. We then explore the paradigm of Foundation Models that bridge histopathology with transcriptomics to accelerate the identification of spatially resolved biomarkers, improve patient stratification for immunotherapy and targeted treatments, and advance the clinical translation of mechanistic insights derived from the tumor microenvironment.

title: Label-Free and Strain-Resolved Characterization of AI-2 Associated Quorum Sensing Functional Phenotypes in Bacterial Isolates Using Single-Cell Raman Spectroscopy and Deep Learning.
abstract: We evaluated the relationship between Raman spectral profiles obtained by single-cell Raman spectroscopy (SCRS) and autoinducer-2 (AI-2)-associated quorum sensing (QS) functional phenotypes using experimentally measured relative BB170 reporter responses as functional reference values. Based on this relationship, this study provides a rapid, label-free SCRS-based model for characterizing AI-2-associated QS functional phenotypes in bacterial isolates. The optimized residual neural network (ResNet) achieved an R2 of 0.8351 under spectrum-level 10-fold cross-validation, while strain-level aggregated evaluation showed good agreement with experimentally measured responses within the represented dataset (R2 = 0.8840). In an independent-isolates set of 21 strains from multiple sources spanning the No-, Low-, Medium-, and High-response categories, the model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.092, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.148, an R2 of 0.805, and an overall category accuracy of 80.95%. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) detected luxS expression in all 21 independent isolates, providing complementary evidence for their potential AI-2-associated signaling capacity. In addition, furanone C-30 treatment of W37 resulted in concordant decreases in experimentally measured and model-estimated relative BB170 reporter responses, further supporting the responsiveness of the captured spectral phenotype to within-strain functional perturbation. Integrated Gradients (IG) analysis highlighted coordinated Raman spectral regions associated with proteins, lipids, polysaccharides, nucleic acids, and sulfur-containing groups, suggesting that model estimates were based on multiband spectral patterns rather than a single characteristic feature.

title: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Correlation Improves the Prediction of Anticancer Drug Candidates.
abstract: Predicting the anticancer effects of compounds is critical for computational drug evaluation. However, traditional transcriptomics-based virtual screening relies on bulk RNA profiling, causing intratumoral spatial heterogeneity to be averaged across the entire tissue and thereby limiting predictive accuracy. This limitation is particularly consequential for triple-negative breast cancer, which lacks receptor-guided treatment options and exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity that can obscure region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities when assessed by bulk analysis alone. To address this limitation, we developed a spatially resolved computational framework that integrates spatial transcriptomics to improve the prediction of anticancer drugs. Using a data set of 1291 diverse compounds, we compared the predictive performance of conventional disease-specific bulk signatures with that of localized spatial gene expression signatures. Whereas bulk signatures yielded insufficient predictive performance, incorporating spatial information improved prediction accuracy. Analysis of the predicted drug rankings further demonstrated that the spatial layer substantially improved the prioritization of known anticancer drugs while also identifying unclassified and nononcology compounds with potential anticancer effects. These findings indicate that the predicted therapeutic relevance of a compound depends on localized transcriptomic states rather than representing a static property across an entire heterogeneous tumor section. Ultimately, the proposed method provides a robust, region-aware computational framework for accurately characterizing the anticancer properties of compounds and offers a more nuanced paradigm for transcriptomics-based drug evaluation.

title: Chemical Biology in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Ligand Discovery to Virtual Cells
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how scientists, including chemical biologists, conduct research. This review is intended to serve as an introduction for chemical biologists to applications of artificial intelligence in chemical biology. We review how chemical and biological data are featurized, the types of models commonly used in chemical biology applications, challenges in assessing accuracy of artificial intelligence models, and recent developments in agentic artificial intelligence for autonomous research. The applications we will cover include protein structure prediction, ligand discovery, peptide and protein design, prediction of mutational effects, interactomics and gene regulation, and virtual cells.

title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

title: Multi-omics, spatial omics and artificial intelligence in chronic diseases: current applications and future directions.
abstract: Chronic diseases exhibit multiscale heterogeneity and spatial organization, yet analytical frameworks often fail to connect molecular perturbations, tissue architecture, and clinical outcomes within a unified evidence framework. Bulk and single-modality approaches can identify regulatory or cellular alterations but provide limited insight into why pathogenic programs emerge in anatomical regions, how they shape disease niches, and how they drive divergent clinical trajectories. Multi-omics partially addresses this gap by resolving interconnected layers of regulation, transcription, protein activity, and metabolism, whereas spatial omics maps these processes within preserved tissue architecture, enabling the delineation of lesion topology, interface states, and multicellular microenvironments. Artificial intelligence (AI) may further extend this framework by integrating molecular, spatial, imaging, and clinical data into disease representations that support disease stratification, the discovery of mechanistic patterns, and clinically testable predictions, provided that models are externally validated, biologically interpretable, and robust to dataset bias and domain shift. In this review, we examine how multi-omics, spatial omics, and AI can bridge the disconnect between molecular profiling, spatial pathology, and clinical translation in chronic disease research. We discuss six representative disease domains before synthesizing insights into how these approaches define molecular endotypes, map pathological niches, identify recurrent mechanistic patterns, and generate interpretable surrogate readouts for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment stratification. We also highlight limitations, including preanalytical variability, inconsistencies across platforms, limited external generalizability, and the challenges of translating high-dimensional outputs into deployable clinical tools. Finally, we outline priorities for scalable evidence systems, mechanism-guided validation frameworks, multimodal model interpretability, and prospective clinical implementation.

title: Artificial intelligence aids multi-omics data integration in cancer drug discovery and development: from targets to drug synergy
abstract: The emergence of multi-omics technologies has enabled the integration of genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data to characterize the molecular complexity of cancer. Single-cell and spatial profiling further resolve intratumoral heterogeneity, cell-cell interactions, and the microenvironmental determinants of therapeutic responses. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) provides computational approaches for integrating these heterogeneous data types across target identification, drug response prediction, toxicity assessment, and drug-combination modeling. Across these domains, the available evidence indicates that multi-omics integration is most beneficial when the included layers provide complementary biological information; that single-cell and spatial omics analyses reveal treatment-resistant populations and niches but remain largely research-grade and thus not ready for routine clinical deployment; and that although foundation models support some representation-learning tasks, their advantages in perturbation-response prediction require confirmation via stringent evaluation. By distinguishing externally validated advances from retrospective proof-of-concept studies, we provide a practical framework for evaluating the translational readiness of AI-driven multi-omics tools in precision oncology.

title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations
abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出细胞级统计检验，量化 RNA velocity 嵌入相对高维原始结构的忠实度。
llm.summary_zh: velotest 是细胞级统计检验，用于评估 velocity 投影与高维数据结构之间的一致性。作者在多个数据集和多种嵌入方法上应用该检验，发现不同嵌入方法、数据集以及同一数据集的不同区域之间，嵌入质量差异显著。

title: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
abstract: Similarity of body-plan features across distant phyla provides striking testimony to the Darwinian concept of common descent throughout Metazoa. In both the cnidarian Nematostella and chordates, gastrula organizers direct the initial establishment of embryonic axes. Whether these domains share a common evolutionary origin is a fundamental question for understanding the origin of the chordate body plan. To address this question, we combine trans-species transgenesis, perturbations of signaling pathways, cross-phylum single-cell transcriptomic comparisons, and transplantation assays. We show that cis-regulatory elements that recapitulate NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin expression in Nematostella —and therefore report the endogenous cnidarian organizer regulatory environment—also drive organizer-restricted activity in chordate embryos, consistent with chordate organizer gene-regulatory logic. Moreover, we show that, as in chordates, Smad2/3-mediated signaling is active in the Nematostella organizer and is required for organizer-specific expression of NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin . Together, our data support remarkable homology between cnidarian and chordate gastrula organizers and are consistent with the idea that the cnidarian–bilaterian ancestor possessed a blastopore organizer with the potential to generate dorsal–anterior chordate fates. On this basis, we propose a scenario in which asymmetric positioning of the ancestral blastopore organizer and skewed body-axis elongation contributed to the emergence of the chordate body plan.
affiliations: Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Molecular Genetics

llm.novelty_zh: 利用跨物种转基因和信号扰动，提出刺胞动物与脊索动物胚胎组织者之间的同源性证据。
llm.summary_zh: 研究在海葵Nematostella中鉴定出可再现NvBmp2/4与NvChordin表达的顺式调控元件，并证明其在脊索动物胚胎中也驱动组织者特异性活性。作者还显示Smad2/3信号在两者组织者中均起作用。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为脊索动物体轴形成的进化起源提供了分子层面的支持证据。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及该同源性结论在其他无脊椎动物中的普适性。

title: scMomer: a pretraining framework for inferring robust cellular representations from single-cell transcriptomes
abstract: High-quality cellular representations are important for understanding complex biological systems. However, due to limitations in both data availability and practical utility, most existing computational methods are designed for a single modality (e.g., scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq), restricting their ability to capture cellular heterogeneity. Here, we propose scMomer, a multistage pretraining framework designed to infer robust cellular representations by integrating multimodal knowledge into scRNA-seq-only inputs. The framework progressively learns through three stages. Firstly, it pretrains unimodal encoders on single-modality datasets to obtain modality-specific representations. Secondly, it aligns these modalities using paired data to learn joint representations. Thirdly, it applies knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge of the missing modality (scATAC-seq) into a cross-modal student encoder, enabling the inference of multimodal-aware representations from scRNA-seq-only inputs. We perform extensive experiments show that the representations learned by scMomer achieve superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods across diverse tasks, including cross-modality translation, cell annotation, drug response prediction, perturbation prediction, and gene property prediction, demonstrating its robustness and versatility. Overall, we demonstrate that scMomer enables unimodal data to yield robust cellular representations, providing an effective solution to missing-modality modeling.
affiliations: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

llm.novelty_zh: 通过多模态对齐与知识蒸馏，把 scATAC 模态的知识迁移到仅以 scRNA 为输入的学生编码器。
llm.summary_zh: scMomer 是三阶段预训练框架：先分别预训练单模态编码器，再用配对数据对齐模态，最后通过知识蒸馏把缺失的 scATAC 模态知识迁移到只输入 scRNA 的学生编码器。作者报告其在跨模态翻译、细胞注释、药物响应及扰动预测等任务上优于现有方法。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为只有单模态数据时获得多模态感知的细胞表征提供了缺失模态建模思路。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

llm.novelty_zh: 首次利用视觉型大语言模型比较并排序空间域划分结果，再据此构建共识图谱。
llm.summary_zh: L-STAR让大语言模型视觉比较候选空间域图，对方法进行排序，并基于排名靠前的结果构建共识划分。摘要称其在不同组织、物种和技术的数据上比专家注释更吻合，排序在颜色和顺序变化时依然稳定，并能为各域给出生物学名称。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 展示了大语言模型作为分析评估器的应用潜力，可能提升空间转录组分析的自动化与可解释性。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及大语言模型输出的随机性、计算成本以及对不同模型版本的依赖。

title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. The heterogeneous nature of peak feature spaces across samples hinders the effectiveness of existing methods, while the absence of dedicated tools for detecting perturbed cell types and states in scATAC-seq data further limits the depth of downstream analyses. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. At its core, the Peak Embedding Informed Variational Inference (PEIVI) framework within EpiPack enhances mappable reference construction, query mapping, and label transfer, demonstrating that leveraging heterogeneous features in scATAC-seq data outperforms methods relying solely on conventional homogeneous features. In addition, EpiPack’s global-local out-of-reference (OOR) detection framework achieves robust and efficient detection of perturbed cell types and states, extending the utility of scATAC-seq to disease and perturbation contexts. With its modular design and transferable pre-trained references, EpiPack can be readily applied to diverse analytical tasks and is available as a Python package at https://github.com/ZhangLabGT/EpiPack .

llm.novelty_zh: 提出 PEIVI 变分推断框架，利用异质 peak 特征完成 scATAC-seq 参考映射与域外细胞检测。
llm.summary_zh: EpiPack 是面向 scATAC-seq 的计算工具包，支持参考构建、查询映射与标签迁移，并借助异质特征提升效果。其全局-局部域外（OOR）检测框架可识别扰动相关的细胞类型与状态。工具以 Python 包形式提供，并支持可迁移的预训练参考。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为异质 peak 空间下的 scATAC-seq 映射与扰动相关细胞状态检测提供实用工具。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Retrospective single cell lineage tracing with highly mutable homopolymers
abstract: Retrospective reconstruction of cell lineages from somatic mutations holds substantial promise for understanding development, tissue homeostasis, and disease. Yet, current approaches are often constrained by low marker density, technical noise, and incomplete molecular readouts that limit the resolution and accuracy of inferred lineages. Here, we present RETrace2, a single-cell dual-omic method for simultaneous lineage tracing and cell-type identification. By identifying and targeting highly mutable homopolymers, which we show are approximately twice as informative as conventional microsatellite repeats, combined with technical improvements to increase marker coverage and reduce experimental errors of reading and amplifying homopolymers, RETrace2 can trace lineage continuously at an estimated resolution of fewer than five cell divisions in microsatellite-unstable organisms. Simultaneously, sparse methylation profiles are obtained from the same cells for cell-type identification. We validate the method using in vitro ground-truth models and demonstrate its utility in vivo by reconstructing multi-organ lineage trees from the brain, kidney and liver of Msh2 -deficient mice.
affiliations: St. Anna Children's Cancer Research Institute

llm.novelty_zh: 靶向高突变率同聚物实现更高分辨率的回溯谱系追踪，并同时获得甲基化谱用于细胞类型鉴定。
llm.summary_zh: RETrace2 是单细胞双组学方法，通过靶向高突变率的同聚物追踪细胞谱系，并从同一细胞获得稀疏甲基化谱用于细胞类型鉴定。作者在体外真值模型中验证了方法，并在 Msh2 缺陷小鼠的脑、肾和肝中重建了多器官谱系树。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为体内细胞谱系回溯提供了分辨率更高的技术工具。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. We identify 17.7 million pharmocogenomic expression interactions in 625,866 cells representing baseline and post-therapeutic molecular phenotypes. This single-cell pharmacogenomic compendium confirms previously known gene-driven molecular phenotypes, elucidating both poorly characterized genes and gene dosage-molecular phenotype relationships. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds.
affiliations: Agency for Science, Technology and Research

llm.novelty_zh: 用直接捕获Perturb-seq在胃癌细胞系中大规模刻画表观遗传药物与基因扰动的联合分子表型图谱。
llm.summary_zh: 作者对200余个胃癌相关基因与4种表观遗传疗法进行Perturb-seq扰动，构建了包含约62.6万个细胞的单细胞药物基因组学图谱。研究发现耐药相关通路（EMT、细胞周期和代谢重编程）在存活细胞中被扰动特异性激活，并将体外表型映射到原发胃癌中以关联预后和空间异质性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为扰动响应建模提供了大规模、多药物、多细胞系的数据资源，可用于检验基因-药物相互作用模型。
llm.limitations_zh: 仅涉及胃癌相关细胞系和4种疗法，体外结果向原发肿瘤的外推依赖映射分析。

title: Isoform-resolved spatial transcriptomics on a lab-made high-density array via a single-chip NGS-TGS workflow
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics maps gene expression within tissue sections, but dominant short-read approaches have limited ability to resolve full-length transcript structures such as alternative splicing. Long-read sequencing provides transcript-structure information, although its higher sequencing error rates can complicate spatial-barcode identification on high-density arrays. Here, we show a lab-made, high-density spatial transcriptomics system that uses a tri-part combinatorial barcode design to expand barcode capacity and facilitate spatial assignment of long reads. By splitting full-length complementary DNA generated from a single capture chip, the workflow combines high-depth short-read quantification with single-molecule long-read profiling within the same spatial coordinate system. In incompatible tomato–pepper grafts and mouse embryos, the approach identifies spatially localized unannotated isoforms and intron-retention events, and reveals regional differences in isoform usage that are not apparent from gene-level expression alone. Together, this system provides a framework for combining spatial gene-expression quantification with full-length transcript-structure analysis in the same tissue.
affiliations: Southern University of Science and Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 用三段式组合条码的高密度阵列实现空间定位的长读长转录本分析。
llm.summary_zh: 研究构建了高密度空间转录组系统，将同一捕获芯片的 cDNA 分流为短读与长读，在番茄-辣椒嫁接体和小鼠胚胎中发现空间定位的未注释异构体和内含子保留事件。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 同时获得空间定位的基因表达与全长转录本结构，拓展了空间转录组的分辨维度。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及方法的通量和成本。

title: Mapping dynamics of subcellular RNA and protein localization and organization using optimal transport
abstract: Subcellular molecular polarity is essential for early development and represents a key layer for building virtual cell models that connect molecular organization to cell fate. Yet how RNA and protein localization patterns are established, erased, and rebuilt during the transition from oocyte to zygote remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we integrate high-resolution axial cryo-sectioning with multi-omics profiling across six stages of Xenopus laevis early development and develop an optimal-transport-based framework to quantify spatial polarity and temporal remodeling of molecular distributions. Here, we show that proteins, rather than RNAs, carry the dominant and rapidly remodeled polarity signature, undergoing polarity collapse from stage VI oocytes to unfertilized eggs and rapid re-establishment after fertilization; this protein-specific rewiring contrasts with relatively stable RNA localization, reveals uncoupling between transcript storage and protein spatial deployment, and provides a spatial multi-omics foundation for modeling early embryogenesis toward virtual cells.
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
Huazhong University of Science and Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 用最优传输量化RNA与蛋白在亚细胞尺度上的极性动态，揭示蛋白极性在受精前后的重塑。
llm.summary_zh: 作者结合高分辨轴向冷冻切片与多组学，在非洲爪蟾早期发育的六个阶段测定RNA与蛋白的空间分布。基于最优传输框架量化极性与时间重塑，发现蛋白而非RNA承载主要且快速变化的极性信号。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为理解卵母细胞到受精卵的分子组织转变提供了空间多组学资源，也与构建虚拟细胞的思路相关。
llm.limitations_zh: 研究对象限于一种模式生物的早期发育，摘要未提及计算模型对新条件的预测能力。

title: Enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of human forebrain development provides insights into autism
abstract: Cell differentiation is orchestrated by transcription factors binding to enhancers, shaping gene regulatory networks that drive neuronal lineage specification. Deciphering these enhancer-driven networks in human forebrain development is essential for understanding the genetic basis of neurodevelopmental disorders. Through integrative epigenomic and transcriptomic analyses of human forebrain organoids derived from 10 male individuals with autism spectrum disorder and their neurotypical fathers, we construct a comprehensive enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of early neurodevelopment. This network reveals hierarchical regulatory layers upstream of neuronal cell fate genes, experimentally validated via CRISPR interference and loss-of-function analyses. A subnetwork links autism-associated transcriptomic alterations to opposite activities of the transcription factors FOXG1, BHLHE22, EOMES, and NEUROD2, driving increased or decreased excitatory neuron specification in (respectively) macrocephalic or normocephalic individuals with autism. These findings support the association of autism with disruption of enhancer-driven regulatory networks altering neuronal cell fate decisions in the developing fetal brain.
affiliations: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke

llm.novelty_zh: 整合表观基因组与转录组数据，从自闭症个体来源的前脑类器官构建增强子驱动的调控网络，并以CRISPRi验证关键转录因子。
llm.summary_zh: 研究利用10名自闭症男性个体及其正常父亲的前脑类器官，整合表观基因组与转录组分析，构建增强子驱动的早期神经发育调控网络。作者通过CRISPR干扰与功能缺失实验验证了FOXG1、BHLHE22、EOMES与NEUROD2等因子，并解释了兴奋性神经元分化的差异。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该网络将自闭症相关转录变化与神经元命运决定联系起来，为理解神经发育障碍的调控基础提供线索。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Author Correction: A machine learning model reveals expansive downregulation of ligand-receptor interactions that enhance lymphocyte infiltration in melanoma with developed resistance to immune checkpoint blockade
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there was a coding error that originated in our single-cell RNA-seq cell-cell interaction tool, SOCIAL, in which cell-type-specific ligand-receptor interactions were not calculated correctly from the single-cell data. As SOCIAL is integrated into our spatial transcriptomics tool, SPECIAL (also introduced in this article), the downstream spatial transcriptomics analyses were also affected. We have corrected the error in SOCIAL and regenerated the affected single-cell and spatial transcriptomics results (Fig. 2I-J; Fig. 5; Supplementary Figs. 7–10 and associated figure legends and text). The conclusions are not affected. We have updated the SOCIAL code deposited in GitHub. The HTML and PDF versions of the article have been updated. For comparison, the original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

llm.novelty_zh: 更正 SOCIAL 细胞间互作工具的一处计算错误，并重新生成受影响的单细胞与空间转录组结果。
llm.summary_zh: 这是对一篇关于肿瘤免疫检查点耐药黑色素瘤中配体-受体互作研究的更正说明。作者指出 SOCIAL 工具中细胞类型特异性配体-受体互作的计算有误，已修正并重新生成受影响的单细胞与空间分析结果，文章主要结论不受影响，代码已在 GitHub 上更新。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提示使用 SOCIAL 与 SPECIAL 工具的研究者需要更新结果与代码。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: A neuroimmune dichotomy for T cell immunity in the mesenteric iymph node in mice
abstract: Peripheral nerves innervate lymphoid organs, yet how they decode immune signals and direct adaptive immunity remains unknown. Here we show, using three-dimensional tissue imaging, in vivo calcium recordings, single-cell transcriptomics, and chemogenetics in mice, that the mesenteric lymph node (mLN) harbours functionally antagonistic neural circuits that govern T cell fate. Vagal sensory neurons selectively detect IL-1β and TNF-α and release calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), which suppresses Foxp3⁺ regulatory T (T reg ) cells and expands cytotoxic CD8⁺ effector T (T eff ) cells. Conversely, sympathetic neurons sense IL-6 and release norepinephrine (NE), promoting T reg accumulation while restraining effector responses. During Citrobacter rodentium infection, the sympathetic–NE–T reg axis is protective, whereas the vagal–CGRP axis drives immunopathology. T reg -specific deletion of the CGRP receptor or the β₂-adrenergic receptor confirms that these opposing signals converge on T reg cells to calibrate mucosal host defence. These findings establish the mLN as an autonomic rheostat for intestinal immunity.
affiliations: Shanghai Medical College of Fudan University
Frontiers Center for Brain Science of the Ministry of Education
Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University

llm.novelty_zh: 发现肠系膜淋巴结中迷走神经CGRP通路与交感神经去甲肾上腺素通路对Treg与效应T细胞具有相反调控作用。
llm.summary_zh: 研究利用三维成像、体内钙记录、单细胞转录组和化学遗传学，证明肠系膜淋巴结中存在功能相反的神经回路。迷走感觉神经经CGRP抑制Treg并扩增细胞毒性CD8+效应T细胞，交感神经经去甲肾上腺素促进Treg积累。在柠檬酸杆菌感染中，两条轴分别表现出保护或致病作用。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 揭示了神经系统通过调控T细胞命运影响肠道免疫的新机制。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment1-8, suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear9-13. Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)-a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution-and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

llm.summary_zh: 作者用 scDORI 分析了一百多万个胶质母细胞瘤原发肿瘤单核多组学细胞，推断增强子驱动的基因调控网络。结合患者来源模型中的系统扰动筛选，发现激活因子与抑制因子的非对称相互作用维持低可塑性状态。MYT1L 作为其中的关键抑制因子，在体内抑制肿瘤生长与侵袭，缺失后则重新激活可塑性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提示肿瘤低可塑性状态依赖持续抑制维持，并提出了有别于分化诱导剂的候选治疗靶点。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
abstract: Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour1-5. However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD1-3. Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge4. Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals5, and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts6,7; however, the biological basis of this 'female protective effect' (FPE) has remained unknown8,9. Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST. Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals10, emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

llm.summary_zh: 研究在人神经祖细胞中分别扰动18个ASD相关基因，发现这些扰动在基因表达上呈现趋同效应，并伴随其他ASD基因的广泛下调。通过重建基因调控网络，识别出CHD8、REST以及X连锁转录因子ZFX等关键调控因子，其中ZFX被认为可缓冲女性大脑中的致病突变。
