title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease.
abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease 1,2 . Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling 3 , we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb-seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment 1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

title: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
abstract: Mounting evidence implicates microglia in neurodegeneration, but linking disease-associated genetic variants to target genes and cellular phenotypes is hindered by the inaccessibility of these cells. We differentiated 261 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines into microglia-like (iMGL) cells in pools with phenotypic (differentiation, phagocytosis and migration) and single-cell transcriptomic readouts. Burden analysis of deleterious variants detected 36 genes influencing microglial phenotypes. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis identified 7,121 eQTL-associated genes and 79 colocalizations across four neurodegenerative disease genome-wide association studies, half of which had limited prior evidence of causality. Integration of eQTL and phenotypic associations highlighted the role of disease-relevant variants, including LRRK2 and TREM2 acting through microglial phagocytosis. A coupled CRISPR screen identified a role for TREM2 in phagocytosis and highlighted the importance of cell type in the directionality of phenotypic effects. By contextualizing variant effects within iMGLs in different inflammatory states, we provide a comprehensive framework for interpreting the function of risk loci in neurodegenerative disorders.

llm.novelty_zh: 在混池的iPSC来源小胶质细胞中，将eQTL、表型关联与CRISPR筛选相结合，系统推断神经退行性风险位点的作用。
llm.summary_zh: 作者将261个iPSC系分化为类小胶质细胞并进行混池表型和单细胞转录组检测，识别出36个影响表型的基因并完成7121个eQTL相关基因的分析。通过耦合CRISPR筛选，研究证实TREM2参与吞噬作用，并强调细胞类型对表型效应方向的影响。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为从遗传风险变异推断细胞功能提供了可扩展的实验框架，对神经退行性疾病的机制研究具有参考价值。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及体内验证，且结论主要基于体外分化的类小胶质细胞。

title: An ulcerative colitis taxonomy defined by individual patient-reported response trajectories
abstract: A barrier to precision medicine for ulcerative colitis (UC) is the inability to predict and mechanistically explain treatment responses. Using patient-reported outcomes (PROs) from a phase 3b comparative trial of 768 participants, we identified four distinct patient response-trajectory groups for vedolizumab (anti-integrin) and adalimumab (antitumor necrosis factor). Validation in a second phase 3 trial of 576 participants linked PRO-defined vedolizumab trajectories to long-term disease complications. Bulk, single cell, and spatial transcriptomics and proteomics identified vascular inflammation as associated with vedolizumab nonresponse through interactions between SPP1+ macrophages and endothelial cells. In two separate real-world cohorts of 4,981 and 3,854 patients with UC, concomitant use of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (modulators of vascular inflammation) was associated with reduced long-term complications for vedolizumab but not anticytokine therapies. These findings define a response-trajectory-based taxonomy that requires prospective validation for clinical utility and applications for selecting vedolizumab combination therapy in UC.

llm.novelty_zh: 基于患者报告的应答轨迹定义溃疡性结肠炎分型，并关联血管炎症机制。

llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为溃疡性结肠炎的精准用药选择提供了基于应答轨迹的分型思路。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要提到分型仍需前瞻性验证方能用于临床。

title: Nondisruptive 3D profiling of combinations of epigenetic marks in single cells
abstract: Advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies have enhanced our understanding of diverse cellular identities, compositions, architectures and functions. However, the single-cell three-dimensional (3D) organization of the epigenome is still not well understood, due to an absence of spatial single-cell methods that allow high-resolution, locus-specific detection of combinations of epigenetic marks while maintaining 3D genome organization. Here we develop epigenetic proximity hybridization reaction (Epi-PHR), a nondisruptive image-based single-cell spatial epigenetic profiling technology. Epi-PHR detects combinations of epigenetic marks in situ at hundreds of gene targets within single cells while preserving 3D genome organization. Phased Epi-PHR combined with chromatin tracing reveals unexpected associations between epigenetic mark enrichment and chromatin folding of an imprinted gene cluster at the single-chromatin-copy level for the distinct alleles from different parental origins. We expect Epi-PHR will be broadly applicable in research requiring single-cell spatial epigenetic information, advancing our understanding of the combinatorial epigenetic code and its relationship with chromatin organization.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出在保持三维基因组结构的前提下，对单细胞中多种表观修饰组合进行原位定位的Epi-PHR技术。
llm.summary_zh: Epi-PHR是一种非破坏性的单细胞图像法，可在数百个基因位点上原位检测表观修饰组合。结合染色质追踪，作者揭示了印记基因簇在不同亲本等位基因上的表观修饰与染色质折叠关联。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为研究表观修饰组合与三维染色质结构之间的关系提供了新的单细胞空间工具。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及检测通量和可扩展性的限制。

title: PANGEA: an integrated cell atlas across diverse biological contexts enables systematic profiling of multicellular responses in human diseases
abstract: Diseases affect multiple cell types within tissues, but the overall landscape of the multicellular responses in human diseases remains largely unexplored. Here we categorize the multicellular responses of human diseases based on a remapped atlas of human cells, PANGEA, incorporating 12.6 million cells acquired from a pipeline that automatically processes raw sequence files from public repositories. We constructed a hierarchical cell classification framework comprising 32 major cell types and 165 cellular subtypes. On the basis of this annotation framework, we explored an extensive atlas of human cells containing 46.5 million cells from 160 diseases across 48 organs and revealed core archetypes of human diseases repeatedly found across organs. We show that this cell atlas could also serve as a reference for unbiased analysis in spatial transcriptomics, revealing spatial features associated with immunotherapy responses. Collectively, our study provides foundational resources for cell ontologies, enabling cross-tissue comparisons of cellular features in human diseases.

title: Transforming molecular evolutionary analyses with protein foundation models
Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
abstract: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR-Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression.

llm.summary_zh: 作者提出Superb-seq，整合Cas9编辑、T7原位转录和单细胞RNA测序，在约3.5万个细胞中检测编辑及其转录效应。在K562细胞中检测到5761个编辑细胞及36个脱靶位点，并与4种批量脱靶检测方法比较，鉴定出19个与差异表达相关的脱靶编辑。

title: An accuracy and calibration benchmark of scGPT pipelines and matched classical models for cell type annotation
abstract: Foundation-model embeddings are used for single-cell annotation, but their value depends on biological holdout, comparator design and downstream learning. We compared frozen scGPT 0.2.5 embeddings with matched expression; both were paired with independently tuned Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost. Training-fitted SVD-512 was evaluated with Logistic Regression across all atlases and with all classifiers only in TNBC and brain. Five donor-held-out folds yielded 965,427 analysed cells from 312 donors. Matched expression achieved higher pooled Macro F1 in six TNBC/PBMC comparisons; scGPT was higher in three brain comparisons. Donor-cluster bootstraps supported the six expression advantages and the brain Random Forest scGPT advantage, while the other brain intervals crossed zero. Where available, SVD-512 remained close to expression, arguing against compression alone as the explanation. Under strict PBMC label scarcity, expression reached Macro F1 0.818–0.930 versus 0.779–0.881 for scGPT. Held-out-donor temperature scaling reduced mean expected calibration error from 0.0072 to 0.0057 but not in every pipeline. Class analyses identified lymphocyte-boundary errors in TNBC and PBMC and rare-class errors in brain. Performance was atlas- and classifier-dependent for this frozen-scGPT pipeline; official fine-tuning, newer checkpoints and cross-cohort transfer were not tested.

llm.novelty_zh: 以供体留出的严格评估比较冻结scGPT嵌入与表达矩阵及经典分类器，属于已有模型的基准分析，无新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 研究用冻结的scGPT 0.2.5嵌入与匹配的表达矩阵，分别搭配逻辑回归、随机森林和XGBoost进行细胞类型注释，采用五折供体留出评估，共分析约96.5万个细胞、312名供体。结果显示多数TNBC/PBMC比较中表达矩阵的宏F1更高，脑数据中scGPT仅在部分比较中占优，SVD压缩结果也接近表达矩阵。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提醒单细胞基础模型在注释任务中需与强基线及校准指标比较，对评测实践有参考价值。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要显示脑数据中部分置信区间跨越零，结论在部分比较中并不确定。

title: Multimodal cell foundation models require synergistic integration beyond alignment
abstract: Integrating measurements across modalities and scales into unified quantitative frameworks of cellular function is a central goal in computational biology. Although powerful unimodal foundation models exist, the scarcity of large-scale paired data limits joint multimodal training. This constraint favours compositional foundation models, which fuse frozen unimodal experts through a learned interface. However, it remains unclear when such fusion provides task-relevant information beyond the strongest unimodal representation rather than merely aggregating redundant signal. Here we introduce Synergistic Information Score, a metric grounded in partial information decomposition that quantifies information gain arising only from cross-modal interactions. Extending theory from self-supervised learning, we show that standard alignment-based objectives with frozen encoders collapse to detect linear redundancies, which constrains their ability to capture nonlinear synergistic states. This distinction is especially important for tasks that connect tissue morphology with gene expression. Benchmarking ten fusion methods on spatial transcriptomics datasets, we demonstrate that tasks dominated by linear redundancies are well served by unimodal baselines, whereas complex niche definitions benefit from synergy-aware integration. Finally, we perform a scaling analysis and show that fine-tuning a dominant unimodal expert is the most sample-efficient strategy for standard tasks. Together, these results suggest that progress in multimodal modelling of cellular state requires shifting from alignment-based objectives to synergy-driven integration that exploits complementary cross-modal signal.

llm.novelty_zh: 基于部分信息分解提出协同信息分数，量化仅由跨模态交互带来的信息增益，并指出对齐目标的局限。
llm.summary_zh: 该文提出基于部分信息分解的 Synergistic Information Score，用于衡量仅由跨模态交互产生的信息增益，并论证冻结编码器下的对齐目标只能捕捉线性冗余。作者在空间转录组数据上比较十种融合方法，发现线性冗余主导的任务适合单模态基线，而复杂生态位定义则受益于协同感知的整合。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为何时需要多模态融合提供了可量化判据，对细胞基础模型的多模态设计有指导意义。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals organizational properties of the mouse spinal cord and alterations in neuropathic pain
abstract: The spinal cord integrates diverse somatosensory inputs and executes motor outputs through anatomically and functionally distinct circuits. Here, we employed spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the adult mouse spinal cord to gain insights into the organizational logic of the spinal cord. Our results reveal distinct spatial and laminar distributions of neuronal subtypes, including axial level and sex-specific differences. Many neuronal subtypes exhibit lamina-specific somatic proximities, suggesting potential regionally specific connectivity. Additionally, neuronal subtypes within the dorsal horn exhibit a wide range of predicted cell-cell communication motifs, as assessed by the spatial distribution of neuropeptide- and other ligand-receptor pairs. Finally, we identified several neuronal subtypes with altered transcriptomic states and predicted cell-cell communications in a model of neuropathic pain. This spatially resolved cellular and molecular map of the spinal cord will facilitate the decoding of circuit mechanisms underlying somatosensory and motor functions in health and disease.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
published_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

llm.novelty_zh: 用空间转录组绘制成年小鼠脊髓神经元亚型的空间分布与细胞通讯图谱。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
abstract: Introduction Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. Areas covered This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. Expert opinion AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出虚拟细胞、数字孪生与智能体孪生的六项能力嵌套框架，用于组织药物发现中 AI 虚拟细胞的进展。
llm.summary_zh: 这篇叙述性综述以嵌套框架组织 AI 虚拟细胞能力，涵盖由群体数据构建的虚拟细胞、与具体生物对象对应的数字孪生，以及加入空间与环境反馈的智能体孪生。作者认为这类模型可作为跨任务迁移生物知识的基础模型，但其价值取决于外推能力和前瞻性验证。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未给出具体模型的定量比较，框架的可操作性仍有待后续工作验证。

title: Identifying multi-omics spatial domains via masked autoencoder and diffusion-based latent regularization with SpaMEDM
abstract: Spatial multi-omics data provide complementary molecular views of tissue organization. However, their integration remains challenging due to data sparsity, technical noise, and modality-specific distributions. Here, we present Spatial Masked autoEncoder and Diffusion-based Model (SpaMEDM), an end-to-end graph representation learning framework that augments a dual-attention graph-integration backbone with masked reconstruction and diffusion-based latent noise-prediction regularization. In the masked track, randomly masked spot features are recovered by leveraging modality- and graph-specific neighborhood information. In parallel, Gaussian perturbations are applied to modality-specific latent representations at randomly sampled noise levels, and a spatial-graph-informed network is trained to predict the injected noise. This diffusion-based objective is used exclusively during training to encourage robustness to latent perturbations, rather than to perform iterative reverse diffusion or sampling during inference. Furthermore, cosine-based paired-spot directional alignment and adjacency reconstruction encourage compatible cross-modality representations and preservation of the selected graph structure. SpaMEDM flexibly supports purely spatial, dual feature-spatial, and modality-specific feature-pruned spatial graph configurations. Evaluations across diverse spatial multi-omics datasets demonstrate competitive spatial-domain identification performance and produce integrated embeddings that facilitate downstream exploratory analyses.

llm.novelty_zh: 将掩码自编码器与扩散式潜在噪声预测正则化结合到双注意力图整合网络中，用于空间多组学域划分。
llm.summary_zh: SpaMEDM在双注意力图整合骨干上加入掩码重建和训练期的扩散式潜在噪声预测，以提高对潜在扰动的稳健性。摘要称其在多种空间多组学数据上具有竞争力的空间域识别性能，并输出便于下游分析的整合嵌入。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为空间多组学的整合与空间域识别提供了自监督表征学习方法，有助于组织结构的解析。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及与其他空间多组学方法的定量比较细节，也未说明扩散式正则化的超参数敏感性。

title: MitoLODE: a virtual mitochondrion framework with knowledge graph priors for trajectory modeling and mechanistic perturbation analysis
abstract: Mitochondria play a central role in the pathogenesis of major diseases. Tracking how they evolve under disease conditions is valuable for understanding pathological mechanisms and identifying intervention windows. Existing single-cell trajectory inference methods rely on pseudotime rather than a real temporal axis, and rarely model disease and control as independent trajectories. Virtual cell methods target one-shot drug perturbation responses and do not handle the continuous temporal evolution of disease phenotypes. To address these gaps, we propose a virtual mitochondrion research paradigm. We first curate and construct MitoKG, a mitochondria-specific heterogeneous knowledge graph integrated from five authoritative databases. MitoKG contains 2549 nodes of four types and 23 019 edges of five relation types. Building on these priors, we develop MitoLODE, a conditioned dual-trajectory neural ordinary differential equation framework. MitoLODE embeds graph priors and temporal features throughout encoding, continuous-time dynamics, and decoding, modeling disease and control evolution as two coupled paths. Benchmarked against eight baselines across four datasets covering Parkinson's disease, cardiac, and pancreatic differentiation, MitoLODE leads in most settings and remains robust under low-data regimes and extrapolation to unseen time points. Two synthetic datasets with known ground truth validate its trajectory recovery under controlled conditions. Building on the trained model, we design a gradient-guided perturbation procedure that identifies potential intervention targets aligned with known Parkinson's pathology. We develop MGMI, a large language model-based reasoning module that grounds model outputs in MitoKG nodes and turns them into confidence-graded mechanistic hypotheses, which nonetheless require experimental validation.

llm.summary_zh: 该文构建线粒体知识图谱 MitoKG，并基于其设计 MitoLODE 双路径条件神经 ODE，用于线粒体随时间变化的轨迹建模。作者在帕金森、心脏和胰腺分化等四个数据集上与八种基线比较，并通过梯度引导扰动识别潜在干预靶点，再由 LLM 模块生成需实验验证的机制假设。

title: spOT-NMF: gene expression deconvolution via optimal transport with proximity-aware niche mapping for spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables direct profiling of cellular organization within intact tissues, yet two challenges limit its full exploitation: accurate reference-free deconvolution of mixed expression signals (including species-admixed models such as xenografts), and lack of tools that can translate per-spot program usage values into spatial niches. We developed spOT-NMF, an optimal transport-based non-negative matrix factorization method that replaces standard reconstruction loss with the Wasserstein distance to disentangle mixed signals without requiring matched single-cell atlases. While the generalized OT-NMF factorization is applicable to any expression matrix, a proximity-based niche inference module further translates program co-usage from spatial transcriptomes into directional co-occurrence networks that define tissue compartments and their boundaries. Benchmarking across five gold-standard datasets spanning sub-cellular to multi-cellular resolutions, multiple platforms, and two-species admixture scenarios, spOT-NMF ranks first among reference-free methods, with particular advantage under the signal imbalance conditions characteristic of xenografts. We show that reference-free deconvolution recovers cell populations absent from matched single-cell atlases, highlighting the value of unsupervised analysis. Applied to glioblastoma xenografts and human colorectal cancer, spOT-NMF reveals spatially restricted interferon signaling, invasion routes, and CAF-tumor boundaries. spOT-NMF is available as an open-source Python package with GPU, CPU, and HPC support.

llm.novelty_zh: 用Wasserstein距离替代NMF的重构损失，实现无参考的空间转录组表达反卷积，并加入邻近感知的生态位推断模块。
llm.summary_zh: spOT-NMF以最优传输距离代替标准重构损失进行非负矩阵分解，实现无需单细胞参考的空间转录组反卷积。作者在五个标准数据集上进行基准测试，报告其在无参考方法中排名第一，并在异种移植和结直肠癌中揭示了空间限定的干扰素信号与肿瘤-成纤维细胞边界。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该方法可在缺少匹配单细胞图谱时发现未被参考覆盖的细胞群，并以开源包形式提供。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling
abstract: Recent advances in single-cell biology enable the profiling of multiple molecular layers, such as the transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins, within a single cell. Tackling the complexity of these data from multiple perspectives allows researchers to gain the most comprehensive insights into cellular biological properties. Here, we propose a graph-based topic modelling method called bionSBM. Our method leverages well-known community-detection methods for multipartite graphs and the interpretability of topic modelling to cluster and explain high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell matrices. We applied our algorithm to paired single-cell multi-omics data, such as 10X Multiome, SHARE-seq, and CITE-seq. We showed that it achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods for ground-truth label retrieval, with high specificity and distinct biological interpretability.

title: ASAOT: an accentuated structure-differentiated asymmetric optimal transport model for cell type and single-cell spatial mapping
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (STs) characterizes spatiotemporal gene expression and facilitates analysis of cellular architecture and cell-cell crosstalk within tissue microenvironments. However, existing spatial deconvolution methods employ globally fixed smoothing without local sharpening, which blurs cellular boundaries and impedes reconstruction of layered, heterogeneous cellular patterns in brain tissue. Here, we present Accentuated Structure-differentiated Asymmetric Optimal Transport (ASAOT), a deconvolution framework built on structure-enhanced asymmetric optimal transport. Coupled with spatial neighborhood constraints, ASAOT introduces a differentiated accentuated sharpening term to maintain global spatial continuity, enhance boundary detection, and preserve spot-level expression heterogeneity. Using asymmetric optimal transport, the framework jointly estimates spot-wise cell-type proportions and performs spatial assignment of reference single-cell coordinates. Benchmarks on diverse simulated datasets demonstrate that ASAOT achieves competitive overall accuracy and robustness across moderate spatial resolutions, with the best average comprehensive rank among tested methods. Applications to mouse olfactory bulb and cerebral cortex datasets demonstrate that ASAOT reduces signal diffusion and boundary distortion, effectively recovering layered brain anatomy and stratified cell distributions to build interpretable spatial maps of reference single-cell profiles. Collectively, ASAOT addresses critical drawbacks of conventional methods via a sharpening regularization term, serving as a reliable tool for STs analysis and mechanism exploration of tissue spatial organization.

llm.novelty_zh: 在非对称最优传输中加入结构增强的锐化项，改善空间转录组解卷积的边界还原。
llm.summary_zh: ASAOT 是用于空间转录组细胞类型比例估计与参考单细胞坐标空间分配的解卷积框架。方法在非对称最优传输中加入空间邻域约束与锐化正则项，以提高边界清晰度。在模拟数据以及小鼠嗅球和大脑皮层数据上，方法减少了信号扩散并恢复了分层脑结构。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提升了空间解卷积对组织分层结构的刻画能力，便于解析组织空间组织。
llm.limitations_zh: 基准测试主要基于中等空间分辨率的模拟数据。

title: Structured multi-view relational learning for drug response prediction
abstract: Drug response prediction (DRP) requires models that jointly characterize molecular drug structure and heterogeneous cellular states. Although recent deep learning approaches have integrated multi-omics profiles with drug representations, many treat omics views as parallel feature sources or merge them before relational modeling, which can weaken omics-view-specific cell-line relation structures. Here, we propose MulDR, a structured multi-view relational learning framework that preserves omics-view-specific cell-line relation structures before drug-conditioned cell-drug interaction. MulDR constructs separate relation structures for pathway activity, gene expression, mutation, and DNA methylation, learns view-specific relational cell representations, and uses complementary motif-level, geometry-aware molecular graph, and Morgan fingerprint drug representations to condition their fusion. With this design, cell-line similarity remains view-dependent until the interaction stage, rather than being prematurely compressed into a single feature or relation space. Extensive experiments show that MulDR consistently outperforms representative and recent baselines under the same evaluation protocol, reducing root mean square error by 6.07% relative to the strongest baseline. Cold-start evaluations on unseen drugs and cell lines further show that MulDR generalizes to previously unseen entities, while ablation studies show that removing either view-specific relational modeling or drug-conditioned fusion consistently compromises predictive performance. Together, these results suggest that preserving omics-specific cell-line relations before drug-conditioned interaction modeling provides an effective strategy for robust DRP.

llm.summary_zh: MulDR为药物反应预测框架，对通路活性、基因表达、突变和DNA甲基化分别构建细胞系关系结构，再以药物条件化方式进行交互。摘要称其优于代表性基线，RMSE较最强基线降低6.07%，并在未见药物和细胞系的冷启动评估与消融实验中表现稳定。

title: Response to comments on “SpatialDG: a novel spatial domain identification method for spatially resolved transcriptomics data based on dual-graph neural network”
abstract: We respond to concerns regarding reference-label-informed epoch selection in SpatialDG. We acknowledge this limitation and report a matched DLPFC reevaluation of SpatialDG and Spatial-MGCN under the same reference-label-independent checkpoint-selection rule, in which SpatialDG achieved the higher three-seed mean ARI on all 12 slices.

llm.novelty_zh: 针对评论的回应，不提出新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 这是一篇对 SpatialDG 评论的回应，承认参考标签参与训练轮次选择的问题，并在与标签无关的检查点规则下重新评估 SpatialDG 与 Spatial-MGCN，结果显示 SpatialDG 在 12 个切片上的三次平均 ARI 更高。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及方法本身的新改进。

title: IsoPrism predicts isoform usage from short-read transcriptomes through structure-guided competitive allocation
abstract: Short-read (SR) single-cell and spatial transcriptomics characterize gene expression but provide limited resolution of within-gene isoform usage. Here we present IsoPrism, a structure-guided competitive allocation framework that predicts isoform proportions from gene-level expression. IsoPrism combines individual expression and local expression context with transcript structural annotations, using shared iterative updates to preserve non-negative, gene-normalized proportions. Joint supervision from individual long-read (LR) counts and group-level isoform usage enables prediction in samples without matched LR measurements. Across five transfer scenarios derived from three paired transcriptomic resources, IsoPrism achieved the highest mean dominant isoform accuracy, compositional similarity, and cluster-level allocation correlation among eight evaluated methods. Ablation analyses supported complementary contributions from structural queries, expression context, iterative allocation, and dual-resolution supervision. Applied to a developing mouse cortex atlas, IsoPrism identified stage- and cell-type-associated isoform-usage patterns, including variation in the predicted relative usage of two Pkm transcripts. IsoPrism enables isoform-usage analysis of SR transcriptomes by transferring information from paired LR references, extending the analytical value of existing single-cell and spatial gene-expression atlases.

llm.novelty_zh: 以结构注释引导的竞争性分配框架，从短读长转录组预测异构体比例，并以长读长数据作为监督。
llm.summary_zh: IsoPrism根据基因水平表达与转录本结构注释预测异构体比例，并通过个体长读长计数与分组异构体使用的双重监督，实现向无长读长样本的迁移。作者在五种迁移场景中与八种方法比较，并在小鼠皮层图谱中识别了阶段与细胞类型相关的异构体使用模式。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工具扩展了现有短读长单细胞与空间转录组数据的异构体分析能力。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: spaDWGCN: a spatial distance weighted graph convolution network for accurate spatial tissue structure identification
abstract: The continuous development of spatial transcriptomics enables us to obtain gene expression matrices alongside spatial coordinate labels for cells or spots, providing tools for understanding spatial tissue microenvironments and spatially resolved cell-cell interactions. Although numerous methods have been developed to identify spatial tissue architecture, most of them adopt binary adjacency matrices that treat all neighboring cells equally, and few comprehensively incorporate distance information into both graph construction and feature representation. Here we introduce spaDWGCN, a spatial distance weighted graph convolutional network algorithm that takes cellular gene expression and microenvironment composition as inputs. This approach introduces fine-grained distance weighting at two levels: replacing the conventional 0-1 binary adjacency matrix with a distance-weighted adjacency matrix at the graph level, and substituting the neighbor count matrix with a distance-weighted microenvironment composition matrix at the feature level. Furthermore, spaDWGCN jointly models gene expression and microenvironment composition through separate graph convolutional network branches and trainable fusion, integrating transcriptional patterns with their local neighborhood context within a unified framework. Experiments on spatial transcriptomics multi-platform datasets, including MERFISH, STARmap, Stereo-seq, Slide-seqV2, and 10× Visium, demonstrate that this distance-weighted strategy achieves competitive performance in spatial domain identification and other downstream analyses.
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Industrial Control Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 将距离加权邻接矩阵与距离加权微环境组成引入图卷积网络，用于空间组织结构识别。
llm.summary_zh: spaDWGCN 是一种距离加权图卷积网络，分别建模基因表达与微环境组成两个分支并进行可训练融合，用于识别空间组织结构。作者在 MERFISH、STARmap、Stereo-seq、Slide-seqV2 和 10× Visium 数据上报告了有竞争力的空间域识别结果。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该方法改进了空间组织结构识别中的图构建方式，主要服务于空间组学分析，与虚拟细胞建模的关联有限。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: GLAlign integrates single-cell multi-omics data via global manifold and local marker gene alignment
abstract: Integrating heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics datasets remains challenging because different modalities are measured in distinct feature spaces and lack cell level pairing. Existing manifold alignment or feature conversion framework are often affected by weak cross-modality associations, geometric ambiguity, and overcorrection. Here we present GLAlign (Global manifold and Local marker gene Alignment), an optimization framework that jointly leverages global manifold structure and local marker gene information to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. GLAlign learns a shared latent space through a global objective comprising maximum mean discrepancy, distortion, and penalty terms, together with a local contrastive triplet loss guided by cross-modality marker gene overlap between independently inferred clusters. We demonstrate GLAlign's methodological contribution in extending the manifold alignment by biologically informed prior to ensure geometrically plausible and biologically correct alignments without requiring paired cells or manual cell type annotations. We evaluated GLAlign on simulated data and real datasets spanning PBMC scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq, mouse brain SNARE-seq, single-donor and multi-batch CITE-seq, and NCI-N87 scDNA-seq/scRNA-seq integration. Across the evaluated datasets, GLAlign achieved strong modality mixing and biological conservation, remained stable under moderate cell type imbalance and variations in clustering and marker information, and supported cross-modality label transfer and paired cell recovery. These results demonstrate that biologically structured coupling of global and local alignment provides an interpretable framework for heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics integration. GLAlign is freely available at https://github.com/Bateer-Bio/GLAlign.

llm.novelty_zh: 在全局流形对齐基础上加入基于标记基因的局部对比约束。
llm.summary_zh: GLAlign 用全局 MMD、畸变与惩罚项，以及基于标记基因重叠的局部三元组损失，在无配对细胞条件下对齐不同模态的单细胞数据。在 PBMC、SNARE-seq、CITE-seq 等数据上验证了混合与生物学保守性能，代码公开可用。

title: Computational immunogenicity prediction for mRNA vaccines: benchmarks, bottlenecks, and the peptide-nucleotide gap.
abstract: Computational prediction of T-cell epitopes has become indispensable to vaccine design, yet the field still relies on the assumption that how much of a given antigen is produced is fixed by its coding sequence. However, this is not the case with mRNA vaccines, i.e. the design of the mRNA template can vastly alter the quantity of the same protein produced. Codon usage, guanine-cytosine (GC) content, untranslated-region (UTR) design, and predicted secondary structure together define how fast the message is translated and how long it survives, and therefore how much antigen ever reaches the presentation pathway. This is a variable that no current immunogenicity predictor represents. Herein we appraise three decades of computational immunogenicity prediction, tracing the path from position-specific scoring matrices through pan-specific neural networks to transformer-based protein language models, and we use that history to expose the peptide-nucleotide gap between these tools and the way mRNA vaccines are designed. A structured synthesis of published evaluations of leading predictors across human leukocyte antigen (HLA) alleles, peptide lengths and data types shows that headline accuracy masks persistent deficiencies in predicting major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II, which underpins durable T-cell help, and rare alleles, which disproportionately affect under-represented populations. Four bottlenecks continue to constrain the field: class II prediction, T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition, immunodominance, and the disconnection between nucleotide-level design and peptide-level prediction. We argue that the last of these, which has drawn the least attention, is, in our assessment, the most likely to yield near-term gains for personalised cancer vaccines and pandemic preparedness, and we set out an architecture that couples translation-rate prediction to peptide presentation. Building it will require data that do not yet exist; we specify what must be measured, and on which platforms.

title: Interpretable anticancer drug response prediction in cell lines with tissue-specific gene weighting
abstract: Accurate prediction of anticancer drug response from molecular profiles is central to precision oncology, yet existing deep learning models typically ignore tissue-specific gene expression patterns and rely on post-hoc explanation methods, limiting both biological insight and clinical utility. Here, we propose a tissue-aware framework that integrates tissue-specific gene weighting derived via the Rank of Outlier in K-statistics algorithm with cross-attention-based multimodal learning. By reweighting gene expression according to tissue-specific patterns, this approach explicitly encodes tissue context into the prediction pipeline. On Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer benchmarks (114 215 pairs, 181 drugs, and 682 cell lines) under the pair-level transductive split, the model achieves ${R}^2$ = 0.947 (Pearson's r = 0.977), outperforming all reproduced baselines by a wide margin ($\Delta{R}^2$ ≥ 0.132). Exploratory gene-importance analysis recovers known drug response determinants (e.g. BRAF at rank #2 of 35 830 combined genomic features for Dabrafenib; P < 10-4). A separate six tissue control study reduced mean squared error by 21.0% relative to unweighted inputs, with improvements in all six tissues across three seeds. These results demonstrate that, under the transductive evaluation in cancer cell lines, incorporating biological structure into model design yields pharmacogenomic models that are both highly accurate and interpretable through post-hoc, drug-conditioned gene-importance rankings. Source code is freely available at https://github.com/born-june04/drug-response-prediction.

llm.novelty_zh: 用ROKin算法获得组织特异性基因权重，并在跨模态注意力框架中显式编码组织背景，用于药物反应预测。
llm.summary_zh: 该模型依据组织特异基因加权方法重新调整基因表达，再通过交叉注意力融合药物与细胞系表示，以预测抗癌药物反应。作者在GDSC基准（114215对药物-细胞系组合）上报告R²为0.947，并在六组织对照实验中降低了均方误差。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作显示把组织生物结构纳入模型设计，可以同时提高药物反应预测的准确性与可解释性。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Distilling direct effects via conditional differential gene expression analysis.
abstract: Motivation Differential gene expression (DGE) analysis is foundational for interpreting RNA sequencing data, but it conflates direct biological effects with correlations propagated through gene co-expression. Across three RNA sequencing datasets (including a genome-scale perturb-seq experiment), we find that only a small fraction of differentially expressed genes have direct effects on the trait of interest, while the majority are undirected or passengers whose associations are mediated through other genes. Results To distinguish direct effect genes, we introduce conditional differential gene expression (CDGE) analysis, a framework that tests for conditional rather than marginal association between each gene and the trait of interest. Implemented via the GhostKnockoff procedure with lasso regression, CDGE delivers false discovery rate control, operates on summary statistics from existing DGE pipelines, and accommodates batch effects. The genes identified by CDGE mediate the effects of most other differentially expressed genes and show stronger enrichment for known protein-protein interactions and biological pathways than DGE-identified genes. These results suggest that the field has been systematically over-interpreting DGE outputs, and that distinguishing direct from mediated effects is essential for prioritizing genes for functional follow-up and therapeutic development. Availability and implementation To facilitate public access to knockoff-based CDGE analysis, we have developed the R package "KnockoffCDGE" as an integrated implementation, which is freely available at https://github.com/GuJQ5/KnockoffCDGE (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23241517).

llm.summary_zh: 研究指出差异表达分析常将直接效应与共表达传播的关联混为一谈，并提出CDGE框架以条件而非边际关联检验基因与性状的关系。作者在三个RNA-seq数据集（含基因组尺度Perturb-seq）上验证了该方法的FDR控制，并以R包KnockoffCDGE提供实现。

title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data
abstract: MOTIVATION: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging. RESULTS: We present scPhyloGRN, a supervised framework that integrates single-cell gene expression with cellular phylogeny to prioritize directed transcription factor (TF)-target candidates within the observed gene set. The framework maps cell ancestry to gene associations that guide graph construction, attention in a dual-stream encoder, and lineage-consistency regularization. We evaluated scPhyloGRN against 10 methods across 17 dataset-reference settings spanning four mouse embryos and one Caenorhabditis elegans dataset. scPhyloGRN showed an overall advantage in regulatory edge prioritization, supported by additional evaluations using shared candidate spaces. Removing lineage information reduced AUPRC in the ablation analyses, while branch-level and regulator-level analyses showed improved ranking and recovery of reference-supported regulatory candidates. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Source code and analysis workflows are available at https://github.com/Maria0852/scPhyloGRN, with a versioned archive at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22793831.

title: Deep learning-based enhancing spatial biological context parsing.
abstract: Motivation The rapid advancement of spatial transcriptomics (ST) has established a foundation for the complementary integration of multimodal information from gene expression profiles, spatial localization, and histological images. However, noise and data heterogeneity complicate the characterization of spatial relationships and tissue structure. Results In this study, we develop a deep learning framework, CroSP, based on a multi-view graph autoencoder. The framework integrates gene expression profiles, spatial locations, and tissue morphology information into a low-dimensional latent representation. Cross-view contrastive learning and metric learning coordinate the complementary views. Across datasets from multiple platforms and spatial resolutions, CroSP improved spatial domain identification and delineated brain and olfactory bulb structures. Analyses using established downstream methods further characterized spatially variable genes and the spatial heterogeneity, immune microenvironments, and cell-cell communication in human breast cancer tissue. These results support the use of CroSP for spatial biological analysis in healthy and diseased tissues. Availability and implementation Source code and tutorials: https://github.com/Biowust/CroSP.git. Archived code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22675113. Public raw datasets: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22533825.

llm.summary_zh: 论文提出CroSP框架，通过多视图图自编码器整合基因表达、空间坐标与组织形态，学习低维潜在表示。在多平台数据上，该方法改善了空间域识别，并支持乳腺癌微环境分析。

title: TMCells: A topic-based probabilistic framework for interpretable metacell construction in single-cell data
abstract: MOTIVATION: Metacells have emerged as an important analytical strategy for addressing the computational barriers posed by the scale and complexity of large-scale single-cell omics data, while preserving biologically relevant information and improving analytical interpretability. However, existing metacell inference methods usually have limited biological interpretability, rely on deterministic assignments that insufficiently capture continuous state transitions, and may lose potential biological signals due to prior feature selection or dimensionality reduction. RESULTS: We propose TMCells, an interpretable metacell identification algorithm based on a probabilistic generative framework. TMCells introduces the concept of topic modeling and uses a Gaussian mixture model as the prior for topic distribution, defining metacells as statistical distribution centers in the latent topic space. By modeling the cell generation process, TMCells enables the simultaneous learning of topic representations and metacell partitions in an end-to-end manner, capturing the continuity and uncertainty in cell state transitions. TMCells effectively identifies high-quality metacells, eliminating technical noise while preserving the original biological heterogeneity, thereby enhancing downstream analyses such as differential expression, rare cell type identification, and trajectory inference. Furthermore, TMCells provides an intuitive interpretation of cellular heterogeneity through latent topics associated with biologically meaningful regulatory programs, offering a generative perspective for dissecting regulatory dynamics during cell-state transitions. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The TMCells along with detailed documentation is freely available at https://github.com/Jinsl-lab/TMCells with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24198840. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

llm.novelty_zh: 用概率主题模型与高斯混合先验在潜在主题空间中定义元细胞，实现端到端学习。
llm.summary_zh: 作者提出TMCells，基于概率生成框架以主题建模识别元细胞，使用高斯混合先验刻画主题分布，将元细胞定义为潜在主题空间中的统计中心。方法同时学习主题表示和元细胞划分，并能保留生物异质性，用于差异表达和轨迹推断等下游分析。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为大规模单细胞数据降维与可解释的元细胞构建提供了生成式方法。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及在大规模数据上的计算效率比较。

title: SpatialMuSC: Spatial Graph-Conditioned Diffusion Refinement for Robust Spatial Multi-Omics Integration
abstract: MOTIVATION: Emerging spatial multi-omics technologies enable the simultaneous profiling of multiple molecular layers within the same tissue section, offering new opportunities to interrogate tissue organization in its native spatial context. However, sequencing-derived spatial multi-omics data are often affected by intrinsic perturbations, such as technical noise, missing values, sparsity and measurement bias. These perturbations make existing methods that mainly use spatial graphs for neighborhood aggregation insufficient to recover continuous tissue-region structures, while unconstrained representation learning may propagate noisy associations and lead to fragmented spatial domains. RESULTS: We present SpatialMuSC, a robust spatial multi-omics integration framework centering on spatial graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency. SpatialMuSC introduces spatial topology as conditional information into the latent diffusion process, enabling spatial adjacency to guide neighborhood aggregation, spatial structure propagation and graph-aware denoising of latent states. Perturbation-invariant fusion consistency further encourages stable multi-omic fusion under perturbed observations. We evaluate SpatialMuSC on diverse spatial multi-omics datasets across different tissues and sequencing platforms, including 10x Visium, Stereo-CITE-seq, SPOTS and spatial epigenome-transcriptome data. Across these benchmarks, SpatialMuSC consistently outperforms ten state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification and tissue-structure preservation. Ablation analyses confirm the contributions of graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency, rather than post hoc graph smoothing or graph propagation alone. In particular, SpatialMuSC effectively distinguishes adjacent tissue regions, preserves block-wise smoothness and layered architectures, and shows more stable performance in missing-observation stress tests, while hippocampal marker, enrichment, and paired RNA-ATAC analyses identify a GCL-associated neuronal program and a TTR-associated accessibility feature in a choroid plexus-enriched domain. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code is available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/SpatialMuSC. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available online.

llm.novelty_zh: 将空间邻接作为条件输入引入潜在扩散过程，用于空间多组学的鲁棒整合。
llm.summary_zh: 作者提出SpatialMuSC，在空间多组学整合中引入空间图条件扩散精修与扰动不变融合一致性，以恢复连续组织区域结构。在10x Visium、Stereo-CITE-seq、SPOTS和空间表观转录组数据上，相对十种现有方法在空间域识别上表现更好。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为空间多组学的组织结构解析提供了较稳健的整合方法，代码已公开。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及计算成本以及对更多组织类型的泛化边界。

title: GLAND: Resolving small and non-continuous tissue domains via a hybrid attention mechanism
abstract: MOTIVATION: Recent advances in spatial transcriptomic technology provide unprecedented insights into tissue architecture by enabling high-throughput gene expression profiling with the corresponding spatial context. While identifying spatial domains is a prerequisite for understanding tissue heterogeneity and functional organization, current computational methods often fail to resolve non-continuous or small domains that, despite their biological significance, exhibit complex spatial distribution. RESULTS: We present GLAND, a deep learning framework with a hybrid attention mechanism designed to capture multi-scale spatial dependencies. GLAND utilizes a spatial outlier detection strategy to refine the spatial graph, coupled with a hybrid encoder that simultaneously captures long-range biological similarity and localized spatial continuity. Comprehensive benchmarking across 39 slices and 7 spatial transcriptomic platforms demonstrates that GLAND achieves superior performance in identifying not only traditional continuous spatial domains but also non-continuous and small domains. Within the complex tumor microenvironment, GLAND accurately resolves non-continuous tumor regions and small lymphoid aggregates. Its learned spot embeddings bridge spatial gaps by preserving the transcriptomic identity of tumor domains across distal locations, facilitating a unified characterization of heterogeneous tissue landscapes. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: GLAND is freely available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/GLAND. All data have been deposited to Zenodo at https://zenodo.org/records/18756215. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出结合空间离群点检测与混合注意力编码的GLAND，以识别小型及非连续空间域。
llm.summary_zh: GLAND是一种用于空间转录组的深度学习框架，通过空间离群点检测优化空间图，并用混合编码器同时捕获长程生物学相似性与局部空间连续性。作者在39个切片和7个平台上进行了基准测试，结果显示其在非连续和小型域识别上表现更优。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为肿瘤微环境等复杂组织中的空间域识别提供了工具。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: scPriorDiff: Bridging Single-Cell Modalities through Biological Network Prior-Guided Latent Diffusion
abstract: MOTIVATION: Single-cell multi-omics sequencing enables joint profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility, yet high-quality paired data remain scarce. Cross-modal translation based on generative modeling enables inference of an unmeasured modality from limited paired observations. However, substantial differences between gene expression and chromatin accessibility complicate cross-modal relationship modeling and the effective use of observed-modality information to guide target-modality generation. RESULTS: We propose scPriorDiff, a biological network prior-guided conditional latent diffusion model. scPriorDiff integrates diverse biological networks into a multimodal heterogeneous graph and employs a message-passing graph neural network (GNN) to learn biologically informed modality-specific representations that capture cross-modal and intra-modal relationships. To enable full-graph representation learning, a prior-regularized cross-modal completion module infers target-modality node representations during inference. The GNN-derived source representation conditions diffusion for target-modality generation. Across six paired single-cell multi-omics datasets, scPriorDiff outperformed eight representative methods and showed strong generalization across batches and to unseen cell types. Downstream analyses further demonstrated that the generated profiles preserved cell identities, molecular signatures, and biologically relevant functions. AVAILABILITY: The scPriorDiff software is publicly available at https://github.com/ChrisOliver2345/scPriorDiff and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23408383. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available as a separate file.

llm.summary_zh: scPriorDiff 在配对单细胞多组学中，由已观测模态推断未测量模态，例如由表达推断染色质可及性。方法将多种生物网络整合为异构图，用 GNN 学习模态表征并作为扩散模型的条件。在六个配对数据集上优于八种代表性方法，并对批次与未见细胞类型表现出泛化能力。
