title: Cellular and spatial continuum of TAM functional states governs immune exclusion and dictates immune checkpoint resistance in melanoma.
abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has transformed melanoma treatment, yet many patients either fail to respond or develop resistance after an initial response. The cellular and spatial determinants within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that underlie these divergent ICI therapy outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we aimed to characterize the immune composition and spatial organization of the TME associated with ICI response and resistance. Methods We integrated public scRNA-seq data (N = 32) with in-house spatial transcriptomics and imaging mass cytometry from an independent melanoma cohort (N = 6) to achieve high-resolution spatial profiling of the TME. This multimodal approach allowed us to map cellular heterogeneity within discrete spatial neighborhoods. To validate our findings, we constructed a scRNA-seq derived signature-matrix and deconvoluted a bulk RNA-seq cohort (N = 334). Clinical associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox hazard models, and a machine-learning classifier. Results We identified a distinct tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state, termed lipid-associated TAMs (LA-TAMs), characterized by conserved lipid metabolic programs and tumor-specific adaptations in glycolysis under hypoxic conditions. Deep spatial multi-omics profiling revealed divergent immune architectures associated with treatment outcomes. In non-responder patients, LA-TAMs colocalized with sparsely distributed TIM3⁺ exhausted CD8⁺ T cells within an immune-excluded TME. In contrast, responder patients harbored interferon-primed CCL4 + TAMs (IFN-TAMs) spatially associated with Granzyme B⁺ activated CD8⁺ T cells, reflecting an immune-active microenvironment. These findings define contrasting macrophage-centered immune neighborhoods linked to ICI response. Interestingly, patients with LA-TAM-enriched neighborhoods were consistently non-responders or progressed during follow-up, irrespective of the presence of IFN-TAM neighborhoods. Lastly, we constructed a single-cell-derived signature matrix that estimates TAM fractions from bulk RNA-seq data and revealed LA-TAM abundance as a robust, independent predictor of poor ICI response and survival in a validation cohort. Conclusions Our study defines the spatial landscapes of TAM-heterogeneity in melanoma and identifies LA-TAM neighborhoods as an important feature of ICI resistance. Although patients span a continuum of TAM-centered immune states, the presence of LA-TAM is likely to diminish the beneficial effects of IFN-TAM-associated immune activation. Finally, our proposed Melanoma-TME-derived signature-matrix provides a translatable framework to robustly predict ICI response and resistance.

title: Harnessing single-cell omics for farmed animal improvement and human health.
abstract: Cellular heterogeneity underlies the regulation of complex traits and diseases, making cell-resolved molecular characterization fundamental for advancing precision agriculture and human biomedicine. Rapid advances in single-cell omics technologies, together with the ever-evolving computational methods, have led to the establishment of large-scale single cell atlases across multiple species, providing unprecedented opportunities to systematically dissect cellular diversity and regulatory mechanisms underlying complex phenotypes. In this review, we summarize recent progresses in single-cell sequencing technologies, reference cell atlas projects, and the integration of single-cell omics with population/quantitative genetics, as well as discuss how artificial intelligence and predictive perturbation modelling are reshaping single-cell research. Finally, we highlight future directions toward population-scale single-cell omics, AI-driven virtual cells/tissues, and genotype-cell/tissue-trait frameworks, which are expected to transform biological discovery, enable better design of veterinary medicines and human therapeutics, as well as accelerate sustainable farmed animal improvement and precision medicine.

title: Epigenetic programming of immune cells: unleashing anti-tumor potential and clinical perspectives.
abstract: Immune cell plasticity is a defining feature of tumor immunity and is increasingly recognized as being governed by epigenetic regulation. Advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics have uncovered an epigenetic checkpoint that integrates environmental cues within the tumor microenvironment (TME) to shape immune cell fate and function. In this review, we synthesize recent evidence supporting three interconnected paradigms of epigenetic control in tumor immunity from the perspective of immune cell heterogeneity, ecology, and state transitions. First, dynamic chromatin remodeling programs myeloid cell polarization and functional diversification. Second, epitranscriptomic regulation constrains T and B cell states, contributing to immune dysfunction and exhaustion. Third, spatially resolved epigenetic remodeling influences immune cell trafficking, positioning, and retention within tumors. Collectively, these mechanisms establish durable immune states that reinforce TME-driven immunosuppression. We further highlight emerging pharmacological strategies targeting epigenetic regulators to reprogram immune cell function and enhance anti-tumor immunity. This framework provides a foundation for leveraging epigenetic plasticity to improve the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Translational relevance of telomeric C-circles in cancer: from experimental research to potential clinical applications.
abstract: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) is a recombination-based telomere maintenance mechanism that sustains replicative immortality in approximately 10-15% of human cancers, particularly those of mesenchymal and neuroepithelial origin. As precision oncology increasingly demands biomarkers that accurately define telomere maintenance mechanisms, extrachromosomal telomeric C-circles - partially single-stranded, C-rich telomeric circular DNAs - have emerged as quantifiable indicators of ALT activity with growing diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic potential. Here, we summarize recent mechanistic and translational advances that establish C-circles as both functional readouts of ALT activity and clinically actionable biomarkers. We integrate emerging evidence into a unified model in which replication stress drives C-circle production through pathways that are dynamically shaped by telomeric DNA structures and DNA repair factors, linking the molecular origin of C-circle to specific vulnerabilities with therapeutic implications. We further critically evaluate current detection technologies, spanning the gold-standard C-circle assay and its quantitative PCR and high-throughput adaptations and single-cell native FISH, which collectively enable sensitive and scalable detection across tissue specimens and liquid biopsies, including exosome-protected C-circles. Therapeutically, the molecular circuitry underlying C-circle production exposes selective ALT dependencies on replication stress and DNA repair regulators. Perturbation of these nodes reshapes C-circle dynamics while revealing synthetic lethal vulnerabilities that can be exploited through helicase-, nuclease-, chromatin-, replication stress-, and G-quadruplex-targeted strategies. We also discuss the important caveat that telomerase-positive tumors with hyperextended telomeres can generate C-circles, emphasizing the need for cautious interpretation of C-circle measurements. Clinically, CC appear to define ALT status more reliably than surrogate genomic markers such as ATRX/DAXX loss and may refine patient stratification, with potential implications for patient outcomes and treatment selection. In addition, the detection of circulating CC in liquid biopsies raises the possibility of their use as biomarkers for treatment monitoring and disease surveillance. Collectively, CC have evolved from experimental hallmarks of ALT into mechanistically informative and potentially actionable biomarkers. Continued assay standardization and integration into tissue and liquid biopsy workflows will be essential to support their clinical translation.

title: Super-enhancers: regulatory mechanisms, biological functions, diseases, and therapeutic targets.
abstract: Super-enhancers (SEs) are operationally defined as clusters of cis-regulatory elements associated with high transcriptional activity and cell-identity genes. They display dense transcription factor and coactivator occupancy, strong H3K27 acetylation, and enhancer-promoter communication, but their annotation varies across platforms, algorithms, and thresholds. This review examines SE architecture, identification, and validation, distinguishing chromatin-based annotation from functional dependence demonstrated by locus-specific perturbations. Mechanisms of SE-associated transcription include pioneer factors, chromatin remodelers, three-dimensional genome organization, transcriptional condensates, non-coding RNAs, and extrachromosomal DNA. Physiological functions in development, immunity, and metabolic homeostasis are considered alongside context-dependent dysregulation in cancer, inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, neurological disorders, and metabolic diseases. Breast cancer provides a model for examining subtype-specific regulation and transcriptional plasticity. Particular attention is given to enhancer remodeling during endocrine therapy, cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibition, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted treatment, and chemotherapy, which may support bypass signaling, stemness, and persistent resistance. Causal regulatory changes must nevertheless be distinguished from correlates of treatment selection. Therapeutic approaches targeting bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins, CDK7/9, chromatin regulators, enhancer RNAs, and regulatory loci are critically evaluated. Definitional uncertainty, model dependence, limited reproducibility, systemic toxicity, and insufficient clinical validation remain major barriers. Priorities include standardized annotation, temporally resolved perturbation, single-cell and spatial profiling, artificial intelligence-assisted integration, patient-derived models, and biomarker-guided therapeutic development. Together, these perspectives position SEs as a context-dependent framework linking regulatory architecture to disease progression and treatment resistance, while emphasizing the evidence required to establish therapeutic vulnerabilities.

title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network
abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

title: SpatioCAD: Context-aware graph diffusion model for pinpointing spatially variable genes in heterogeneous tissues
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables comprehensive characterization of tissue architecture, and the identification of spatially variable genes (SVGs) is a critical step for defining region-specific molecular markers and uncovering spatially regulated mechanisms across diverse biological contexts. However, most existing methods for SVG detection overlook cell density variations, a major confounding factor in complex tissues such as tumors, where heterogeneous cellularity frequently introduces false-positive calls. Here we present SpatioCAD, a computational framework that explicitly decouples genuine spatial expression patterns from confounding effects driven by cellularity. SpatioCAD introduces a graph diffusion model that inherently incorporates cell-density-aware conditions to simulate expression propagation, supporting the identification of SVGs across a broad range of expression levels. Systematic evaluations on simulated datasets demonstrate its superior statistical power and specificity. Applied to breast cancer, lung cancer, and glioma datasets, SpatioCAD identifies functionally diverse SVGs, including low‑abundance transcripts with established roles in tumor progression, while also recapitulates biologically meaningful tissue architecture features. Importantly, SpatioCAD is fast and scalable to large tissues.

llm.novelty_zh: 用细胞密度感知的图扩散模型区分真实空间表达模式与细胞密度混杂效应。
llm.summary_zh: 作者提出SpatioCAD，用图扩散模型识别空间可变基因，并显式考虑细胞密度变化带来的混杂效应。模拟数据显示其统计功效和特异性较高，并在乳腺癌、肺癌和胶质瘤数据中识别出功能多样的空间变异基因。

llm.limitations_zh: 评估主要基于模拟数据，摘要未提及与近期方法的系统比较。

title: Systematic clustering alignment and feature characterization for single-cell omics using ACE-OF-Clust
abstract: Clustering is widely used to identify cell types in cellular-resolution transcriptomic data, including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST). Mixed-membership clustering assigns fractional memberships across clusters and captures continuous variation beyond hard clustering, but integrating and interpreting results from either approach is complicated by the "clustering alignment problem," which arises from label switching, multi-modality, and differences in model settings (including differing numbers of clusters). We introduce ACE-OF-Clust, enabling a four-step workflow for single-cell clustering: multiple clustering, clustering alignment, model comparison, and identification of informative features. ACE-OF-Clust introduces direct comparison of clustering solutions, assesses consistency against annotations, and leverages feature-level clustering profiles to prioritize genes discriminating among cell types, as well as to evaluate how gene sets contribute to clustering patterns. We demonstrate its utility using PBMC scRNA-seq data, breast cancer and mouse embryo ST data, and single-cell multi-omic data. ACE-OF-Clust quantifies cross-omic clustering variability and suggests putative cross-omic regulatory links. Overall, ACE-OF-Clust increases the interpretability, flexibility, and robustness of single-cell clustering, providing a scalable tool for studying cellular heterogeneity and gene expression dynamics.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出四步单细胞聚类工作流，直接比较多次聚类结果并解决标签交换导致的聚类对齐问题。
llm.summary_zh: ACE-OF-Clust面向混合隶属聚类结果，提供多次聚类、聚类对齐、模型比较和特征识别的完整流程，并能对照注释评估一致性。作者在PBMC、乳腺癌和小鼠胚胎空间数据以及单细胞多组学数据上展示其应用。

title: Sphinx: An R package for adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling and functional analysis in spatial omics
abstract: Spatial omics enables analysis of tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, but most spatial tools are optimized for transcriptomics and poorly suited to proteomics data. We developed Sphinx, an R package providing a comprehensive workflow for spatial proteomics, including preprocessing, cell annotation, adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. Importantly, it introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework guided by spatial statistical metrics and incorporates computational optimizations for large-scale datasets, enabling robust neighborhood modeling. Notably, Sphinx offers improved computational efficiency and scalability. Across lung adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and mouse spleen datasets, Sphinx robustly identifies cell types and spatial functional units, including tertiary lymphoid structures. We also explored the application of Sphinx to paired high-resolution spatial transcriptomics datasets, illustrating its potential applicability. Sphinx provides a flexible and efficient framework for spatial proteomics, enabling robust characterization of spatial organization and tissue microenvironments.

llm.summary_zh: Sphinx 是面向空间蛋白质组的 R 包，涵盖预处理、细胞注释、自适应空间邻域建模与功能分析，在肺腺癌、结直肠癌和小鼠脾脏数据中识别包括三级淋巴结构在内的空间功能单元。

title: Transforming Neuroscience Research through AI-Driven Data Integration and Analysis
abstract: Integrating multimodal data is essential to advance neuroscience as a discipline. Large-scale collaborative efforts, exemplified by the BRAIN Initiative, together with advances in single-cell and spatial omics, multimodal imaging, human genetics, behavioral phenotyping, protein structure prediction, and related technologies, are transforming neuroscience into a data-rich, highly interconnected science. As experimental resources, scientific literature, and collaborative networks continue to expand, integrating discoveries across modalities, species, and levels of biological organization has become the field's central bottleneck. This Perspective argues that artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming essential for overcoming these constraints. Using six evolving approaches we outline strategies to accelerate AI adoption through community building and pilot projects that drive AI transformation at both the organizational and technological levels. Organizational transformation cultivates broad AI awareness and a pro-AI culture while technological transformation improves the efficiency, scalability, and quality of data analysis, allowing researchers to generate insights more rapidly and effectively. Together, these advances position AI as a key driver for advancing neuroscience at scale.
affiliations: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

llm.novelty_zh: 观点文章，提出六种推动神经科学AI转型的方法路径，无新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 该观点文章认为多模态数据与跨物种整合已成为神经科学的核心瓶颈，AI是应对这一挑战的关键。作者提出六种演进中的方法，并区分组织层面与技术层面的AI转型。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 讨论神经科学大规模数据整合与社区建设，对研究组织方式有启发。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Evaluating Cross-Cohort Transfer and Model Explanations in a Fine-Tuned Single-Cell Foundation Model for Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Because complex gene networks are pleiotropic, representations learned from single-cell transcriptomes may encode information relevant to multiple traits rather than a single disease endpoint. We asked whether scGPT, a foundation model for single-cell data, could predict Alzheimer's disease (AD) across independent studies and what other information its internal representations retained. We fine-tuned scGPT on ROSMAP and applied the five resulting cross-validation models to SEA-AD without retraining. Classification performance, measured by AUC, averaged 0.827 ± 0.058 in held-out ROSMAP donors and 0.827 ± 0.025 in SEA-AD. We compared two input sets of about 2,000 genes: genes with high cell-to-cell variation and genes associated with AD after adjustment for sex, age, and postmortem interval. Both sets produced similar prediction accuracy and stable gene-importance rankings, but their representations differed. Donor sex was almost perfectly predictable from the high-variability representation, whereas the adjusted-gene representation remained strongly predictive of AD while sex was much less predictable. Sex-related signals may be easier to identify because they include strong expression from sex-linked genes, whereas AD reflects a more complex combination of genetic, cellular, environmental, and clinical factors. In microglia, genes highlighted by the adjusted-gene models overlapped in both cohorts with published AD-related gene sets, including 6–7 of the 15 TYROBP-network genes available in the panel. Overall, scGPT transferred useful AD classification performance across cohorts, but the information it learned depended on gene selection. The results are consistent with scGPT capturing overlapping gene pathways that may help predict multiple traits.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series

llm.novelty_zh: 将在ROSMAP上微调的scGPT直接迁移到SEA-AD，并比较两类基因集下表征所编码信息的差异。
llm.summary_zh: 研究在ROSMAP上微调scGPT，并将五折模型直接用于SEA-AD，阿尔茨海默病分类AUC约为0.83。比较高变基因与疾病相关调整基因两种输入，发现性别信息在高变表征中极易预测，而调整基因表征对AD保持较强预测力。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 说明scFM的跨队列迁移效果依赖于基因选择，对解释基础模型学到的内容有参考价值。

title: An open and reproducible benchmark for virtual cell models in human preimplantation embryo single-cell atlases
abstract: This study delivers an open, reproducible evaluation framework for virtual cell / single-cell foundation models in the setting of human preimplantation embryo atlases. It is entirely computational, uses only publicly available previously published data, and involves no wet-laboratory work and no new biological samples. The primary scientific gap is stated in advance: paired perturbational single-cell data (Perturb-seq / CRISPRi with matched differential-expression ground truth) from human preimplantation embryos are largely unavailable. The study therefore does not claim to benchmark embryo perturbation prediction directly. Instead it measures how far representations trained in other contexts remain usable when projected onto early embryo atlases, and reports the boundary of valid inference.

llm.novelty_zh: 面向人类植入前胚胎图谱，构建开放、可复现的虚拟细胞表征评估框架。
llm.summary_zh: 研究提出一个开放可复现的评估框架，用公开的已发表数据考察在其他情境中训练的单细胞基础模型表征投影到早期胚胎图谱后的可用程度，并报告推断的有效边界。作者明确说明由于缺乏配对扰动数据，并不直接评估胚胎扰动预测。

title: Do single-cell foundation models annotate immune cells less accurately for donors of African ancestry? A preregistered benchmark
abstract: Single-cell foundation models (scGPT, Geneformer, UCE, scFoundation) are increasingly used to annotate cell types, yet their training data come overwhelmingly from donors of European ancestry. In CELLxGENE Census (release 2025-11-08), only 4 of 2,252 healthy blood donors are recorded as African ancestry. This study tests whether these models annotate peripheral blood immune cells less accurately for African-ancestry than European-ancestry donors, and whether any gap exceeds that of non-foundation baselines (scVI, CellTypist, PCA). The primary analysis uses an open dataset in which African American and European American donors were processed within the same 10x captures (Randolph et al. 2021, GSE162632; 45 vs 45 donors), with replication in an open prostate cancer PBMC cohort (GSE270387; 33 vs 24 donors). The outcome is per-donor macro-F1 against reference cell-type labels, analysed at the donor level with a preregistered smallest effect of interest of 2 macro-F1 points and equivalence testing for null results. Secondary aims test ancestry-balanced fine-tuning, the cell types driving any gap, and ancestry structure in model embeddings. Data preparation, QC, labelling and donor splits were completed before registration; no ancestry-stratified result has been computed or viewed

llm.novelty_zh: 预注册检验单细胞基础模型在非欧洲血统供体上的免疫细胞注释是否存在差距。
llm.summary_zh: 研究预注册了一项基准，比较 scGPT、Geneformer、UCE、scFoundation 与 scVI、CellTypist、PCA 对非洲裔与欧洲裔供体外周血免疫细胞的注释表现。主要分析基于 GSE162632 的同批次数据，并在 GSE270387 前列腺癌 PBMC 队列中重复。目前仅完成数据准备，尚未计算分层结果。

title: A POSTN-centered feed-forward regulatory network drives fibroblast ECM remodeling in OPLL
abstract: This dataset contains the complete supplementary data tables (Supplementary Tables 1-12) supporting the manuscript "A POSTN-centered feed-forward regulatory network drives fibroblast ECM remodeling in ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament". The tables were generated by integrative re-analysis of six publicly available transcriptomic datasets: GSE69787 (bulk RNA-seq, OPLL vs. control; discovery cohort), GSE188760 (bulk RNA-seq; independent OPLL tissue cohort), GSE188759 (orthogonal chondrogenic-differentiation model), GSE183752 (OPLL disease-neighborhood tissue), GSE83569 (OPLL-derived fibroblasts under cyclic tensile strain), and GSE241505 (single-cell RNA-seq atlas of OPLL). Contents (one worksheet per table): - Table 1. Basic characteristics of the public datasets included in this study. - Table 2. Complete differential-expression results (2A: GSE69787; 2B: GSE188760; 2C: GSE241505 pseudobulk). - Table 3. Complete marker-gene table for the major single-cell clusters. - Table 4. Fibroblast-focused reclustering markers, subcluster annotation, and cell metadata (4A-4C). - Table 5. Complete ligand-receptor interactions and communication summaries (5A-5C). - Table 6. Integrated core candidate genes (6A-6B). - Table 7. Pseudotime-associated genes and ranked qPCR validation candidates (7A-7C). - Table 8. Motif-pruned pySCENIC regulon summary, target-level results, and metadata (8A-8C). - Table 9. Cross-dataset triangulation summary and targeted external-validation statistics (9A-9H). - Table 10. Feed-forward network TF-ECM regulatory weights and GENIE3-derived TF-target edges (10A-10B). - Table 11. Module-level discriminative performance (AUC) across independent datasets. - Table 12. In silico perturbation predictions for the feed-forward network. Analysis methods: bulk differential expression with DESeq2; single-cell preprocessing, clustering, and preliminary annotation with scanpy; cell-cell communication inference using a CellPhoneDB-based ligand-receptor reference; diffusion pseudotime (DPT); motif-pruned pySCENIC (GRNBoost2 + cisTarget + AUCell); genome-wide gene regulatory network inference with GENIE3; directional integration of inferred TF-target edges with STRING v12 and TRRUST v2; and in silico TF perturbation based on normalized regulatory weights. File organization: "Supplementary Tables.xlsx" contains all tables as individual worksheets, each preceded by its title and legend.
keywords: ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament

llm.novelty_zh: 发布 OPLL 研究的补充数据表，包括整合六个公共转录组数据集得到的差异表达与调控网络结果。
llm.summary_zh: 该数据集包含 12 张补充表，由六个公开转录组数据集（含 bulk 与单细胞）再分析得到，涵盖差异表达、标记基因、配体受体互作、pySCENIC 调控子与外部验证等内容。它是论文的支持数据，而非新的实验平台。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及样本规模及各数据集之间的批次校正方式。

title: Development of a Modular Computational Virtual-Cell Framework Integrating Drug–Target Interactions, Intracellular Signaling, Energy Metabolism, and Vesicular Trafficking
abstract: Understanding drug effects at the cellular level requires consideration of interconnected processes, including molecular target engagement, intracellular signal transduction, energy metabolism, gene expression, and vesicular trafficking. Computational biology provides methods for representing these processes at different levels of detail, but integrating them in a transparent and extensible software architecture remains challenging [1–3]. This paper de scribes the conceptual design and initial Python implementation of a modular computational virtual-cell framework for a simplified eukaryotic cell. The framework uses a two-dimensional circular geometry, a discretized plasma membrane, membrane-associated components, mitochondria, microtubules, vesicles, and lysosomal compartments. The current implementation includes spatially proximity-based ligand–receptor interactions, receptor clustering, abounded second-messenger variable with an MAPK-associated proxy, simplified mitochondrial ATP accounting, delayedtranscription/translation events, and ATP-dependent vesicular transport. Drug–target interaction modeling and pathway-specific representations of RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK (MAPK/ERK), PI3K–AKT–mTOR, and JAK–STAT are specified as planned extensions; they are not yet complete molecular modules in the current code. Mathematical formulations are provided to guide these extensions and to make assumptions explicit. The framework is therefore presented as a developing computational architecture, not as an experimentally validated predictive model. Its purpose is to provide a modular foundation for subsequent implementation, software verification, parameterization, and biological validation.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出模块化的简化真核细胞虚拟架构，把药物靶点、信号、能量与囊泡运输纳入同一软件框架。
llm.summary_zh: 该文描述一个二维简化真核细胞模块化虚拟细胞框架的概念设计与初始Python实现，包括配体-受体相互作用、第二信使、线粒体ATP计算与囊泡运输。药物-靶点以及MAPK、PI3K-AKT-mTOR、JAK-STAT通路仍是规划中的扩展。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为后续整合药物效应与细胞过程的模拟提供了可扩展的架构基础。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要明确其为概念架构，未经实验验证，药物-靶点及通路模块尚未完成。

title: A Survey of AI Virtual Cells: Representation Learning, Perturbation Prediction, and Intervention Design
abstract: Predicting cellular responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports disease research and therapeutic discovery. Experimental screening is costly, limiting coverage of interventions and cellular contexts. This survey reviews artificial intelligence virtual cells (AIVC) through the progression from state representation learning to perturbation prediction and intervention design. We describe how state representations support response modeling and how learned responses guide intervention selection across previously untested interventions and diverse cellular contexts. We summarize data resources, representative model families, evaluation strategies, and multimodal, temporal, and spatial extensions, then discuss generalization and experimental feedback. A curated resource collection is available at https://github.com/ttruan2426-dot/Awesome-Single-Cell-Perturbation-Prediction.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述性质，系统梳理从状态表征到扰动预测再到干预设计的 AIVC 研究脉络，本身不提出新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 这篇综述按照状态表征学习、扰动预测、干预设计的顺序梳理 AI 虚拟细胞领域，总结了数据资源、代表性模型家族、评估策略及多模态、时序和空间扩展，并讨论了泛化与实验反馈，同时提供了一份策展资源列表。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 对新入门研究者和方向规划有参考价值，并提供了可持续维护的资源索引。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及文献检索范围与纳入标准。

title: From Contact Maps to Causal Biology: Benchmarking and Validating Computational Methods for 3D Genome Interpretation
abstract: Background: The three-dimensional (3D) organization of the genome is a key factor in gene regulation, cellular differentiation and disease pathogenesis. Chromatin interaction studies have been revolutionized by the advent of high-throughput chromosome conformation capture technologies, such as Hi-C, Micro-C, ChIA-PET, HiChIP, and single-cell Hi-C. However, computational analysis of these data remains challenging. This review aims to critically evaluate computational methods for 3D genome interpretation, with an emphasis on benchmarking strategies, methodological limitations and the experimental evidence supporting computational predictions. Methods: We performed targeted searches of PubMed and Google Scholar databases for studies published between January 2015 and August 2026 and followed up with reference chaining to find peer-reviewed publications related to computational analysis, benchmarking and experimental validation in 3D genomics. The emphasis is on representative and influential methods, not an exhaustive list. The cited evidence base excluded preprints, theses, duplicate citations or non-peer reviewed materials. Results: The literature can be divided into six recurring themes: TAD detection, loop calling, A/B compartment analysis, 3D structure reconstruction, deep learning, and single-cell Hi-C analysis. In all these divisions, we found that the reported performance is highly sensitive to sequencing depth, matrix resolution, assay type, cell type, preprocessing, and the selection of the validation proxy. Due to the lack of a universal biological ground truth, studies often integrate simulations, cross-method agreements, protein or histone enrichment, orthogonal assays, imaging, and perturbation experiments. Conclusions: Methodologically, the study of the 3D genome by computation is very diverse and is dependent on the study design. Transparent reporting, depth- and resolution-aware evaluation, orthogonal validation, and explicit separation of predictive accuracy from biological causality are essential for reliable interpretation. Future studies should focus on reproducible benchmark datasets, cross-assay testing, interpretable models, and experimentally testable chromatin structure-to-function relationships.

llm.novelty_zh: 系统梳理三维基因组计算方法的基准化与实验验证策略，属综述性归纳。
llm.summary_zh: 综述涵盖TAD检测、环识别、A/B区室分析、三维结构重建、深度学习和单细胞Hi-C六类计算方法。作者指出，这些方法的性能对测序深度、矩阵分辨率、细胞类型和验证代理高度敏感，并强调需要可复现的基准数据集和正交验证。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为评估染色质结构计算方法的可靠性提供了参考框架。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Agentic Virtual Cells (AVCs): From Cell Models to Auditable Discovery Systems
abstract: Virtual cells, computational models that predict how cellular state changes under genetic, chemical or environmental perturbation, are increasingly built, queried and revised by artificial intelligence (AI) agents rather than by human modellers alone. Here we argue that the consequential change is not a further increase in the capacity of any single model but the explicit implementation of an operator layer: the decisions about which model to trust, which evidence to add and which experiment to run that human modellers have always made implicitly. We define an agentic virtual cell as a coupled system of a predictive cell model, an agent policy, an evidence ledger and a laboratory interface, and we distinguish four couplings through which agents and virtual cells interact: agents use models as instruments, build models, plan with models as world models and learn from models as verifiers. Drawing on the 2025 Virtual Cell Challenge, recent benchmark disputes and the first agent-built and agent-operated systems, we show that current performance limits arise jointly from model capacity, coverage of biological context and evaluation design, and that agents can relieve the second but cannot, by orchestration alone, create causal identifiability. We propose a two-tier evaluation of model outputs and agent trajectories and state five falsifiable predictions for the next five years.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出「智能体虚拟细胞」概念，将模型选择、证据增补与实验决策形式化为一个显式的操作层。
llm.summary_zh: 这是一篇观点论文，主张虚拟细胞的关键变化在于引入显式的智能体操作层，而非单纯扩大模型容量。作者定义了由细胞模型、智能体策略、证据账本与实验接口构成的系统，并区分四类智能体与模型的交互方式。文章基于2025年虚拟细胞挑战赛与基准争议提出两级评测思路与五项可证伪预测。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为AI智能体参与虚拟细胞建模的研究议程提供了概念框架与可检验的预测。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及具体的实证验证，主要为论证性质。

title: The STP Open Challenge: A Community Effort to Define and Benchmark Spatial Transcriptome-to-Proteome Prediction
abstract: While spatial transcriptomics technologies are increasingly accessible, spatial proteomics remains constrained by high costs and limited throughput. Furthermore, poor mRNA-protein correlation, driven by post-transcriptional regulation, necessitates multi-omics integration for complementary biological insights. Current RNA-to-protein prediction models, primarily trained on bulk or single-cell data, often overlook critical spatial context. Consequently, it remains unclear which model architecture, spatial representation, or histopathological features best facilitate spatial protein abundance inference. To address these gaps, we defined the STP (Spatial Transcriptome-to-Proteome) task and launched the STP Open Challenge, a competition for predicting spatial proteomics from spatial transcriptomics of adjacent tissue sections. Utilizing a curated paired spatial dataset and a standardized evaluation framework, the challenge attracted 101 teams and yielded 896 valid submissions. Top-performing methods achieved strong predictive performance while preserving spatial organization. The landscape of submitted models revealed diverse modeling strategies and motivated us to develop a consensus-based ensemble framework that leverages various participant methods to enhance prediction robustness. Extended evaluation on unseen datasets demonstrated that the top-performing models outperformed existing baselines, highlighting the effectiveness of the community effort for this task. By formally defining the STP task and providing a standardized benchmarking platform, this work establishes a foundation for scalable, cost-effective spatial proteomics prediction and future multi-omics integration.
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Southern University of Science and Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 定义空间转录组到空间蛋白组（STP）的预测任务，并以开放竞赛形式建立标准化评测平台。
llm.summary_zh: 研究组织了 STP Open Challenge，要求依据相邻切片的空间转录组预测空间蛋白丰度，共吸引 101 个团队提交 896 份有效结果。论文还提出了基于参赛方法的共识集成框架，并报告其在未见数据集上优于现有基线。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作为低成本的空间蛋白组推断建立了统一任务与评测标准，对后续多组学整合具有基础意义。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Inverse design of chemical perturbations for desired cellular state transitions with GEMGen
abstract: Perturbation biology links interventions to resulting cellular changes, providing a basis for understanding and manipulating biological processes. Recent advances in computational modelling have enabled prediction of cellular responses to diverse perturbations. However, many biomedical applications require going beyond response prediction to identify perturbations capable of inducing desired responses, an inverse design problem that remains largely underexplored compared to the forward prediction task. Here we introduce GEMGen, a large language model-based framework for the inverse design of chemical perturbations conditioned on desired cellular state transitions. GEMGen represents transitions as text-based, rank-ordered differential-gene instructions, generates molecular structures autoregressively, and uses a compound-response scorer to prioritize candidates for experimental testing. Across multiple benchmarks, GEMGen recovered small molecules structurally or mechanistically relevant to ground-truth compounds, and also generalized across perturbation modalities by generating chemical interventions from genetic perturbation signatures, outperforming existing perturbation design approaches. Beyond in silico evaluation, when conditioned on transcriptional signatures related to tissue fibrosis, GEMGen yielded eight novel antifibrotic structures from 17 de novo synthesized candidates. Notably, one lead candidate, GEMGen-010, exhibited strong antifibrotic activity in animal models of liver fibrosis without any structural optimization. Together, these results establish GEMGen as an effective approach extending perturbation modeling toward intervention design, broadening the methodology and application scope of perturbation biology.

llm.novelty_zh: 将转录响应表示为有序差异基因文本，由LLM自回归生成分子结构，从期望的细胞状态转移反推化学扰动。
llm.summary_zh: GEMGen是基于大语言模型的化学扰动逆向设计框架，将细胞状态转移表示为有序差异基因文本指令，自回归生成分子结构，并用化合物响应评分器对候选物排序以供实验检验。作者报告其在多个基准上优于现有扰动设计方法，并在17个从头合成的候选物中得到8个新型抗纤维化结构，其中先导物在肝纤维化动物模型中显示活性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 将扰动建模从响应预测推进到干预设计，并给出湿实验与动物模型验证，实用价值突出。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及跨基准的完整基线细节及合成可行性的系统分析

title: Learning reproducible cellular perturbation responses from limited independent measurements
abstract: Large-scale perturbation atlases are increasingly used to train models that predict cellular responses, yet responses to individual perturbations are often measured only a few times. The resulting averages are commonly used as training targets, although they contain both reproducible perturbation effects and measurement-specific variation. Here we present RePert, a framework that uses independent measurements to construct reproducible targets for cellular-response prediction. RePert learns from separate measurements of the same perturbation, combines complementary estimates using independent calibration data, and uses a second assay to refine an existing response estimate. In two Cell Painting datasets and one gene-expression dataset, RePert estimates agreed more closely with held-out measurements than averages of the same measurements. In Cell Painting, they also better distinguished the correct compound from matched alternatives. In BBBC047, these estimates outperformed larger neural networks given identical inputs. Matched measurements from a second assay provided additional compound-specific information, with smaller gains when more Cell Painting measurements were available. The recovered responses also better preserved independently supported morphological features, response directions and patterns across doses. As training targets, they improved prediction of unseen compounds in BBBC047, whereas in sci-Plex3, with two measurements per condition, the effect depended on the prediction setting. Target construction is therefore a design dimension of perturbation modelling, distinct from model architecture and capacity.

llm.novelty_zh: 利用同一扰动的独立测量构建可复现的响应靶标，并借助独立校准数据与第二种检测方法进行整合。
llm.summary_zh: RePert 利用同一扰动的独立测量构建可复现的目标，结合独立校准数据组合互补估计，并用第二种检测方法细化已有响应。在两个 Cell Painting 数据集与一个基因表达数据集上，其估计与留出测量的吻合度优于同一测量的平均值；在 BBBC047 中，这些估计的表现优于输入相同但参数更多的神经网络。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 指出训练靶标构造本身是扰动建模的重要设计维度，对缓解测量噪声导致的训练偏差具有实际意义。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要指出在 sci-Plex3 中效果依赖预测设定，且 Cell Painting 测量增多时第二检测方法的增益减小。

title: Digital spatiotemporal landscaping of human chondrocyte differentiation during post-embryonic development
abstract: Chondrocyte differentiation governs skeletal formation, underpinning our understanding of human skeletal development and cartilage regenerative design. Existing human datasets are limited to early embryonic and late adult stages, leaving the critical post-conception week 9 to postnatal window poorly resolved. This gap obscures how compartmentalized osteochondral architectures are assembled from homogeneous mesenchymal condensates, and hinders digital predictive modeling of osteochondral biology and regeneration. Here, we comprehensively profiled human post-embryonic digits and identified prominent chondrocyte diversification from post-conception week 11 onwards. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with in situ validation, we resolved osteochondral, perichondral, vascular, and hematopoietic subpopulations and characterized key transitional chondrocyte states, including naive, typical, hypertrophic, and fibrotic chondrocyte subsets. Our analyses revealed the emergence of COL2A1high chondrocyte subpopulations, their cell-cell crosstalk, and their bifurcated developmental trajectories toward articular-surface and bone fates respectively. We mapped the spatiotemporal patterns of crucial progenitor cell biomarkers within the niche, including gremlin1 (GREM1), proteoglycan 4 (PRG4), and periostin (POSTN). Moreover, a rare HLA-DRA high subpopulation was discovered. This subpopulation co-expressed chondrocyte markers and antigen-presenting cell signatures, representing a fundamental but undiscovered transitional state during cartilage-to-bone differentiation. We further demonstrated that our digital Post-Embryonic Chondrocyte Niche Atlas was a reliable reference for optimizing human cartilage organoid engineering. These advances have led to the identification of new transition states in chondrocyte developmental plasticity. In summary, these studies provide new fundamental knowledge for post-embryonic skeletal maturation, and a robust digital resource to advance chondrocyte-based research and future regenerative therapies.

llm.novelty_zh: 填补胚胎早期与成体之间的人类软骨细胞分化数据空白，并构建数字化的出生后软骨龛图谱。
llm.summary_zh: 作者对人类出生后手指组织进行单细胞与空间转录组分析，并结合原位验证，鉴定了软骨细胞亚群及其过渡状态，包括COL2A1高表达亚群，描述了其向关节面和骨骼命运分叉的发育轨迹。研究还发现了HLA-DRA高表达的过渡亚群，并证明该图谱可作为优化软骨类器官工程的参考。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为骨骼发育与软骨再生研究提供了可复用的参考图谱。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: MuSpec: an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder recovers conserved granuloma niches and nominates host-directed repurposing candidates in human pulmonary tuberculosis
abstract: Abstract Background. Tuberculosis (TB) granulomas are spatially organised host–pathogen structures, and the spatial arrangement of immune and stromal cells within the granuloma shapes disease outcome. Spatial transcriptomics can now resolve these structures at single-cell resolution, but most spatial-niche models have been developed and validated on tumour tissue. There is a shortage of unsupervised methods benchmarked on infectious-disease granulomas, and little evidence on how such niche models behave under input noise, missing modalities, and cross-sample transfer — the conditions that decide whether a niche atlas is translational or merely descriptive. Methods. We assembled MuSpec , an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder, and applied it to two single-cell-resolution Stereo-seq slides from human TB lung: B1 (pulmonary granuloma; Y40012NC13; 36,382 cells) and P1 (peri-lesional lung; Y40012LA11; 51,834 cells). Each cell was represented as a 39-dimensional input (7-dimensional cell-type composition from cell2location deconvolution against a 146,345-cell peripheral-blood scRNA-seq reference, 30 expression principal components, and 2 spatial coordinates). MuSpec smooths the input at three kNN scales (k = 10/20/30), rasterises each scale onto a ≤ 224² lattice, and passes the three feature maps through four deep-learning modules built on published attention-and-fusion designs — ASFF cross-scale fusion, TripletAttention, ExternalAttention, and a Fourier graph network (FGN) — to produce a 16-dimensional niche embedding; a shared encoder is trained jointly across both slides with an MSE reconstruction loss plus a spatial-smoothing loss, and niches are obtained by KMeans (K = 9). We benchmarked MuSpec against BANKSY at matched numbers of spatial domains, ran a three-seed module ablation and a 34-configuration single-factor hyperparameter sweep, and used the recovered granuloma signature for multi-library signature-reversal drug repurposing (LINCS L1000 chemical perturbations, GEO perturbations, NIBR DRUGseq 2025, and the original CMAP, merged) and AutoDock Vina docking against the host target SP110. Results. MuSpec produced a compact, sub-million-parameter model (782,251 parameters; 93.9% in ASFF) that trains in minutes on a single consumer GPU (≈ 7 GB peak). On every matched-K comparison, MuSpec embeddings separated niches far more sharply than BANKSY (Δsilhouette + 0.31 to + 0.40 on both slides); MuSpec’s own K = 9 silhouette was 0.322 (B1) and 0.285 (P1). Three-seed ablation showed that no module was removable losslessly : removing ExternalAttention lowered niche separation (Δsilhouette − 0.093) but raised robustness and cross-slide transfer (Δ of + 0.137 to + 0.362), identifying a clean separation↔robustness trade-off. For normalisation, a three-seed paired design showed that 7 of 8 robustness metrics changed sign across seeds, so we report no seed-stable difference between global and per-slide normalisation, with only a small stable (+ 0.010 ± 0.003) silhouette advantage to per-slide normalisation on B1. The hyperparameter sweep revealed a monotone separation–robustness frontier with no cliffs, on which the default setting was the robustness optimum (mean noise-robustness ARI 0.758; drop-composition ARI 0.683 on B1 and 0.518 on P1, the highest in the sweep). Joint niche characterisation recovered myeloid/granuloma (SPP1, MMP9, CTSK), airway/club (MUC5B, SCGB1A1, BPIFB1), fibrotic (SFRP2, COL1A1, INHBA) and fibroblast (IL11, TFPI2, PI16) niches, and an SP110–IFN hub analysis. A 324-gene granuloma signature (233 up, 91 down) yielded top signature-reversal hits led by a PPARγ-agonist trio (pioglitazone 90.08, troglitazone, rosiglitazone), and in-silico docking of a focused 6-ligand panel against SP110 gave the strongest affinities for withaferin A (− 7.18 kcal/mol) and nintedanib (− 6.92 kcal/mol). Conclusions. MuSpec provides an unsupervised, reproducible, computationally light route to spatially resolved niche atlases in infectious-disease tissue, and its systematic benchmarking exposes a separation↔robustness trade-off that should be reported rather than hidden. Applied to human TB lung, it recovered biologically coherent, cross-slide-conserved granuloma niches and nominated host-directed repurposing candidates.

llm.novelty_zh: 把已有注意力与融合模块组合成轻量的空间生态位编码器，并用于结核肉芽肿的药物重定位。
llm.summary_zh: MuSpec是一个无监督多尺度空间生态位编码器，应用于两张人肺结核Stereo-seq切片，识别肉芽肿生态位并与BANKSY进行匹配比较。研究还用签名反转在多个扰动库中检索候选药物，并对SP110进行分子对接。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 它为传染病肉芽肿的空间组学分析提供了无监督基线，并把空间生态位与药物重定位联系起来。
llm.limitations_zh: 归一化方式的差异在三个随机种子间不稳定，药物重定位与对接结果依赖计算，摘要未提及湿实验验证。

title: In silico perturbation as an adversarial attack: combinatorial searchover cell states in single-cell foundation models
abstract: Background: Identifying which genes to perturb in order to drive a cell towards a desired state is a common problem in biology, and the answer is often a combination of genes. Single-cell foundation models can predict the effect of forcing a gene on without an experiment, but in silico perturbation has been confined to single genes or to a few hundred enumerated combinations. In token-based models, choosing which genes to force on is formally the same optimization problem as a discrete adversarial attack on a language model. We therefore investigated whether Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), a search developed for such attacks, can be used to find combinations of genes. Results: Our results suggest that GCG is useful for finding combinations of genes. In Geneformer, the effect of a set was well below the sum of the individual effects of its members, which suggests that assembling combinations from single-gene effects is not a promising approach. GCG exceeded forward-selection greedy search at equal cost in two models (Geneformer and scGPT) and at every set size. Against published reprogramming protocols, GCG recovered the reported factors at a rate well above chance and higher than the random-pool and all-gene greedy searches at equal cost, although ranking genes by their individual effect gave a higher recovery rate. Recovery corresponded to whether a search used the embedding gradient, which suggests that the gradient is useful for narrowing the search, whereas stronger optimization of the objective did not raise recovery, which suggests that the similarity induced by the model does not fully reflect the regulatory logic of genes. Conclusions: These results are obtained within the constraints of the foundation models; nevertheless, searching for combinations of factors with foundation models extends in silico perturbation beyond single genes, reveals a property of the induced objective that single-gene evaluation does not, and points to a new direction for using and evaluating the models.

llm.novelty_zh: 将离散对抗攻击搜索算法 GCG 用于在单细胞基础模型中寻找多基因组合扰动。
llm.summary_zh: 作者将 Greedy Coordinate Gradient 用于 Geneformer 与 scGPT 中的基因组合选择，与前向贪心搜索、随机池及全基因贪心搜索在等成本下比较。结果显示 GCG 在两个模型各组合规模下均更优，并能以高于随机的比例召回已发表重编程方案中的因子，但单基因效应排序的召回率更高。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为在基础模型中设计多基因干预提供了可借鉴的搜索方法，有助于缩小实验候选范围。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及模型预测在真实实验中的验证，也未讨论搜索结果在不同细胞状态下的稳定性。

title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
abstract: High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.

llm.novelty_zh: 将JUMP Cell Painting表型证据、基于证据的假设生成、独立批判与人工复核分流组合为多智能体框架。
llm.summary_zh: DISCOVERY-AGENT把JUMP Cell Painting表型谱与基于证据的假设生成相连，并加入独立批判与有界的人工复核分流。初步CRISPR/ORF分析仅在CRISPR平板层面发现4个FDR显著关联，化合物身份基准的AUROC为0.6142。作者强调其结果仅表明可审计证据处理与弱形态信号的可行性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作为基于表型图谱的AI假设生成提供了可审计的流程范式，并明确了独立生物学验证的必要性。
llm.limitations_zh: 形态信号较弱（AUROC 0.6142），ORF基因无显著发现，且尚未完成专家复核与前瞻性安全评估。

title: Exploring Representation-Aware Model Selection for Out-of-Distribution Gene Perturbation Prediction
abstract: Prediction of transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is difficult when the target perturbation is absent from model training. A further challenge is that different predictors can behave differently on different unseen perturbations. This study therefore examines out-ofdistribution (OOD) perturbation prediction as a model-selection problem rather than assuming that one predictor is uniformly optimal. Using an Adamson Perturb-seq dataset containing 65,899 cells, 5,060 genes, and 82 perturbation conditions, we analyze 21 perturbations held out from training. Four candidate predictor configurations are evaluated: GO-only MLP, GenePT-only MLP, GenePT + GO concatenation MLP, and Gated Attention Fusion. For each perturbation, the observed candidate-model performance is used to quantify the opportunity for perturbationspecific selection. The best fixed strategy has mean R 2 =0.399650, while the oracle upper bound is 0.466234, giving an available selection gap of 0.066584. Importantly, the perturbation-level retrospective adaptive values reported in the study average to R 2 =0.421228, corresponding to a 0.021578 absolute and 5.40% observed relative improvement over the fixed strategy. Embedding Coverage is also examined as a compact representation-availability descriptor. In this exploratory analysis, it shows negative Spearman associations with OOD difficulty (ρ =−0.5472, p = 0.0103) and with the observed adaptive improvement (ρ = −0.4741, p = 0.0299), with both p-values treated as nominal exploratory results, whereas the paired Wilcoxon comparison between adaptive and fixed outcomes is not significant (p = 0.0638). These results provide exploratory evidence that representation coverage can be useful for characterizing OOD behavior, but they do not establish universal superiority of adaptive selection. The study is deliberately positioned as a focused single-dataset analysis and identifies the validation required for broader claims.

llm.novelty_zh: 把未见扰动的预测视为模型选择问题，并以嵌入覆盖率刻画表示的可得性。
llm.summary_zh: 研究在 Adamson Perturb-seq 数据集的 21 个留出扰动上比较四种预测器，量化逐扰动选择的空间。自适应选择的平均改进约为 5.4%，配对 Wilcoxon 检验不显著；嵌入覆盖率与 OOD 难度存在名义上的负相关。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提示表示覆盖率可能有助于刻画 OOD 扰动预测行为，为后续验证提供方向。
llm.limitations_zh: 仅基于单一数据集，相关性 p 值为探索性结果，作者也承认不能确立自适应选择的普遍优势。

title: Immune Dynamics of Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Prognostic Implications.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, with 5-year postoperative recurrence rates as high as 70%, severely limiting long-term survival after surgical resection. The success of immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced HCC has driven their expansion into the neoadjuvant setting, where pathological complete response (pCR) has emerged as a potential endpoint associated with improved outcomes, although its validation as a surrogate for overall survival requires further prospective evidence. This review systematically synthesizes current evidence on the immune dynamics underlying pCR following neoadjuvant immunotherapy in HCC. Pooled analyses report pCR rates of approximately 18-24%, while certain intensive regimens, such as dual immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations, have achieved rates up to 41% in selected populations, albeit with increased toxicity. The peripheral infiltration and expansion of high-frequency intratumoral T-cell clonotypes are associated with pathological response, although a causal relationship remains to be established. Baseline tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte density, tertiary lymphoid structures, and dynamic changes in circulating tumor DNA are emerging as promising predictive biomarkers. In pan-tumor analyses, patients achieving pCR demonstrate substantially improved relapse-free survival, with 3-year event-free survival rates ranging from 78.6% to 100%; however, HCC-specific prospective data remain limited. However, heterogeneity in pCR definitions, lack of standardized pathological assessment, and limited long-term follow-up data constrain the definitive qualification of pCR as a surrogate endpoint. Future directions include standardization of pCR assessment, multi-omics integration for improved prediction, biomarker-guided patient selection, and large-scale prospective validation. This review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the immune mechanisms of pCR and its clinical implications, offering guidance for clinicians and researchers in the evolving landscape of neoadjuvant immunotherapy for HCC.
affiliations: Department of General Surgery, Chaoyang City Center Hospital of China Medical University, Chaoyang, Liaoning, People's Republic of China.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述性质，总结肝细胞癌新辅助免疫治疗pCR的免疫动态与生物标志物，无新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述汇总了HCC新辅助免疫治疗中的pCR率，并讨论T细胞克隆扩增、TILs、三级淋巴结构和ctDNA动态等与反应相关的生物标志物。文章同时探讨了pCR作为替代终点的可靠性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为HCC新辅助免疫治疗的疗效评估与患者选择提供了临床证据梳理。
llm.limitations_zh: 综述指出pCR定义不统一、病理评估缺乏标准化，且HCC特异的前瞻性数据有限。

title: Applications of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Bioinformatics and Their Experimental Validation
abstract: A sequence model can identify a base substitution predicted to alter a splice junction, and a cancer model can assign a tumour to a pathway-defined group. Researchers often interpret these outputs as explanations, although each calls for a different experimental test. This narrative review examines how explainable artificial intelligence is used in regulatory genomics, RNA processing, cancer genomics, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, protein science, molecular property prediction and microbial genomics. It compares the biological entity being explained, the reference used to calculate an effect and the evidence available beyond the original model. Base substitutions and matched molecular pairs permit explicit contrasts. Pathway scores, tissue neighbourhoods and internal protein features require additional tests to separate the proposed mechanism from correlated measurements. Recent evaluations of foundation models also show why comparisons with simple predictors and genuinely held-out biological units matter before interpretation. Across applications, the clearest route to experimental follow-up is to specify an expected molecular event, its direction and a result that would challenge the prediction. This approach separates faithful descriptions of model behaviour from claims supported by an independent assay and clarifies what an explanation contributes to the selection of the next experiment.
venue: Research Journal of Life Sciences Bioinformatics Pharmaceutical and Chemical Sciences
published_venue: Research Journal of Life Sciences Bioinformatics Pharmaceutical and Chemical Sciences

llm.novelty_zh: 综述性质，提出以预期分子事件、方向与可证伪结果来设计可解释AI的实验验证。
llm.summary_zh: 该叙述性综述考察可解释AI在调控基因组学、RNA加工、癌症基因组、单细胞空间转录组与蛋白质科学等领域的应用。作者强调应先明确解释对象、参照与可证伪的预期结果，再通过独立实验验证。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 区分模型行为描述与独立实验证据，有助于选择后续实验。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: COMPUTATIONAL AND MACHINE LEARNING APPROACHES FOR SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS: FROM CELLULAR HETEROGENEITY TO BIOLOGICAL DISCOVERY
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed gene expression analysis by revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk tissue measurements. This is particularly relevant to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), where malignant, immune, stromal, and endothelial cells interact within a complex tumor microenvironment. However, the high dimensionality, sparsity, sequencing variability, and batch effects of scRNA-seq data present substantial challenges for reliable biological interpretation. This review examines computational and machine-learning approaches across the scRNA-seq analysis workflow, encompassing quality control, normalization, feature selection, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and cell annotation. Conventional methods, including k-means, hierarchical, and graph-based clustering, are considered alongside advanced approaches such as autoencoders, variational autoencoders, and graph neural networks. Their applications in downstream analyses, including differential expression, pathway enrichment, trajectory inference, and cell-cell communication, are discussed within a LUAD-focused context. The review further evaluates how analytical assumptions, model interpretability, and validation practices influence biological conclusions. Emerging developments in spatial transcriptomics, multimodal integration, and explainable machine learning are also highlighted. The key contribution is an integrated, validation-oriented framework connecting computational outputs with biological interpretation and evidence-supported claims, moving beyond a descriptive catalogue of methods. This perspective emphasizes rigorous method selection and independent validation to strengthen insights into cellular heterogeneity and LUAD biology.
venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
published_venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

llm.novelty_zh: 以验证导向框架梳理scRNA-seq计算方法与生物学结论之间的联系，而非单纯罗列方法。
llm.summary_zh: 综述覆盖scRNA-seq从质控、归一化到细胞注释的分析流程，讨论聚类、自编码器与图神经网络等方法在肺腺癌背景下的应用。文章还强调分析假设、模型可解释性与独立验证对生物学结论的影响。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该综述为肺腺癌单细胞分析的方法选择与结论验证提供了参考框架。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要为综述形式，未提供新的实验或定量基准比较。

title: Circulating tumor cells in solid tumors: biological adaptation, detection technologies, and clinical implications.
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are rare tumor-derived cells released from primary or metastatic lesions into the bloodstream and represent key intermediates in hematogenous dissemination. As intact cellular components of liquid biopsy, CTCs provide opportunities to investigate tumor heterogeneity, metastatic evolution, therapeutic resistance, and dynamic molecular alterations that may not be fully captured by tissue biopsy or circulating cell-free analytes. This review summarizes current advances in the biological mechanisms, detection technologies, and clinical applications of CTCs in solid tumors, with particular emphasis on their adaptive responses within the circulation. CTCs exhibit substantial phenotypic and metabolic plasticity, including epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, altered energy metabolism, and enhanced resistance to oxidative and mechanical stress. Their interactions with platelets, neutrophils, and other immune components can further promote survival, immune evasion, and metastatic competence, particularly through the formation of homotypic and heterotypic CTC clusters. Technological advances in antigen-independent enrichment, microfluidic isolation, single-cell multi-omics, and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis are progressively extending CTC assessment beyond enumeration toward molecular and functional characterization. Emerging clinical evidence supports the potential value of CTCs for prognostic stratification, treatment monitoring, and biomarker assessment in breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, and head and neck cancers, although clinical utility varies considerably among tumor types and platforms. Further standardization and prospective validation, together with integration of metabolic, immune, and multi-omic CTC features, will be essential to establish their role in precision oncology.
affiliations: The First Affiliated Hospital of Henan Medical University, Xinxiang, China.
The First Clinical College of Henan Medical University, Xinxiang, China.
venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
published_venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

llm.novelty_zh: 综述性质，总结循环肿瘤细胞适应性与检测技术的进展，无新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述总结循环肿瘤细胞在上皮间质可塑性、代谢适应以及与血小板和中性粒细胞相互作用中的生物学特征。作者同时回顾微流控、单细胞多组学与AI辅助分析在CTC检测中的进展。

title: Artificial intelligence and multi-omics integration for cardiac regeneration: from cell fate decoding to clinical translation.
abstract: Heart failure remains among the leading causes of death worldwide, and its burden is increasing as populations age. The adult mammalian heart has almost no capacity to replace cardiomyocytes lost to injury: most cardiomyocytes leave the cell cycle, and the infarcted muscle is replaced by scar, so that function declines progressively. This constraint is not fixed. Neonatal mice regenerate myocardium for a brief window that closes within the first postnatal week, whereas adult zebrafish retain the capacity throughout life; the machinery for regeneration therefore exists, but is held in check. Cell-based therapy was expected to circumvent the problem, yet its clinical benefit has remained modest: transplanted cells survive and engraft poorly, their fate resists precise control, and the host microenvironment actively suppresses regeneration. These shortcomings are symptoms of a single underlying difficulty-scale. The regulatory logic of cardiac regeneration is distributed across transcriptional control, intercellular communication, spatial microenvironments and protein interactions, so that no omics layer examined in isolation, however high its resolution, can recover the integrated picture from high-dimensional, sparse and heterogeneous data. This review proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-multi-omics integration framework for cardiac regeneration. We survey the methodological progress that becomes available when single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics and proteomics are modelled jointly, and examine what these approaches can and cannot establish about cardiac lineage cell fate determination, about regeneration trajectory reconstruction, and about the failing-heart microenvironment. We then consider the translational pathways, and the limits of the evidence for each. The resulting evidence is uneven: the sections on the failing-heart microenvironment rest largely on direct cardiac data, whereas most of the methodological progress has been made outside the heart and transfers only under additional assumptions. One qualification is therefore stated at the outset: evidence for AI in cardiac regeneration is still scarce. The review is positioned as a methodological framework and a forward-looking perspective rather than a synthesis of established conclusions, and the evidence supporting each principal claim is graded, from direct experimental evidence in the heart to methodology.

title: Suture stem cells and AI-enabled multi-omics in craniosynostosis: from niche biology to regenerative medicine
abstract: Craniosynostosis, the premature fusion of cranial sutures, affects approximately 1 in 2,100–2,500 live births and remains exclusively treated by surgery, which carries risks of resynostosis, secondary intracranial hypertension, and neurodevelopmental sequelae. Over the past decade, the cranial suture has been redefined from a passive fibrous joint into a dynamic stem cell niche: mesenchymal stem and progenitor populations marked by Gli1, Axin2, and Prrx1 reside within the suture mesenchyme, sustain calvarial bone homeostasis, and are depleted or dysregulated in craniosynostosis. In parallel, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and single-nucleus epigenomics have produced the first high-resolution atlases of suture development in mouse and human, while machine learning and deep learning methods increasingly shape diagnosis, phenotyping, and data integration. This review synthesizes these converging lines of evidence for a pediatric neurosurgery and regenerative medicine audience. We first describe the cellular and molecular architecture of the suture stem cell niche and its disruption in syndromic and nonsyndromic craniosynostosis. We then review how multi-omics technologies—single-cell transcriptomics, spatial profiling, and chromatin accessibility mapping—are resolving suture cell states, developmental trajectories, and niche interactions, and how artificial intelligence (AI) methods, from variational autoencoders and trajectory inference to gene regulatory network and cell–cell communication models, convert these data into mechanistic hypotheses. We next examine translational progress, including stem cell-based suture regeneration, biomaterial niche engineering, and patient-derived iPSC disease models, and discuss how AI-assisted biomarker discovery, potency prediction, and quality control could support future cell-based interventions. Finally, we outline outstanding challenges—model interpretability, cross-species and cross-dataset transferability, data standards, and the experimental validation of AI-derived predictions—that must be addressed to move toward reliable regenerative strategies for craniosynostosis.

title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. We define the Predictive Dermatome as a computationally derived, anatomically localized skin region characterized by a shared or probabilistically related biological aging state and trajectory inferred from integrated molecular, structural, imaging, clinical, and exposomic data. Unlike a conventional neurological dermatome, which denotes a cutaneous territory associated predominantly with sensory innervation from a spinal nerve root, the Predictive Dermatome is not defined by nerve distribution. The proposed framework integrates spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, single-cell or single-nucleus reference maps, optical coherence tomography, confocal or ultrasound imaging, histology when available, tape-strip biomarkers, extracellular matrix and glycation-related measurements, and exposomic data streams. We describe the learning task, input-output structure, spatial graph construction, modality-specific encoders, transformer-based token fusion, training objectives, regularization strategies, and missing-modality handling. Rather than requiring spatial omics or tissue sampling for every clinical patient, the framework uses transcriptomic, proteomic, histologic, and extracellular matrix measurements as discovery and validation layers from which clinically deployable surrogate models could be trained using non-invasive and minimally invasive inputs. We also outline preprocessing steps for high-dimensional spatial transcriptomic data, cross-modal image-omics registration, validation stages, uncertainty estimation, and ethical safeguards including privacy-preserving learning and bias auditing across skin phototypes. The Predictive Dermatome should therefore be viewed as a staged research architecture for precision dermatology, not as a currently validated clinical decision system. Its value lies in defining how molecular geography, imaging, and environmental exposure may eventually converge to support localized risk stratification, longitudinal monitoring, and biologically guided intervention in skin aging and regenerative dermatology.

title: The ovarian cellular ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome: from cellular heterogeneity to clinical relevance
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most biologically heterogeneous disorders in reproductive endocrinology, extending far beyond the classical features of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory mechanisms associated with PCOS, these processes have largely been investigated independently, and their contribution to the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of the disorder remains incompletely understood. Recent advances in cellular-resolution biology, including single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial omics, and multimodal molecular profiling, together with computational systems biology, enable increasingly detailed characterization of cellular states, spatial organization, and molecular relationships within the ovarian-follicular environment. In this Review, we use the ovarian cellular ecosystem as an operational systems framework to test whether PCOS-associated abnormalities observed in individual ovarian and follicular compartments form reproducible higher-order patterns of multicellular organization. The framework is organized across five measurable domains: cellular composition and states, intercellular signaling relationships, spatial niche organization, cross-compartment molecular coupling, and systemic-ovarian coupling. Current direct human cellular-resolution evidence remains sparse and compartment-specific. Available studies support altered molecular and cellular states within selected ovarian and follicular compartments more strongly than coordinated, spatially organized, or progressive ecosystem-wide remodeling. We critically evaluate how cellular-resolution, spatial, multi-omics, computational and artificial intelligence approaches can be used to test these ecosystem-level hypotheses, explicitly distinguishing direct measurement from computational inference and identifying the validation required for functional or causal interpretation. Finally, we discuss the translational implications of this framework for biologically informed patient stratification, ecosystem-derived biomarker discovery, mechanism-informed therapeutic development, and precision reproductive endocrinology. By integrating current evidence within a falsifiable framework, this Review defines measurable features and validation criteria for testing ovarian ecosystem organization in PCOS and identifies the critical evidence gaps that future cellular-resolution, spatial, and multi-omic studies must address. This provides a practical roadmap for determining whether reproducible ovarian ecosystem states can improve biological stratification, biomarker discovery, or therapeutic target identification beyond compartment-specific abnormalities and established systemic and clinical determinants.

title: Radiomics- based biomarkers for immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer: advances, challenges, and future perspectives in biological interpretation and clinical translation.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet treatment benefit remains heterogeneous and resistance is common. Genomic alterations, tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming across spatial and temporal scales that are incompletely captured by single-site tissue sampling. Radiomics extracts quantitative features from routine images and offers a framework for investigating macroscopic correlates of these processes. This narrative review critically examines computed tomography (CT) and fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT (¹ 8 F-FDG PET/CT) radiomics in relation to oncogenic alterations, immune and stromal phenotypes, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, tumor mutational burden, and metabolic-immune interactions in NSCLC. It should be highlighted that such observed statistical links only generate plausible biological hypotheses and do not constitute experimental proof of true mechanistic relationships. Rather than merely summarizing predictive model performance, we emphasize evidence boundaries and interpretive caveats for radiomic-TME associations. We further elaborate on key translational bottlenecks including limited reproducibility, technical standardization deficits, and retrospective-model overfitting. We discuss ongoing efforts toward cross-scale multi-omics integration, alongside the promises and inherent limitations of explainable artificial intelligence and federated learning for clinical translation. To move beyond purely predictive tools toward mechanism-aware decision-support systems, future radiomic research requires prospective multicenter validation, rigorous data harmonization, and combined analyses integrating spatial transcriptomics, digital pathology, and circulating biomarkers for precision immuno-oncology.

title: High-risk pancreatic cancer pathology reveals a B3GNT3-associated glycosylation program.
abstract: Objective Pancreatic cancer has a poor prognosis and marked heterogeneity, whereas existing pathomics models generally lack biological interpretability. We aimed to construct the pathomics prognostic score GlyPath-Risk and explore the molecular states associated with the high-risk phenotype captured by the score. Methods We integrated H&E whole-slide images from TCGA-PAAD and Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (FMUUH), extracted handcrafted and deep-learning features using CellProfiler and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, and constructed GlyPath-Risk using a combined LASSO and random survival forest model. Prognostic performance was evaluated in training, internal validation, and FMUUH cohorts. Correlation analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and xCell immune-infiltration estimation were used to investigate associations among GlyPath-Risk, the glycosylation transcriptional program, and the tumor microenvironment. Single-cell transcriptomics, CellChat cell-cell communication analysis, Geneformer virtual perturbation, and B3GNT3 knockdown experiments were used to generate and evaluate candidate biological hypotheses. Results GlyPath-Risk comprised six pathological features and showed C-indices of 0.88, 0.68, and 0.83 in the training, internal validation, and FMUUH cohorts, respectively. Its association with overall survival remained after adjustment for age, sex, and clinical stage in the reported Cox model (multivariable HR = 1.230). The glycosylation gene set showed the strongest mean absolute correlation with pathological features among 20 post-translational modification classes. WGCNA identified six co-expression modules significantly associated with GlyPath-Risk (BH-FDR Conclusion GlyPath-Risk showed prognostic associations across the evaluated cohorts. The score was associated with a B3GNT3-related glycosylation transcriptional program and may be related to immune- and vascular-related transcriptomic features. These findings provide a testable framework for investigating the biological correlates of pathomics scores and nominate B3GNT3 as a candidate molecular anchor requiring independent validation.
