title: Episode calibrated thermal residual monitoring for battery fast charging protection
abstract: Temperature-sensor faults can delay protective current reduction during battery fast charging, while unnecessary alarms reduce charge delivery. This study evaluates whole-episode calibration of thermal residual monitors in a reproducible Python simulation. A two-node virtual cell represents a 50 A h battery during a 1200s charging opportunity. Training, calibration, and testing use separate virtual cells. Raw, mean-centered, linear, and quadratic predictors are compared with an identified physical model, repeated calibration draws, alternative fallback policies, and independent parameter shifts. In the original nominal test, quadratic correction achieved a healthy filtered residual root mean square error of 0.396 °C. An identified physical predictor achieved 0.441 °C, with a gradual-bias detection delay of 73.61 s compared with 67.44 s for the original quadratic monitor. Across 20 independent training and calibration repetitions, quadratic healthy-episode alarms averaged 4.84% and ranged from 3.00% to 7.50%. Under simultaneous negative sensor bias and cooling loss, a prediction-independent 75 A fallback increased mean delivered charge from 22.960 to 33.049 A h relative to a 25 A cap, with zero observed 45 °C exceedances in both 400-cell comparisons. Under the combined parameter shift, recalibration reduced the healthy-episode false-alarm rate from 100% (400/400) to 4.75% (19/400). After recalibration, only 22.25% (89/400) of gradual negative-bias episodes were detected after fault onset. A separate public-data check used ten measured 1C charging records from one 2.9 A h cell. The two-node predictor achieved a surface-temperature root mean square error of 0.293 °C on five held-out records, without resolving a distinct fast internal thermal mode. The results favor adequate physical calibration and joint assessment of detection, intervention cost, and calibration transfer. High-rate closed-loop protection remains supported by simulation.

title: Multi-omics integration for precision tuberculosis medicine: from molecular atlases to clinical translation.
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health threat. Its management is constrained by incomplete prediction of antimicrobial resistance, limited ability to identify patients at risk of anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (AT-DILI), and heterogeneous treatment responses. This narrative review examines how multi-omics can address these challenges and adapts an established translational framework to TB-specific decisions. Clinically useful integration requires reproducible measurements, independent validation, and evidence that a result improves care. The relevant phenotypes emerge from interactions among Mycobacterium tuberculosis , host genetic and immune variation, lesion microenvironments, drug exposure, and microbial ecology. No single molecular layer adequately resolves this system. We examine pathogen and host genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome profiling, and single-cell and spatial technologies. We distinguish replicated resistance and NAT2-associated toxicity findings from emerging bacterial regulatory, immunometabolic, and microbiome associations. Selected diagnostic, prognostic, treatment-monitoring, and toxicity classifiers illustrate both the promise of integration and limitations in sample size, comparator selection, confounding, and validation. Their high training discrimination does not establish external performance or clinical utility. The framework links standardized biobanking and fit-for-purpose integration to analytical and clinical validation, functional testing, and evaluation of utility and equitable implementation. Explicit transition criteria distinguish these stages without treating proposed planning thresholds as universal standards. The clinical value of multi-omics will depend less on the number of measured features than on rigorous study design, affordability, and demonstrable benefit to patients.

title: A deep-learning microglial response score integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics for Alzheimer's disease stratification.
abstract: Background Microglia exhibit diverse responses in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet linking these responses to tissue pathology and disease heterogeneity remains challenging. We aimed to develop a deep-learning microglial response score (DL-MRS) integrating single-cell, spatial and bulk transcriptomics to characterize AD-associated transcriptional patterns. Methods We analyzed human single-cell, spatial and bulk transcriptomic data to characterize microglial clearance and inflammatory programs. These programs and tissue-context features formed eight module-level inputs to a multilayer perceptron that generated DL-MRS. Model performance and feature contributions were assessed using five repeats of five-fold cross-validation, cross-cohort testing, feature-set comparisons and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Spatial localization, individual-level prediction using spatial transcriptomic data, and molecular heterogeneity within AD were also examined. Results Single-cell analyses characterized clearance-enriched and inflammation-enriched microglial groups. Descriptive spatial projection visualized regional variation in the weighted microglial and tissue-context programs. Across 697 AD and control bulk samples, DL-MRS achieved a repeated out-of-fold area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.939 and a mean cross-cohort transfer AUC of 0.947. SHAP analysis of the expanded model identified complement as the largest contributor, alongside contributions from microglial and tissue-context modules. Among 129 AD samples, median DL-MRS was higher in the immune-enriched than in the neuronal/synaptic-enriched molecular group (0.970 versus 0.800). These findings support DL-MRS as an interpretable research tool for integrating microglial and tissue-context signals to characterize AD-associated transcriptional patterns and within-disease molecular heterogeneity. Conclusion DL-MRS integrates microglial and tissue-context signals into an interpretable measure of AD-associated transcriptional remodeling. By capturing coordinated variation across immune, glial, vascular, neuronal and synaptic programs, DL-MRS reveals molecular heterogeneity among AD samples and provides a framework for investigating interindividual differences and advancing molecular stratification in AD research.

title: AI and multiomics in stem cell-based repair after ischemic stroke: current evidence and validation priorities
abstract: AI and multiomics can describe therapeutic cell and extracellular-vesicle (EV) products and the postischemic environment, but a molecular signature matters only if it changes a defined development or treatment decision. Existing reviews address stroke single-cell and spatial biology, AI in stem-cell multiomics, or AI-enabled regenerative engineering. This critical narrative review connects those topics through three decisions: whether a finished product has reproducible activity, which host conditions permit that activity, and whether a patient gains benefit attributable to treatment. We compare integration methods by their assumptions for paired, unpaired and mosaic data; distinguish Geneformer, scGPT, scFoundation and universal cell embeddings by input encoding and learning objective; and examine why larger pretraining has not produced consistent gains over simpler baselines. A worked EV-potency task specifies candidate functional labels, independent training units, controls and external validation. Representative stroke studies are mapped from molecular description through experimentally tested mechanisms to prediction of unseen product lots and controlled clinical benefit. The reviewed stroke and adjacent cerebrovascular literature includes AI-assisted molecular prioritization, computational graft-host analysis and automated behavior quantification, but does not establish an externally validated AI predictor of finished-product potency or treatment-attributable patient benefit. Cross-scale virtual-cell and heterogeneous protein representations offer transferable methods, not validated ischemic-repair models. The framework identifies the experiments needed to turn molecular associations into decisions with measurable biological value.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述卒中干细胞治疗中 AI 与多组学的应用，提出产品效力与临床获益的验证框架，未给出经外部验证的模型。

title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell-cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
abstract: Objective To summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues. Methods This narrative review synthesizes findings from studies identified primarily through PubMed searches supplemented by manual curation of reference lists. Search terms included "single-cell," "spatial transcriptomics," "MASLD," "NAFLD," "NASH," "MASH," "steatohepatitis," and "liver fibrosis." Studies applying single-cell transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell eQTL analysis, and integrative multi-omics approaches were included. The last literature search was conducted in July 2026. Results: Single-cell technologies have revealed key cellular alterations during MASLD progression, including disrupted hepatocyte metabolic zonation, heterogeneous activation states of hepatic stellate cells, macrophage functional reprogramming, immune cell dysfunction, and dynamic remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment. Spatial transcriptomics has further resolved the spatial organization of these cellular changes, whereas single-cell eQTL analyses have linked genetic susceptibility loci to cell-specific regulatory programs. Single-cell profiling of intestinal, adipose, and vascular tissues has expanded the understanding of extrahepatic contributions and gut-liver communication in MASLD. These advances provide a foundation for drug target identification, mechanistic understanding of current and investigational therapies, and assessment of treatment response at cellular resolution. Conclusion Single-cell multi-omics is transforming MASLD research from tissue-level characterization toward cellular-resolution understanding, providing novel insights into disease stratification, therapeutic target discovery, and biomarker development, and advancing precision hepatology.
affiliations: Dongzhimen Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, Beijing, China.
Institute of Liver Diseases, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, Beijing, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述性工作，无新方法或新数据。

title: TwAIns: how artificial intelligence transforms biological digital twins from cell to population, and why validation is the limiting factor
abstract: Artificial intelligence has changed what a biological model can be. The digital twin, a computational replica kept in step with its living original through continuous data assimilation, is now being built at every level of biological organization, from the single cell to the whole population. I argue that deep learning, transformer architectures, physics-informed neural networks, generative models, and the first biological foundation models have moved the twin from a static system of differential equations toward an adaptive, human-relevant instrument, and that this shift is the most promising route yet to replace animal experiments with New Approach Methodologies. I trace five nested scales: the cellular AI Virtual Cell, the in vitro process and organoid twin, the physics-informed organ twin, the individual Virtual Human Twin of precision medicine, and the population twin of the Exposome and virtual control groups. At each level, I ask what the twin genuinely replaces today and what remains aspiration, resisting the temptation to sell a lifetime replica of a human that no one has yet built. The twin will not earn scientific and regulatory trust on cleverness alone. It needs next-generation validation, agreed credibility standards, and lifecycle governance. That, and not more computing, is the work ahead.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出从单细胞到群体的五层嵌套数字孪生框架，并强调验证是限制AI虚拟细胞发展的关键瓶颈。
llm.summary_zh: 文章以观点形式论述深度学习、Transformer、物理信息神经网络与生成模型如何推动数字孪生发展。作者按五个嵌套尺度梳理，包括AI虚拟细胞、器官芯片孪生、器官级孪生、个体虚拟人及暴露组层面的群体孪生。

title: A Testable Framework for Mechanics-Conditioned Perturbation Models in Drug Discovery.
abstract: Perturbation-predictive cell models are advancing quickly, yet they remain predominantly molecular, even though the mechanical state of cells and tissues-stiffness, viscoelasticity, geometry, and force generation-can alter therapeutic response. This review converts that observation into a testable program. It separates four claims that are routinely conflated and gives each its own baseline, estimand, design, and named refutation condition: whether auxiliary mechanical measurements improve prediction of treatment response beyond a complete non-mechanical baseline (H1); whether mechanics computed from images help as a representation rather than as added information (H2); whether experimentally controlled mechanical context modifies treatment effects, including once local drug exposure is held comparable (H3 and H3a); and whether mechanics-aware predictions improve preclinical prioritization decisions under a fixed budget (H4). Current evidence is graded against an explicit, reproducible rubric, and the two links the framework actually requires, mechanical conditioning of perturbation response and prospectively validated mechanics-aware decisions, are unpopulated. A worked pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma program specifies donors, materials, gemcitabine exposure measurement, endpoints, simulation-based power, staged costs, and a blinded decision test, with a reduced-scope minimum implementation for groups that cannot execute the full design. The practical contribution for a bioengineering readership is a transferable specification checklist, covering measurement provenance, units of assignment and inference, leakage control, effect margins, and decision rules, to be completed before resources are committed. We conclude that mechanics should enter perturbation models as a hypothesis carrying a refutation condition, not as a default enrichment. Explicit limitations bound the work: the synthesis is targeted rather than systematic, the evidence grades were assigned by a single assessor, and the framework has not itself been executed.

title: From Brain Rhythms to Network Dynamics: Fractal Measures, Criticality and Biomedical Perspectives
abstract: Neural oscillations, temporal scaling and time-series fractal dimension describe different properties of brain activity. Criticality offers a candidate explanation for relationships among some of these properties, but their co-occurrence does not identify a shared mechanism. This narrative review asks which relationships have been measured in the same preparation, which dynamical transitions could account for them, and what additional evidence is needed for biomedical applications. We compare human and animal observations with computational models, distinguishing oscillatory amplitude-envelope correlations from broadband spectral scaling and graph-dimension estimates. Selected models jointly reproduce oscillations and avalanche statistics, and some connect these observations to amplitude correlations or functional responses. However, these findings do not establish a universal relationship between oscillations, fractal dimension and criticality; stochastic and non-critical mechanisms reproduce important signatures. The synthesis provides a study-level evidence comparison, a model-specific comparison of control parameters and perturbation predictions, and a staged validation pathway for monitoring and adaptive neuromodulation. A TMS example illustrates how short-window features could inform stimulation timing while longer-range scaling requires longer observation periods. The central test is whether joint measurements predict independent neural or functional outcomes better than individual features and competing models. No new experimental dataset, trained architecture or clinical controller is introduced.
affiliations: Institute of Cognitive Sciences and Technologies

title: Beyond Structural Classification: A 4S+G Functional Framework for Non-Coding RNA Biology in Cancer and Its Therapeutic Implications.
abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) regulate gene expression at multiple levels in cancer, yet their functional plasticity and the slow pace of clinical translation remain incompletely explained. This review is organized around a unifying theme: ncRNAs act as integrative nodes connecting the epigenetic, transcriptional, signaling, and metabolic regulatory layers. Building on the established signal, sponge, scaffold, and guide archetypes of long non-coding RNA function, we extend this schema into a 4S+G model that adds a splice-regulatory archetype and embeds all five modes in a three-axis taxonomy spanning structural topology, subcellular localization, and molecular mode of operation, thereby capturing context-dependent functions that binary structural categories cannot accommodate. We dissect chromatin remodeling dynamics, evaluate the competing endogenous RNA hypothesis against stoichiometric evidence, and trace metabolic-epigenetic feedback circuits that stabilize malignant states. We then critically appraise the clinical record of ncRNA therapeutics, from the termination of MRX34 to the modest efficacy of subsequent candidates, and analyze the delivery, immunogenicity, and biomarker barriers that distinguish oncology from other indications for RNA drugs. Emerging solutions, including ligand-directed extrahepatic delivery, spatial transcriptomics, and deep learning-based target prediction, are assessed against these bottlenecks. The 4S+G framework links mechanistic understanding to a realistic roadmap for developing ncRNA-targeted cancer therapeutics with favorable risk-benefit profiles.

title: Single-Cell Dissection of Sarcopenia and Aging in Human Skeletal Muscle Reveals Heterogeneous Mechanisms via Deep Transfer Learning.
abstract: Background: Sarcopenia is characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, yet conventional bulk RNA sequencing approaches cannot resolve the cellular heterogeneity underlying the transition from physiological aging to pathological muscle decline. Methods : This study employed Diagnostic Evidence GAuge of Single cells (DEGAS), a deep transfer learning framework, to integrate bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data and transfer donor-level clinical information to individual skeletal muscle cells. Sarcopenia- and age-associated scores were assigned to individual cells, followed by differential expression, pathway enrichment, cis-Mendelian randomization (cis-MR), and in silico perturbation analyses. Results : DEGAS revealed marked transcriptional heterogeneity among skeletal muscle cells. Compared with bulk RNA-seq, which identified only four differentially expressed genes, DEGAS identified 134 genes between high- and low-sarcopenia-score cells, showing enhanced cytoplasmic translation (fold enrichment [FE] = 29.85, p p = 0.02) and muscle adaptation programs. Within high-sarcopenia-score cells, aging was associated with 484 differentially expressed genes, characterized by increased translational programs (FE = 31.97, p p p Conclusions : This study demonstrates that sarcopenia comprises heterogeneous cellular states driven by distinct mechanisms, including metabolic failure, microenvironmental deterioration, and impaired adaptive muscle function. Integrating genetic evidence with perturbation analysis identifies RPS2 as a potential regulatory node in sarcopenia-associated muscle states.

title: Digital Twins in Oncology: Current Evidence, Multiscale Modeling Approaches, and Challenges in Clinical Translation—A Narrative Review
abstract: Digital Twin (DT), a dynamic simulation technology derived from the engineering field, has been deeply integrated into the field of tumor precision medicine, empowered by both multi-omics technologies and artificial intelligence. It offers a novel approach to overcoming the limitations of traditional paradigms in tumor research, diagnosis, and treatment. This article reviews the full-scale application system of tumor DT, spanning from the molecular to the individual level, and constructs a progressive simulation architecture of "virtual cell-virtual knockout/virtual overexpression-virtual organoid-virtual patient". The virtual cell enables the in silico representation of tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment, serving as the fundamental unit for dissecting molecular mechanisms. Virtual knockout/overexpression provides non-invasive, high-throughput methods for target prioritization, significantly shortening research and development cycles. The virtual organoid achieves computational reconstruction of the three-dimensional (3D) tumor microenvironment, bridging the gap between single-cell and individual-scale simulations. The virtual patient, in turn, supports personalized therapeutic decision-making and virtual clinical trials. By synthesizing the latest research findings in the field, this article delineates the technical pathways, primary modeling tools, and representative empirical cases for each application tier. It further provides an in-depth analysis of core challenges, including multi-source data heterogeneity, insufficient model accuracy and interpretability, and obstacles to clinical translation. Corresponding solutions, such as data standardization, cross-scale technology integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration between medicine and engineering, are proposed. The aim is to provide a comprehensive reference for leveraging DT to advance tumor research and facilitate its translation into clinical practice.
affiliations: The Institute of Applied Lithotripsy, Peking University, Beijing 100044, China.
Department of Urology, Peking University People's Hospital, Beijing 100044, China.

llm.summary_zh: 综述从分子到个体层面梳理肿瘤数字孪生的应用体系，并构建了四层递进的模拟架构。文章讨论了虚拟细胞与虚拟敲除/过表达在靶点优先排序中的作用，并分析了数据异质性、模型可解释性与临床转化等挑战。

title: Imaging Tumor Plasticity Across Space and Time: From Cell State to Metastatic Dissemination.
abstract: Cancer cell plasticity-the capacity of tumor cells to alter phenotypic and functional states under microenvironmental and therapeutic pressure-contributes to invasion, metastasis, and therapy resistance, but is poorly captured by endpoint assays. This review asks which manifestations of plasticity current imaging and spatially resolved technologies can detect, and which conclusions their signals support. We critically reviewed studies using fluorescent and bioluminescent reporters, intravital microscopy, tissue clearing and light-sheet microscopy, spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed imaging, MRI, PET, liquid biopsy, and computational image analysis, prioritizing work that combined imaging with lineage tracing, functional perturbation, or clinical outcomes, and compared approaches using a state-space-time-causality-translation framework. Each approach resolves a defined cellular state, spatial scale, and temporal window. Reporters and intravital microscopy capture cellular dynamics but remain largely preclinical; spatial profiling provides molecularly rich snapshots without temporal history; MRI, PET, and liquid biopsy are clinically accessible but indirect. Lineage-tracing studies show that observed phenotypes must be distinguished from demonstrated state transitions, and few imaging-derived signals have been validated as biomarkers of plasticity. Integrating longitudinal imaging with spatial profiling, lineage tracing, and targeted perturbation is required to separate correlates of metastasis and therapy resistance from causal drivers and to develop clinically validated biomarkers.
affiliations: Department of Molecular Biology, Faculty of Medical Sciences in Katowice, Medical University of Silesia, 18 Medyków Street, 40-752 Katowice, Poland.
Students' Scientific Society, Medical University of Silesia, 40-752 Katowice, Poland.

llm.summary_zh: 综述评估了荧光与生物发光报告、活体显微、光片成像、空间转录组、MRI、PET与液体活检等技术检测肿瘤细胞可塑性的能力。文章指出多数成像信号尚未被验证为可塑性生物标志物，需结合谱系追踪与扰动实验加以确认。

title: From Genomes to Function: Bioinformatics and Multi-Omics Approaches to Insect Chemosensory Receptors.
abstract: Insect chemosensory receptors are essential for detecting environmental chemical cues that influence insect survival and behavior. Advances in genome and transcriptome sequencing have expanded the identification of olfactory receptors (ORs), gustatory receptors (GRs), and ionotropic receptors (IRs), while also providing new opportunities to investigate their expression, evolution, and function. Nevertheless, the functions of many identified receptors remain unknown. This review summarizes recent methods and findings in insect chemosensory receptor research, covering receptor identification and annotation using genomic and transcriptomic data, cell-specific expression analysis using single-cell and single-nucleus sequencing, and evolutionary analysis based on comparative genomics and phylogenetics. We also discuss structural studies of OR-Orco complexes and GRs, computational approaches to receptor-ligand prediction, including structure modeling, molecular docking, and machine learning, and experimental methods for functional characterization. Finally, we discuss how multi-omics integration can combine complementary data layers, such as transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility data, to improve the identification and interpretation of insect chemosensory receptors. By examining how these approaches complement one another, we highlight current progress and outstanding challenges in linking receptor sequences to ligand recognition and biological function.

title: scLAP: A Liver-Adapted Contrastive Shared-Latent Framework for Pseudo-Pairing Single-Cell Transcriptomes and Chromatin Accessibility Profiles.
abstract: Matched single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (scATAC-seq) profiles from the same cells remain limited in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), hindering cell-resolved integration of transcriptional programs and regulatory chromatin states. To address this challenge, we developed single-cell Liver-adapted Alignment and Pseudo-pairing (scLAP), a liver-adapted contrastive shared-latent framework for cross-study RNA-ATAC pseudo-pairing. scLAP was trained on a paired liver single-nucleus multiome reference using 2000 highly variable RNA features and 697 ATAC features, including 647 transcription factor motif activity scores and 50 latent semantic indexing components. On a prespecified cell-level test partition ( n = 3235), scLAP achieved an ATAC-to-RNA Top 10 exact-pair retrieval rate of 21.48% and a mean fraction of samples closer than the true match (FOSCTTM) of 0.0431. In six leave-one-sample-out folds, the corresponding macro means were 5.23% and 0.2278, respectively, indicating above-random ranking but limited exact-pair transfer to unseen samples. A validation-selected scButterfly configuration using 20,000 native ATAC peaks achieved 8.93% Top 10 retrieval and a mean FOSCTTM of 0.0811 on the same test cells; comparisons with Con-AAE and scMODAL remained study-specific adaptations. Applying reciprocal retrieval, a validation-derived cosine-similarity threshold, and greedy one-to-one assignment to independent HCC datasets yielded 4007 similarity-filtered candidate RNA-ATAC pseudo-pairs. Downstream analyses identified an NRCAM-associated accessibility candidate and separate exploratory MET-, CAV1-, and AP-1-associated observations.

title: Construction and Application of Testicular Organoid Models in Multi-Omics-Driven Male Reproductive Toxicity Assessment: A Review.
abstract: Conventional male reproductive toxicity testing relies on rodent bioassays and two-dimensional cultures, which are limited by species extrapolation, low throughput, and weak mechanistic resolution. Testicular and seminiferous-tubule organoids partially restore the Sertoli-Leydig-peritubular myoid niche and permit serial, non-terminal sampling, making them compatible with multi-omics profiling in a way earlier models were not. This review examines the field across four layers: the biological hierarchy and regulatory pathways that constrain model design; organoid construction strategies together with computational simulation of morphogenesis and mass transport; multi-omics integration algorithms and toxicity feature extraction; and retrospective validation on publicly deposited datasets. We compare cell sourcing, scaffold, and culture configuration routes against tubule formation and meiotic completion, derive critical-radius and shear-stress criteria governing construct viability, and evaluate similarity network fusion, latent factor decomposition, joint matrix factorization, and graph neural network approaches. Retrospective modeling indicates that adding epigenomic input to transcriptomic features yields the largest performance gain, that gradient-boosted trees outperform deep networks at current sample sizes, and that attribution profiles align with established mechanisms. We contribute an integration framework dimensioned for testicular organoid data, a fully open-source reproducible pipeline, and an explicit mapping between quantitative organoid descriptors and toxicity endpoints. Persistent obstacles include incomplete structural reconstitution biasing omics signal, sparse and inconsistently annotated public data, simulation parameter uncertainty, and unverified cross-species transfer. Minimum reporting standards, a shared characterization vocabulary, and an open benchmark platform are proposed as prerequisites for regulatory uptake.
affiliations: School of Life Science and Technology, Shandong Second Medical University, Weifang 261053, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述中提出面向睾丸类器官的多组学整合框架，并给出开源可复现的分析流程。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述讨论了睾丸与生精小管类器官在男性生殖毒性评估中的构建策略、计算模拟和多组学整合算法。回顾性分析显示，加入表观基因组信息可提升性能，且梯度提升树在当前样本量下优于深度网络。

title: Proteomic Landscapes of Aging and Disease: Multi-Omics Integration, Machine Learning, and Translational Opportunities.
abstract: Aging is accompanied by progressive changes in molecular, cellular, and systemic homeostasis. At the protein level, these changes involve altered proteostasis, post-translational regulation, and protein interaction networks, but their direction and functional significance vary by tissue, age, and disease context. Mass spectrometry, affinity-based assays, spatial proteomics, and emerging single-cell methods now support complementary views of proteins across tissues, biofluids, and cell populations. Integrating proteomics with genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and metabolomic data can identify regulatory relationships that are not resolved by a single molecular layer; such integration prioritizes mechanisms but does not by itself establish causality. Machine-learning methods support spectral prediction, multi-omics integration, and prediction from high-dimensional protein profiles, although their performance depends on study design, calibration, and independent validation. This narrative review synthesizes protein alterations associated with aging and major age-related diseases, describes what multi-omics and computational methods add, compares emerging measurement technologies, and evaluates biomarker and therapeutic opportunities. Chronological-age prediction, estimation of biological aging, and prediction of clinical outcomes are treated as distinct objectives. Current evidence supports discovery and candidate prioritization; prospective clinical utility and causal therapeutic benefit remain to be established.

title: FViT: A Foundation-Tokenized Vision Transformer with Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Scale Ensembling for Deep Learning-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathology.
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue morphology but is too costly for routine clinical use, motivating prediction of expression from hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) images. FViT (Foundation-tokenized Vision Transformer) tokenizes a spot and its k nearest neighbours with the frozen foundation model Phikon, fuses the tokens with a small trainable Transformer with a relative-position embedding, predicts expression directly and by k -nearest-neighbour retrieval of measured training expression, and combines three neighbourhood sizes ( k = 8, 16, 24) in a weighted ensemble. We evaluated FViT on two public cohorts, Her2ST (HER2-positive breast cancer, eight patients) and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC, four patients), with leave-one-patient-out validation in which the gene panel, the retrieval parameters and the ensemble weights are selected without the evaluated patient. The ensemble reached a Pearson correlation of 0.180 (Her2ST) and 0.213 (cSCC) on the 50 most highly expressed genes (HEGs), but only 0.067 and 0.059 over all 1000 panel genes. Controls showed that neighbourhood fusion with relative position raised the HEG of direct prediction by +0.038 (Her2ST) and +0.045 (cSCC) over a centre-only model, that retrieval changed it by +0.002 to +0.004 on Her2ST and +0.007 to +0.010 on cSCC, and that the multi-scale ensemble differed from an ensemble of three seeds of a single neighbourhood size by -0.003 to +0.008. Under the same folds and panels, the released mclSTExp model (one seed, released settings) reached 0.141 and 0.177. In a section-level protocol, 99% of the retrieved weight came from other sections of the query's own patient, and the ensemble's retrieval gain fell from +0.013 to -0.002 when these sections were masked. Published results use section-level protocols and other gene panels, so they are not directly comparable. With eight and four patients, the findings are exploratory.

title: Systems Biology and Network Modeling of Lipid Metabolism in <i>Brassica juncea</i>: A Roadmap for Precision Oil Engineering.
abstract: Brassica juncea (Indian mustard) is an economically important oilseed crop, but high erucic acid in traditional seed oils and elevated glucosinolates in seed meal remain important quality-improvement targets. Its allotetraploid genome, developmental regulation, and environmental responses complicate the prediction and engineering of lipid-related traits. This narrative review synthesizes experimentally supported findings on fatty acid biosynthesis, triacylglycerol assembly, and genetic regulation in B. juncea , and distinguishes these findings from evidence transferred from Arabidopsis thaliana , Brassica napus , and soybean. We examine available genomic and multi-omics resources, gene co-expression and regulatory network inference, constraint-based metabolic modeling, and strategies for combining these approaches with genome editing and genomic prediction. Although individual lipid-associated genes and seed traits have been characterized, a comprehensively validated, seed-specific, genome-scale lipid metabolic model for B. juncea remains unavailable. We therefore propose a staged roadmap encompassing developmental multi-omics sampling, homoeolog-aware network reconstruction, model calibration, independent validation, targeted perturbation, and multi-environment field testing. This evidence-led framework could help prioritize robust targets for improving fatty acid composition and seed oil performance without assuming that computationally inferred interactions are experimentally established.

title: Machine Learning-Guided Design of Peptide-Targeted CRISPR Vectors for Tissue-Specific Non-Coding RNA Knockdown.
abstract: CRISPR-based genome/epigenome editing and RNA-targeted therapeutics offer unprecedented precision for correcting disease-causing mutations, yet clinical translation remains constrained by two unresolved bottlenecks: suboptimal guide RNA (gRNA) design limiting editing efficiency and specificity, and the absence of safe, tissue-selective delivery platforms. While machine learning (ML)-driven gRNA design and peptide-mediated delivery have each advanced substantially in isolation, to our knowledge, no existing framework jointly optimizes predictive guide-design models and delivery-vector design within a single pipeline a disconnect that likely underlies persistent efficacy-safety trade-offs in clinical translation. This review addresses that gap by critically synthesizing ML-driven guide design and peptide-engineered delivery within a single mechanistic and computational framework. We first outline the structural basis of peptide-derived vectors, emphasizing how charge, hydrophobicity, secondary structure, and receptor-targeting functionalization govern organ- and cell-type specificity. We then critically appraise ML methods for predicting on-target activity, off-target propensity, and specificity across CRISPR platforms, alongside computational approaches for non-coding RNA target identification, focusing on training-data limitations, feature representation, and cross-platform generalizability that constrain predictive reliability. We synthesize design principles for tissue-specific delivery, including nanocarrier integration, and highlight preclinical cases where ML-guided peptide engineering enabled targeted delivery of mRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, and CRISPR ribonucleoproteins. Finally, we assess persistent barriers data sparsity, limited model transferability, off-target genotoxicity, immunogenicity, and delivery constraints and propose emerging directions: multi-omics integration, AI-enabled de novo peptide design, and translational frameworks. This review establishes a convergent paradigm in which joint ML-guided optimization of guide and delivery design enhances the specificity, efficiency, and safety of next-generation precision genetic medicines.

title: Metabolomics in Cancer Drug-Response Prediction and Target Discovery: From Experimental Models to Clinical Translation.
abstract: Drug response in cancer often remains heterogeneous even among tumors sharing the same genomic driver, indicating that genotype alone does not fully capture the metabolic state underlying therapeutic sensitivity. Metabolomics provides a window into this state by measuring the biochemical consequences of oncogenic signaling, nutrient availability, microenvironmental stress, and drug perturbation, although metabolite abundance does not directly quantify pathway flux. In this narrative review, we examine how cancer pharmacometabolomics is evolving from descriptive biomarker profiling toward drug-response prediction and metabolic target discovery. We organize the evidence across three translational settings: high-throughput cancer models for identifying response-associated metabolic states, patient-derived and in vivo systems for testing metabolic dependencies and resistance mechanisms, and clinical cohorts for treatment stratification and longitudinal monitoring. We further examine isotope tracing, spatial and single-cell metabolomics, multi-omics modeling, and causal inference as complementary approaches for interpreting metabolic changes. We propose five non-cumulative evidence checkpoints (E1-E5) spanning treatment-linked association or prediction, internal evaluation, independent corroboration, source/pathway or target-specific perturbation evidence, and prospective clinical utility. Convergent evidence from predictive modeling, tracer-informed pathway analysis, cross-model corroboration, and genetic or pharmacological perturbation can strengthen target hypotheses. The proposed checkpoints provide a qualitative appraisal framework rather than a formally validated score, and clinical signatures still require independent evaluation before routine use.

title: Deciphering the Mechanisms Underlying Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer through Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Technologies: Current Approaches and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies are recent high-throughput sequencing advancements that enable transcriptome-wide profiling and characterization of cellular populations at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue spatial context. Their integration has been increasingly applied to cancer research, facilitating a deeper understanding of tumor biology and improving diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Growing evidence suggests that combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with ST offers a robust approach for exploring mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance. Together, these technologies support the prediction and monitoring of treatment responses and help identify novel therapeutic targets by revealing critical signaling pathways and immune cell populations associated with resistance. Artificial intelligence, including deep learning, computer vision, and generative models, further enhances the integration and analysis of data generated by scRNA-seq and ST, contributing to tumor resistance research. This review summarizes recent advances in the integrated application of scRNA-seq and ST to study tumor resistance and discusses the opportunities, challenges, and future directions of these technologies as a theoretical foundation for identifying therapeutic targets and developing treatment strategies.

title: Source Geometry and Receiver Ascertainment Limit Spatial Perturbation Inference.
abstract: Spatial perturbation assays locate targeted cells, but neighboring-cell responses can also reflect tissue structure, imperfect guide detection, and dependent sampling. We evaluated these alternatives with a spatial perturbation field diagnostic workflow combining independently specified receiver scores, spatial adjustment, and explicit source references. In 3 Spatial Perturb-Seq chips spanning 4 mice, a Clu -associated score was not exceptional under the stricter reference; training-only mouse holdouts also failed to establish stable program transfer. Known-effect injections showed that refitting spatial background retained 73.7% of the contrast gain at a 150-μm decay scale and 63.3% at 600 μm. In a separate count-level simulation, 3.82% receiver contamination by missed sources produced 33/100 zero-field rejections with source-autonomous expression changes, versus 3/100 without them. Perturb-map stromal contrasts were positive in 2 animals, but dependent sections, unresolved clone identities, and insufficient matched-placement support prevented population-level confirmation. External assays, injury, and clinical cohorts did not establish broad transportability or incremental prediction. These results distinguish limits in receiver ascertainment, source-reference validity, and biological replication, providing reproducible diagnostics rather than a generally calibrated test of causal propagation.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.
abstract: How artificial intelligence (AI) can be rationally applied to antibacterial drug discovery and development to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains insufficiently defined, particularly across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages. The global emergence and dissemination of AMR are compromising conventional antibacterial therapies, while slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and reliance on single-mechanism drug design further increase the risk of inadequate treatment options. With strengths in multi-omics integration, complex pattern recognition, and structure-guided molecular design, AI offers a promising approach to support next-generation antibacterial development. This review focuses on AI-related strategies for antimicrobial development against bacterial resistance and provides a systematic overview of advances in target identification, molecular design, activity prediction, and clinical translation. Rather than proposing a new theoretical framework, the review introduces a pragmatic synthesis tool for evaluating where AI adds value and where important limitations remain, considering application objectives, data properties, validation depth, biological interpretability, and translational feasibility. Major challenges are highlighted, including data heterogeneity, clonal bias, limited external validation, discrepancies between in vitro activity and in vivo therapeutic efficacy, and the absence of regulatory approval for any AI-discovered or AI-designed antibacterial agent. Correspondingly, future directions are delineated, including multimodal data integration, explainable AI methodologies, validation through synthetic biology, and coordinated international regulatory efforts. Overall, this review provides a structured overview of how AI can be integrated with rational antibacterial design while considering both its potential and current limitations for addressing multidrug-resistant pathogens.

title: Cell Reprogramming: Therapeutic Advances and Challenges.
abstract: Cell reprogramming, which forcibly alters cell fate, offers a novel therapeutic strategy for various refractory diseases. Unlike previous reviews focused on a single disease context or a single reprogramming modality, this review is organized around therapeutic applications. It summarizes advances in direct reprogramming, partial reprogramming, and cell fusion-induced reprogramming and further compares their mechanisms, challenges in clinical translation, and safety boundaries. In oncology, reprogramming cancer cells into antigen-presenting cells elicits durable antitumor immunity and remodels the tumor microenvironment, whereas converting cancer cells into nonmalignant somatic cells can reduce their malignant phenotype and tumorigenic potential. In neurodegenerative diseases, direct reprogramming has converted fibroblasts or astrocytes into functional dopaminergic and cortical neurons both in vitro and in vivo. In mouse models of progeria and natural aging, partial reprogramming strategies markedly extend lifespan, ameliorate multiorgan pathology, and enhance tissue regenerative capacity. However, the strength and reproducibility of these findings vary across experimental models, and reported therapeutic benefits do not necessarily establish complete, stable, or safe cell-fate conversion. Against this predominantly preclinical background, ER-100 is the first regenerative therapy based on partial epigenetic reprogramming to receive Food and Drug Administration Investigational New Drug approval and enter clinical testing. It therefore provides an important reference point for the transition from animal studies to human trials. Cell fusion-induced reprogramming has context-dependent roles in tumor immunity. Fusion between tumor cells and immune cells may promote malignant progression. In contrast, dendritic cell-tumor cell fusion vaccines and chimeric exosomes can activate antitumor immune responses in preclinical models and early clinical studies. Major barriers to clinical translation include low reprogramming efficiency, an incompletely defined safety window, and the need to select in vivo or ex vivo strategies according to disease context. In addition, insufficient delivery efficiency, poor targeting, and long-term tumorigenic risk remain important constraints on clinical application. Looking ahead, single-cell multiomics and artificial intelligence may help optimize reprogramming factor combinations, while nonviral systems may improve targeted delivery. Integration with tissue engineering may further facilitate clinical translation across oncology, aging, regenerative medicine, autoimmune diseases, and neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled virtual organoids: Digital-twin frameworks for predictive stem cell biology and precision regenerative medicine
abstract: Stem cell and organoid technologies have transformed the study of human development, disease, and tissue regeneration, yet their broader scientific and clinical utility remains constrained by experimental variability, limited throughput, destructive endpoint measurements, incomplete longitudinal tracking, and the difficulty of systematically interrogating complex cell-cell and cell-microenvironment interactions. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal single-cell profiling, high-content imaging, biosensing, and mechanistic simulation are creating the foundations for a new computational paradigm: Artificial intelligence-enabled virtual organoids (AIVOs). We define AIVOs as dynamically updated, biologically constrained digital representations of stem cell-derived organoid systems that integrate experimental data with predictive models to simulate cell-state transitions, tissue self-organisation, perturbation responses, and therapeutic outcomes. Rather than static computational replicas, AIVOs are envisioned as executable digital twins in which virtual cells represent cellular interactions underlying emergent tissue properties. Their proposed architecture comprises five linked stages: Longitudinal multimodal observation, dynamic internal-state estimation, executable virtual-cell and hybrid multiscale modelling, prediction and virtual perturbation, and experimental validation with iterative updating. Longitudinal multimodal measurements provide temporally resolved evidence for estimating cellular and tissue states. These states can be represented in hybrid mechanistic and data-driven models to support trajectory prediction and virtual perturbations. However, no complete AIVO satisfying all of these criteria has yet been demonstrated. Available studies instead largely represent enabling technologies or methodological precedents, with only limited evidence for partial or early AIVO prototypes. Potential applications span developmental biology, disease modelling, precision medicine, and regenerative medicine. AIVOs may prospectively support investigation of lineage and tissue patterning, representation of patient-specific heterogeneity and disease dynamics, virtual evaluation of treatment strategies, and optimisation of differentiation, biomaterial, and graft-design parameters. However, the realisation of AIVOs will require substantial methodological and conceptual advances. Key priorities include standardised longitudinal datasets, interpretable modelling, uncertainty quantification, causal validation, multicentre benchmarking, and assessment of transferability across donors, laboratories, and platforms. Regulatory evaluation will also need to distinguish exploratory simulation from clinically actionable prediction and to define evidentiary standards for digital-twin-supported decision-making. AIVOs may thereby shift organoid research towards more predictive, testable, and adaptive modelling across stem cell biology, disease modelling, drug development, and regenerative medicine.

title: Benchmarking Extended and Unscented Kalman Filters for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Charge Estimation against a Physics-Based Virtual Cell: Effects of OCV Flatness, Initial Covariance and Temperature
abstract: Kalman-filter state-of-charge (SoC) estimators are usually compared in simulations where the same equivalent circuit model (ECM) generates the data and runs inside the filter, and where errors are computed after the measurement update. Both practices flatter the estimators. This paper benchmarks Coulomb counting (CC), the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and the unscented Kalman filter (UKF) against a physics-based virtual cell: an experimentally parameterised Doyle–Fuller–Newman model of a 5 Ah LG M50 21700 cell with lumped thermal dynamics. A second-order RC ECM is identified from a simulated GITT/HPPC test (2.7 mV RMS fitting error) and then used, unchanged, by all estimators. The cell is driven by repeated UDDS and US06 cycles from 90 % to 10 % SoC at 10, 25 and 40 °C and in an aged state, with 10 mV voltage noise, 25 mA current noise and a 50 mA current offset. Errors are computed from the a priori estimate so that the initial error is always counted. With a correct initial SoC, both filters keep the RMSE between 0.39 % and 0.68 %, while CC drifts to 6.7 % over a 6.9 h UDDS test. A 300-run Monte Carlo study without SoC-limit effects shows that the two filters converge equally fast from under-estimated starts, but the EKF is markedly slower from over-estimated starts: with the recommended initial covariance its mean convergence time into a ±3 % band was 166 s (maximum 1110 s) against 1.2 s (maximum 2 s) for the UKF. All slow EKF runs started between 84 % and 93 % SoC, where the OCV slope of the cell falls to about 0.25 V per unit SoC; the EKF linearises at this flat point and applies too small a correction, whereas the UKF sigma points sample the steeper neighbouring regions. An initial covariance that is too small slows both filters by up to two orders of magnitude. At 10 °C, an ECM identified at 25 °C biases both filters by about −1 % to −2.5 %, which no filter tuning removes. The UKF costs about twice the computation of the EKF. The results show when the UKF is actually worth its cost and how the OCV shape of the specific cell should guide that choice.

title: JosuYeregui/Fast_Aging_Simulations: Fast Aging Simulation Tool
abstract: This repository contains the source code for the Fast Aging Simulation Tool. Contents: main.py and utils/: the simulation core, with the cycler (CC, CC-CV, rest and dynamic-profile steps), the algebraic degradation models, and the parameter loading. evaluation.py: a usage example that ages a single cell and plots SEI thickness, active material fractions, plating thickness and capacity. input/: the LG M50 parameter set (YAML). Dynamic_Profiles/: driving profiles (HWFET, NEDC, NYCC, UDDS, US06, WLTC). tests/: the scripts used to produce the results of the paper: tests/Validation/CC/: comparison against the full PyBaMM SPMe with SEI, plating and LAM, and against the adaptive extrapolation method of Sulzer et al. (2,000 cycles). tests/Validation/Dynamic/: comparison against the Sulzer et al. method under WLTC driving cycles (10,000 cycles). tests/Fleet/: the fleet study of 3,200 virtual cells (128 manufacturing samples × 5 usage archetypes × 5 temperatures), with the plotting scripts and result files. The code is written in Python 3.12. The exact package versions used are listed in requirements.txt (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib, PyYAML, PyBaMM and SciencePlots). Installation and instructions to reproduce each result are in README.md.

title: Mouse BMDC E3-ligase Perturb-seq (GSE327057), reprocessed: counts and per-perturbation differential expression
abstract: Cell x gene counts and per-perturbation differential expression for the Geiger-Schuller et al. E3-ligase Perturb-seq screen in mouse bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells (GEO GSE327057; LPS 3 h; 1,130 E3-ligase and partner targets, 3 guides each, plus non-targeting and cutting controls). The data were reprocessed from FASTQ with STARsolo (STAR 2.7.11b; GRCm39, GENCODE M39; GeneFull counts; EmptyDrops_CR) for 45 of the 46 screen channels. Contents: geiger_bmdc_e3_genefull_counts.h5ad: 504,303 cells x 78,348 genes, raw GeneFull UMI counts, per-cell metadata and per-cell guide UMIs; guide assignments were recomputed. per_target_de_long.tsv.gz and per_target_de_matrices.h5: edgeR quasi-likelihood results for each of the 1,130 targets against non-targeting controls (channel-paired pseudobulks, design ~ channel + condition) on a fixed set of 2,300 genes, with FDR within target and across all targets. per_target_summary.tsv, genes.tsv and guides.tsv. Calibration files from 100 non-targeting pseudo-targets: calibration_ntc_pseudotargets.tsv and empirical_fdr_global_calls.tsv; genes with a null false-positive rate of at least 15% are flagged. cutting_control_de.tsv.gz. The model reproduces the published WDR82 to Zeb2os result exactly. README.md describes every file, the reprocessing, guide assignment, the DE model and calibration. MD5SUMS.txt lists checksums. Please cite the original screen when using these data: Geiger-Schuller et al., bioRxiv (2023), https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.01.23.525198, and GEO GSE327057. Results can be browsed gene by gene in the single-cell gene browser (https://github.com/ericmalekos/single-cell-gene-browser).

title: A reproducible artificial-life world for ecological perturbation, inherited agent state, and genotype-derived digital assets
abstract: We introduce CHIMERIA Digital Aquarium v0.1.0, an open computational research environment in which locally acting software organisms move, consume finite resources, interact as grazers and hunters, reproduce, transmit mutable parameters, and produce inspectable descendants. Each organism has persistent identity and a lineage. A bounded energy ledger tracks externally introduced nutrients and modeled dissipation. We present a controlled in-silico intervention study comprising 36 paired random seeds, five experimental arms, and 160 ticks per run. At the end of the intervention window, the reference arm averaged 25.97 grazers, resource deprivation averaged 2.47, and combined oxygen/toxin/temperature stress averaged 0.67. The corresponding paired mean differences were -23.50 and -25.31 organisms, respectively. Under combined stress, grazer extinction occurred in 61.1% of worlds; after the environment was re-stored, the median remained zero despite a mean of 21.33, demonstrating strong between-world heterogeneity. A nonheritable parameter control did not establish a significant adaptive advantage for inheritance under these conditions. Digital specimens also export deterministic vector artwork and 3D meshes derived from their own genome parameters. The approach is auditablebut is not a biologically calibrated virtual cell, a wet-lab organism, or evidence of consciousness. We present implementation details, negative and positive controls, numerical invariants, raw artifacts, threats to validity, and a staged plan toward multiscale and experimentally constrained artificial-life systems
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Equivalent mean activation, different responding fractions: genome-wide Perturb-seq in primary human CD4⁺ T cells
abstract: Derived tables, production code and frozen parameters for the manuscript "Equivalent mean activation, different responding fractions: genome-wide Perturb-seq in primary human CD4⁺ T cells". What this archive contains - data/: the per-gene effect tables for both conditions (mean effect, activation fraction pi, supra-gate intensity mu+, their q values and donor concordance), the reproducible/reallocated set memberships, the three-way class assignments, the effect-size sensitivity strata, the metric dictionary that fixes one value per quantity, and the supplementary result tables (S1-S9) as machine-readable files. - code/: the analysis pipeline that produced them (lane scanning, scoring and gating, the two-part tests, the artefact and robustness analyses, the figure scripts and two machine audits: figure alignment and number consistency). - docs/: frozen parameters, the prespecified decision criteria, the software and hardware record, and the data-source accessions. What this archive does NOT contain Raw sequencing data. The primary dataset is GEO accession GSE314342; the two external compatibility checks use GSE274751 and GSE330295. All are public and are downloaded by the pipeline, not redistributed here. Reproduction python code/g1_analyze.py --lanes-dir --obs-dir --out-dir out --condition Stim48hr --margin 0.20 --fdr 0.05 --panel-frozen panel_frozen.json followed by code/g2_artifacts.py, code/a3_standard_sets.py and code/k4_sensitivity.py for the robustness tables, and the figure scripts in code/ for the figures. Paths are supplied as arguments; nothing is hard-coded to a machine. Units and definitions - mean_effect: standardised mean difference between a gene's cells and the donor's non-targeting cells, in score units (the activation score is not re-standardised; its own SD is 0.331-0.372 after stimulation and 0.243-0.325 at rest). - dpi: activation fraction (cells above the donor-derived gate) minus the same quantity in the controls. - dmup: supra-gate mean score minus control; both are in score units (z-like). - rep_pi / rep_mup / rep_any: reproducible reallocation through the fraction channel, the supra-gate channel, or either, defined as BH-FDR < 0.05 with >=3/4 donor direction concordance. - Mean equivalence is a TOST criterion: every donor's 90% confidence interval (z0.95 = 1.6449) inside +/-0.20 score units (0.56 and 0.71 of the score's own SD in the two conditions). Licences: data CC BY 4.0, code MIT. No newly generated patient data are reported; this is a secondary analysis of public, de-identified data.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: BioMeme: biological response memory for virtual cells — data, code and reproducibility materials
abstract: Data, code and reproducibility materials supporting BioMeme: biological response memory for virtual cells. BioMeme predicts next-dose cellular responses from measured lower-dose states, combining measured responses in the target cell with the same compound’s response in a reference cell line. This collection provides Supplementary Data 1–49, prepared prediction tasks and archived predictions for LINCS Cell Painting, sci-Plex3 and Tahoe-100M, compound folds and reference selections, numerical results, verification records, and source material for five main and twenty-five supplementary figures. The runnable CPU implementation and tutorials remain available in the retained software package and GitHub release v4.22. Collection 4.28 includes current Source Data for all 30 figures and 74 tables, the current figure sources, and fixed-centre scoring of saved sequential-update predictions. Direction error uses one calibration-target centre per fold shared across budgets; the earlier per-budget-centre scores are retained in separately labelled columns. The correction involved no model refitting. Supplementary Data 48 retains all 320 recorded update steps across twelve folds, all three local MSE increases, measured timings and sixty exact archived-prediction checkpoints. The original 4.27 sequential-replay archive preserves its inputs, specification, code and saved predictions. The new sequential-scores archive provides the current scoring code, results and completed independent checks. The replay is an additional historical analysis, separate from the preregistered comparisons. Supplementary Data 49 provides two post hoc Tahoe plate-13 sensitivity analyses: rescoring registered predictions without eight query compounds, and refitting the closed-form models after removing ten compounds from calibration, reference pools and queries. All registered Tahoe decisions are unchanged. The archived neural comparators were not retrained. The independent implementation first reproduced all 520 registered closed-form predictions; complete refitted predictions, specifications, code and full-precision statistics are included. The registered results retain all 337 compounds. The three original data archives, runnable software and original figure source archive remain unchanged. README.md and SUPPLEMENTARY_DATA_INDEX.md identify the appropriate current and historical packages. The runnable implementation is covered by its included MIT licence; upstream data, microscopy, annotations and third-party software retain their own terms. Consult LICENSES_AND_SOURCES.md and the file-level provenance records. No blanket software licence is applied to the mixed-origin collection. Preregistrations: https://osf.io/dmcb9, https://osf.io/kfv42, https://osf.io/8bnvc, https://osf.io/2cgz3 and https://osf.io/vmrfp.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: V3Cell — hESC amniotic-sac organoid brightfield temporal data Data Brightfield temporal sequences of hESC-derived amniotic-sac organoids. Images are 8-bit grayscale PNG crops of single organoids. Each sequence carries one developmental fate label: cavity formation, cavity collapse or non-cavity (cavity_formation, cavity_collapse, non_cavity in folder and file names). Full sequences. All sequences are released at the acquired frame rate: one frame every 15 min over the 48 h observation window (culture time 48-96 h; treatment added at 48 h), i.e. 193 frames per sequence (t000-t192), named <sequence_id>_tNNN.png. The manuscript models use a temporally subsampled version that keeps every 8th frame (frames[::8], frames t000, t008, ..., t192), giving 25 frames at 2 h intervals. The subsampled version is not shipped separately because it is exactly this slice. Imaging: DeltaVision Elite microscope (Applied Precision), 10x objective, brightfield, stage-top incubator at 37 C and 5% CO2; one frame every 15 min for 48 h. Files File Content Sequences (cavity formation / cavity collapse / non-cavity) amniotic_sequences_full.tar EHDPP (10 uM) and DMSO vehicle-control organoids, 193 frames each, stored as sequences/<fate>/<sequence_id>/. Condition is not recorded per sequence. 266 (31 / 114 / 121) splits.csv Training / test partition of the dynamic model: one row per sequence (sequence_id, fate_class, split, source, n_frames) train 230 (19 / 102 / 109), test 36 (12 / 12 / 12) amniotic_stage1_frames256.zip 6,125 frames (256×256) used to train the static model of amniotic-sac organoids, in the dataset format of the code repository; dataset.json holds the integer class labels: 0 = cavity formation, 1 = cavity collapse, 2 = non-cavity 6,125 frames splits.csv column source: original_pool = sequence from the main labelled pool; heldout = sequence from the separately acquired held-out set (IDs prefixed heldout_). The fate label is also the sequence's folder in amniotic_sequences_full.tar. Which data were used for what Purpose Data Static modeling: the static virtual 3D cell model of amniotic-sac organoids (the basis of the dynamic model) amniotic_stage1_frames256.zip Dynamic modeling (sequence encoder, fate classifier, MotionRNN): training and held-out evaluation amniotic_sequences_full.tar, subsampled to 25 frames (frames[::8]), partitioned by splits.csv (split = train / test); the first 6 frames are the conditioning frames

title: A Two-Gene Single-Cell Signature Refined by Foundation-Model Cell-State Gating Predicts Immunotherapy Resistance in Melanoma
abstract: Immunotherapy has improved the treatment of advanced melanoma, but an estimated 40% to 67% of patients develop resistance, after which survival can fall below 12 months. Current predictors rely on bulk RNA-seq data and large gene panels, which can obscure the cell-state detail revealed by single-cell RNA-seq. To address this limitation, we developed MeloPAIR, a computational framework that predicts melanoma immunotherapy resistance from single-cell transcriptomic data using a two-gene signature of COPE and AGK identified through a genome-wide screen of 6,217 genes in the discovery cohort. We defined an expression index based on the relative expression of these two genes, where positive values indicate a COPE-high/AGK-low pattern and negative values indicate a COPE-low/AGK-high pattern. We then used 512-dimensional single-cell embeddings from scGPT, a single-cell foundation model trained on 33 million human cells, to select a K-means cell state as a gating rule: patients with cells in this state are scored using state-restricted COPE/AGK expression, while all others are scored using the original whole-cell feature. Using a linear support vector machine (SVM), we tested the framework on two independent cohorts, obtaining a discovery AUROC of 0.93 (patient-held-out cross-validation) and an average validation AUROC of 0.89, compared with 0.78 for the two-gene signature without scGPT. Pathway enrichment analysis of the full ranked screen output converged on antigen presentation and MHC class I biology, consistent with the established role of AGK in CD8+ T-cell metabolic function and with COPE’s membership in the COPI coatomer complex, which has been implicated in MHC class I retrograde trafficking. These findings suggest that a minimal two-gene biomarker combined with foundation-model refinement performs comparably to, or better than, substantially larger gene panels in these cohorts. The validation cohorts are small, and replication in larger cohorts and in other tumor types is needed.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Separating mixing from selection: a leave-one-line-out benchmark and an audit protocol for cross-cell-line perturbation evaluation
abstract: Analysis code and derived per-target scores for a leave-one-line-out benchmark of cross-cell-line perturbation prediction. Tier A holds out each of four harmonized cell lines (K562, RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat; 5,486 queries); Tier B holds out each of five heterogeneous lines (H1, K562, RPE1, HCT116, HEK293T; 18,678 queries). The drug panel covers seven to twelve Tahoe-100M lines on 648 or 646 shared conditions, including the twelve-line robustness analyses. Version 1.3.2 is a language revision of the manuscript text; no number, citation, figure, or table changed. Version 1.3.1 rescored the Tahoe coherence and drug-exclusion artifacts with a bounded tie-midrank rule, regenerated the coherence figure and its partial correlations, moved the scGPT comparison to Supplementary Figure S1, renumbered figures, and added a graphical abstract and key points. Version 1.3.0 added metric positive and negative controls, a candidate-pool composition control, and an independent DESeq2 truth-table confirmation for 150 H1 targets, and it regenerated the genetic budget, exchange, and allocation artifacts with the corrected scorer. The archive contains the analysis scripts, summary tables, manuscript source, figures, and the per-target arrays needed to rerun the headline audit. The largest prediction arrays and raw row caches are deposited as separate files. The analysis code is MIT-licensed; derived data and figures are CC BY 4.0. Raw third-party datasets are not redistributed and remain under their original licenses.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Auditing causal gene networks inferred from Perturb-seq with the screens' own controls
abstract: Causal gene networks are now routinely inferred from CRISPR Perturb-seq screens, but their error rates are rarely measured. Curated references cover few regulators, and false-discovery estimates calibrated on noise cannot detect systematic artefacts. perturbaudit turns a screen's internal controls (non-targeting cells, the knockdowns themselves, independent guides, genomic positions and guide sequences) into a verdict for every edge, based on total-effect evidence in the screen. In simulations, decoy-based false-discovery estimates tracked the true false-discovery proportion under noise and confounding, but stayed near zero when a quarter of guides had seed off-targets, while the true proportion among the top 20 edges was 0.44–0.51. Across 480 simulated runs, edges that passed the audit were 80–98% true for three network methods, against 2–12% for flagged edges. We audited 40 networks from seven inference methods on ten panels drawn from public screens. Between 0% and 98% of the top-50 testable edges were not supported by the screen's own knockdown of the claimed parent. Against an all-pairs chance baseline, every genome-scale network was enriched for supported edges (1.8–9.8-fold), while seven method–panel combinations scored at or below chance. In two genome-wide CRISPRi Perturb-seq screens, distant genes with 11–12-nt promoter seed matches were knocked down 6–15% of the time, against about 0.5% expected. K562 edges that passed the audit replicated in three cell lines profiled with the same protocol more often than flagged edges (36 of 36 comparisons) and than random pairs of matched K562 effect size (31 of 36), but less often than the same number of pairs chosen by K562 effect size alone (32 of 36). On an independent platform (HCT116), every edge set transferred poorly, and audited edges did not beat the matched null. The verdicts mark which edges carry intervention evidence in the screen; for predicting other cell lines, the screen's own effect sizes are a stronger simple baseline. perturbaudit is an MIT-licensed Python package, and the seed off-target maps and audit outputs are archived on Zenodo. Preprint (version 1). Supplementary Notes 1-7, Tables S1-S7 and Figures S1-S7 are in the supplementary PDF. Code: https://github.com/mqar96/perturbaudit (release v0.2.1).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.novelty_zh: 利用Perturb-seq筛选自身的对照（非靶向细胞、独立向导、序列脱靶等）为因果基因网络的每条边给出可靠性判定。
llm.summary_zh: perturbaudit 利用筛选内部对照对Perturb-seq推断的因果基因网络逐边审计，并在模拟与40个网络上评估。模拟中通过审计的边真实率为80%–98%，被标记的边仅为2%–12%。跨细胞系结果显示，审计标记主要反映筛选中的干预证据，预测其他细胞系时筛选自身的效应量是更强的简单基线。

title: Single-Cell Gene Expression Heritability Informed by Gene × Cell-Context Interactions
abstract: This record contains the gene-level variance-component (heritability) estimates generated by scHINT (single-cell gene expression Heritability with gene-by-cell-context INTeractions), described in “Single-Cell Gene Expression Heritability Informed by Gene × Cell-Context Interactions” (Wang et al.). scHINT extends Haseman–Elston regression to single-cell data. It partitions expression variance into main genetic (G), gene × cell-state (G×PC), gene × cell-type (G×CT), individual-level and cell-level components. For perturbation screens, the same model treats the perturbation as the “genotype” term. All files are gzip-compressed tables with one row per gene, gene × cell type, or gene × cell-type pair. Values are variance components on the scale of normalized expression variance. Estimates are unbiased and can therefore be slightly negative. 1. G×Cell-State, ROS/MAP brain snRNA-seq (6 cell types, ~13,500 genes)The data come from the integrated Mathys et al. and Fujita et al. ROS/MAP single-nucleus RNA-seq, covering Exc, Inh, Ast, Oli, OPC and Mic. Estimates use cis-SNPs and five cell-state axes (GxPC1–5). The four files differ only in how cell states are defined. scHINT_ROSMAP_GxCS_PCA_within.txt.gz: PCA within each cell type (primary analysis). scHINT_ROSMAP_GxCS_PCA_across.txt.gz: PCA across all cell types, with shared axes. scHINT_ROSMAP_GxCS_residPCA.txt.gz: residual PCA (residPCA). scHINT_ROSMAP_GxCS_cNMF.txt.gz: consensus NMF (cNMF) program usage scores. 2. G×Cell-State, OneK1K blood scRNA-seq (15 cell types, ~9,800 genes) scHINT_OneK1K_GxCS_PCA_within.txt.gz: PCA within each of 15 immune cell types (CD4, CD8, B, NK and monocyte subsets) in 981 donors. 3. G×Cell-Type scHINT_ROSMAP_GxCT_2_cell_type.txt.gz: G×CT estimated for each pair of ROS/MAP cell types. scHINT_ROSMAP_GxCT_all_cell_type.txt.gz: G×CT estimated jointly across all ROS/MAP cell types in which a gene is expressed (2–6 cell types). scHINT_OneK1K_GxCT_all_cell_type.txt.gz: G×CT estimated jointly across OneK1K cell types (3–14 cell types). 4. Perturbation heritability perturbation_cell_state_controlPCA.txt.gz: genome-wide K562 Perturb-seq (2.06 million cells, 7,189 gene perturbations). It holds perturbation × cell-state estimates for each response gene, with cell-state PCs derived from non-targeted control cells and projected onto targeted cells (primary analysis). perturbation_cell_state_targetPCA.txt.gz: the same analysis with PCs derived from the targeted cells (sensitivity analysis). perturbation_cell_type.txt.gz: multiome Perturb-seq (137,604 cells, 19 transcription-factor knockouts, 10 cell types). It holds perturbation × cell-type estimates for each response gene.

title: vec-license-atlas: a three-layer license atlas for virtual-cell and virtual-embryo work (code / weights / data)
abstract: Three-layer license atlas for virtual-cell and virtual-embryo work. For 27 projects the code license, the weights license and the data terms are recorded separately; every row carries the exact evidence URL, the detection method (GitHub's own license API, the LICENSE text, or the site's terms) and the date checked. Seven common misreadings are corrected against primary text: scPerturBench is GPL-3.0, not MIT; CellVQ and PTV-1 ship no LICENSE file at all, so they are all-rights-reserved rather than open source; OpenFold3 and Protenix are Apache-2.0; RF3 is BSD-3-Clause whose LICENSE.md explicitly covers model weights; cz-benchmarks is MIT behind a non-standard wrapper file. 中文:给虚拟细胞 / 虚拟胎胎领域用的一张三层许可图谱。27 个项目,代码、权重、数据三层分开记,每行带证据地址、判定方式和核查日期。校正 7 条常见误判,例如 ArcInstitute/state 代码为 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0,权重与输出另有一份非商业许可并叠加 Acceptable Use Policy,共三层三套条款;scPerturBench 实为 GPL-3.0; CellVQ 与 PTV-1 仓库内没有 LICENSE 文件。 Includes a zero-dependency query CLI (tools/licctl.py), a rebuild and invariant checker (tools/build.py --check), seven invariant tests that run without pytest, and a companion page quoting the Virtual Embryo Challenge data terms (section 14: the dataset is unpublished, so any use in a publication or public presentation needs prior approval from Dr. Neil Chi's group at UCSD). Not legal advice: every row links to the primary text, and rows whose primary text could not be reached are marked confidence=reported rather than guessed.

title: CAPE: benchmarking cross-state perturbation prediction in primary human CD4+ T cells
abstract: Technical benchmark report evaluating CAPE, a neural residual model over a frozen Ridge baseline, on public CD4+ T-cell CRISPRi data across six pooled and 18 donor-partition transfers. After model-selection freeze, CAPE reduced calibration weighted mean squared error in all six pooled and 17 of 18 donor transfers, with metric-specific tradeoffs in centered cosine and uncertainty ranking. The report presents validation and calibration results, matched ablation interpretation, scope limits and aggregate result tables. The transfer tasks reuse four donors and are not independent biological replicates; locked-test responses remained unopened. Athena Sharma implemented the benchmark, evaluated the results and prepared the report. Shodh AI provided computing resources. This report has not undergone peer review. This deposit includes the report and supplementary aggregate tables and plotting files. CC BY 4.0 applies to the original report text and figures; third-party materials retain their own terms.
