title: Accelerating physics-based battery aging simulations by orders of magnitude via analytic decoupling
abstract: Physics-based models capture the mechanisms behind battery aging, but coupling them with degradation kinetics produces stiff equation systems that limit how many cycles and conditions can be studied. We show that, under reasonable quasi-steady-state assumptions, the electrochemical states that drive degradation can be written as algebraic expressions, so the rates of solid electrolyte interphase growth, lithium plating and particle cracking are integrated piecewise within each cycle without a numerical solver. Against a reference physics-based simulation, the framework reproduces two different degradation paths over 2,000 cycles over 1,200 times faster, keeping the capacity within 5\% of the reference. Under dynamic driving cycles, 10,000 cycles are computed in 0.18~s instead of an estimated 188 CPU days, and a fleet of 3,200 virtual cells is simulated in under a minute. This enables lifetime studies so far hindered by the computational cost of physics-based models.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Modeling gene regulation across cellular contexts with deep learning
abstract: Understanding how cells regulate gene expression is a longstanding goal of biology. Deep learning has advanced this effort through sequence-to-function models that predict functional genomic measurements from DNA and cell state models that learn patterns of coordinated gene expression. Connecting these approaches could help predict how sequence effects depend on the cellular environment and how regulatory sequence shapes responses to regulator perturbations. Here, we review emerging approaches to joint modeling and examine how biological measurements, model design, and training data shape the regulatory relationships they can learn. We discuss evaluations that test generalization to unmeasured sequences and cellular conditions, alongside interpretation methods that generate mechanistic hypotheses. We then consider how incorporating cellular dynamics could help predict the propagation and persistence of regulatory responses. Finally, we discuss how pilot scaling studies could guide data acquisition and how AI agents could support model development, interpretation, and experimental design.

title: perturb-audit v0.1.0: a prototype CLI for task-aware auditing of genetic-perturbation prediction evaluations
abstract: perturb-audit is an experimental Python command-line tool that examines selected evaluation-integrity risks in genetic-perturbation prediction workflows. Given an AnnData file, a declared train/validation/test split and a declared task (unseen perturbation, unseen combination, random cell), and optionally condition-level predictions, it checks condition labels and controls, split consistency, condition overlap (including order, case and separator variants), shared-gene dependence among test combinations, batch sharing, prediction alignment and suspicious agreement with held-out means. It also computes descriptive training-only baselines and writes a report, a reproducibility receipt and an RO-Crate-style manifest. Status: prototype. It reports PASS, FAIL, WARN or NOT_RUN per check and never states that a model is good; a result of no detected violations is not evidence that a release is free of leakage. It is tested with 45 automated tests (synthetic planted violations and clean controls) and was run on three splits of one public dataset (Norman 2019, PerturBench processed file). It has not been peer reviewed, it overlaps existing tools (for example DataSAIL and PerturBench's own checks), and its baseline metrics are not identical to PerturBench's official metrics. Limitations are listed in the README.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.summary_zh: perturb-audit 是一个实验性命令行工具，针对遗传扰动预测评估检查标签、划分一致性、条件重叠、共享基因依赖等风险，并生成报告与可复现记录。工具目前为原型，已在Norman 2019的三种划分上运行，并附45个自动化测试。

No wet-lab experiment was performed; the shared latent developmental time axis was never fitted; H2 is reported as not confirmed as a uniform null, with partial evidence against, and not formally falsified. title: Analysis code and derived data for: Benchmark properties, not method differences, dominate cross-context perturbation prediction
abstract: Analysis code and derived data for the paper of that title. Contains the code that produces every number and figure, the loaders that build the derived response matrices from eight previously published CRISPRi screens, every results JSON the figures read, the derived matrices and their independent halves, and resolvability.py, a standalone diagnostic that reports whether the gaps in a leaderboard exceed its own sampling noise. The eight primary screens are not redistributed here; they stay with their own deposits (figshare+ 10.25452/figshare.plus.20029387, GEO GSE264667, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18460279, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7041849, and Hugging Face Xaira-Therapeutics/X-Atlas-Orion). The loaders in code/loaders/ turn those deposits into the matrices, so the chain from public data to published figure is complete. See README.md for layout, the three software environments, and the reproducibility note on anchor-draw seeding.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: ПРИМЕНЕНИЕ ВИРТУАЛЬНЫХ ЛАБОРАТОРИЙ В ПРОЦЕССЕ ПРЕПОДАВАНИЯ БИОЛОГИИ: ОЦЕНКА ЭФФЕКТИВНОСТИ И ОБРАЗОВАТЕЛЬНЫХ ВОЗМОЖНОСТЕЙ
abstract: В статье рассматриваются возможности применения виртуальных лабораторий в процессе преподавания биологии в высшей школе. Исследование направлено на оценку эффективности использования цифровых лабораторных платформ при организации практических занятий и их сравнение с традиционным методом обучения. В исследовании приняли участие 22 студента первого курса, обучение которых проводилось в течение 14 недель в рамках двух последовательных этапов. Для оценки результатов использовались входное и итоговое тестирование, анкетирование, а также анализ отзывов студентов. Особое внимание уделяется использованию платформ LabXchange, PhET, Labster, PraxiLabs, VCell и BioDigital Human. Полученные данные позволяют рассмотреть возможности виртуальных лабораторий для повышения наглядности учебного материала, интереса студентов к практическим занятиям и понимания биологических процессов.
venue: In The World Of Science and Education
published_venue: In The World Of Science and Education

llm.novelty_zh: 教育研究，将虚拟实验平台用于生物教学，不涉及算法新颖性。

llm.why_it_matters_zh: 与虚拟细胞的计算建模没有直接关系，仅涉及教育层面的虚拟实验应用。
llm.limitations_zh: 样本量仅22人，且摘要未提及对照组的分配方式。

title: cellDiffGen: Input Data, Training and Prediction Results
abstract: Dataset 1: Demo Example This demo is using a plant single-cell dataset (PMID: 37055554) (Dataset 2) and to show how CellDiffGen predicts changes in cell state over time. The model is trained on cluster 0 cells from Day 12 and Day 21, then used to predict Day 21 cluster 0 cells from held-out Day 12 cells. To measure prediction performance, the generated cells are compared with the real held-out Day 21 cluster 0 cells. Data split: the cluster 0 cells from each day (Day 12 and Day 21) are split into two subsets:80% are used for training.20% are held out for prediction and evaluation.Genes: each cell has expression values for 39,337 genes. Dataset 2: using a plant single-cell dataset (PMID: 37055554) Dataset 2 zip file 1: (experiment0_plant.zip ) CellDiffGen and Squidiff were seperately trained and used for day-level prediction in the full gene space. Each task holds out one time point, trains on the other two, and predicts the held-out day. The commands are included in commands_scripts/ .There are three task folders, and each one has a CellDiffGen result (celldiffgen_method/) and a Squidiff result (squidiff_method/) and input in (input/):(1) trained on Day 12 and Day 21 to predict Day 0 from Day 21.(predict_day0/)(2) trained on Day 0 and Day 21 to predict Day 12 from Day 21.(predict_day12/)(3) trained on Day 0 and Day 12 to predict Day 21 from Day 12.(predict_day21/) Dataset 2 zip file 2: (experiment0_extension_plant.zip ) This tests how the number of genes affects prediction. CellDiffGen and Squidiff were seperately trained on Day 0 and Day 21 data and used to predict Day 12 from Day 21. Genes were selected as the top n (200 to 30000) highly variable genes in Scanpy.Training and prediction were repeated at each of these gene counts: 200, 500, 2,000, 5,000, 10,000, 20,000 and 30,000.Results: CellDiffGen results (celldiffgen_method/) and Squidiff results (squidiff_method/), so the two methods could be compared. The commands are included in commands_scripts/ , input files in input/ . Dataset 2 zip file 3: (experiment1_plant.zip ) Data split: Day 12 and Day 21 cells were each split at random into 80% for training and 20% for testing. The two 80% training sets were combined for training. At inference, the held-out 20% of Day 12 cells were used to predict the held-out 20% of Day 21 cells. CellDiffGen and Squidiff were trained and used for prediction separately. All analyses use the full gene space. The commands are included in commands_scripts/ , input files in inputs/ .Number of predicted cells:fixed_cells: the number of predicted cells equals the number of held-out Day 12 cells (the test input).CellDiffGen results: celldiffgen_method_fixed_cells_infer/ .Squidiff results: squidiff_method_fixed_cells_training_and_infer/ .flexible_cells: the number of predicted cells equals the number of held-out Day 21 cells (the prediction target).CellDiffGen results: celldiffgen_method_flexible_cells_infer/ .Training and prediction: the models were trained on all cells. Predictions come in two forms:(1) All cells: folders without "cluster" in their names(2) Each cell type: folders named cluster0 to cluster14 (except cluster11) Dataset 2 zip file 4: (experiment3_plant.zip ) CellDiffGen and Squidiff were seperately trained and used for prediction.Training: the models were trained on cells from clusters 0, 7 and 11 at Day 12 and Day 21.Prediction: the trained models predicted every day in between, from Day 13 to Day 20, with 2,000 predicted cells per cluster for each day.Results: CellDiffGen results (celldiffgen_method/) and Squidiff results (squidiff_method/), so the two methods could be compared. The commands are included in commands_scripts/ , input files in input/ . Dataset 3: using single-cell transcriptomics dataset of iPSC differentiation (PMID: 32041960) Dataset 3 zip file 1: (experiment4_ipsc.zip )Combinatorial perturbation prediction: the task is to predict the effect of a double perturbation (gene 1 + gene 2) from the control and single-perturbation cells.Groups:Group 0: control (ctrl), Group 1: gene 1 alone (ZBTB25 + ctrl), Group 2: gene 2 alone (PTPN12 + ctrl), Group 3: double perturbation (PTPN12 + ZBTB25).Experiments:(1): trained on Groups 0, 1 and 2. Predicts Group 3 from Groups 0, 1 and 2(2): trained on Groups 0, 1, 2 and 3. Predicts Group 3 from Groups 0, 1 and 2(3): trained on Groups 0, 1 and 2. Predicts Group 3 from Group 3 cells Dataset 3 zip file 2: (experiment5_ipsc.zip ) CellDiffGen and Squidiff, were each trained on Day 0 and Day 3 data, then used to predict cell states at the other time points. Data: original_data/: the original dataset; input/: the model input, restricted to 203 genes. It has 1,200 cells each for Day 0 and Day 3, and 600 cells each for Day 1 and Day 2. Also include their commands in commands_scripts/ .Day-label conditioning: no_paga/ , Here the models are conditioned on discrete day labels. Folder (no_paga/celldiffgen_method/training_results/): the CellDiffGen trained on Day 0 and Day 3. Folder (no_paga/celldiffgen_method/prediction_results/): predictions from the trained model for four tasks: predict day 1 from day 0, predict day2 from day 0, predict day3 from day0, predict day2 from day1. Folder (no_paga/squidiff_method/): the same training and the same four prediction tasks, using Squidiff.Pseudotime conditioning: with_paga/ , Here the models are conditioned on PAGA-derived pseudotime instead of day labels. The folder is laid out the same way as no_paga/, with one subfolder each for CellDiffGen and Squidiff. Dataset 3 zip file 3: (experiment5_extend_ipsc.zip )Training: the models were trained on Day 0 and Day 3 data at each of these gene counts: 100, 200, 203, 250, 300, 400, 500, 1,000, 2,000, 5,000, 10,000 and 11,231 (all genes). Prediction: based on addtional test data Day 0 to predict Day 3, with 600 predicted cells, also used for prediction at each of these gene counts: 100, 200, 203, 250, 300, 400, 500, 1,000, 2,000, 5,000, 10,000 and 11,231 (all genes).Results: CellDiffGen results (no_paga/celldiffgen_method/) and Squidiff results (no_paga/squidiff_method/) so the two methods could be compared. Input script in (input/) and input data in (no_paga/input/), their commands in commands_scripts/ . Dataset 4: using Mouse embryo development dataset (PMID: 41702400) Dataset 4 zip file 1: (experiment6_mice.zip ) All analyses use the full gene space (55,450 genes), and the cells are split at random into 70% for training and 30% for testing. Two experiments:(1) Effect of training time points: the models were trained on only two days, with all tissues included. Predictions for all tissues are included, with 5,592 predicted cells.(2) Training data scalability: training used days 7 to 18, leaving out Day 19. The day vector is defined by Day 7 and Day 18. Scores and performance are reported for each training data size.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.novelty_zh: 用 CellDiffGen 预测留出时间点的细胞状态变化，并在全基因空间中与 Squidiff 比较。
llm.summary_zh: 该条目为 CellDiffGen 的输入数据、训练与预测结果，以植物单细胞时间序列数据预测留出天数的细胞状态，并与 Squidiff 对比。文中还考察了基因数与细胞数对预测的影响，并附有运行命令与结果文件。

title: PerturbTrust: derived results and analysis code for single-cell perturbation prediction
abstract: Derived results and analysis code for PerturbTrust, a matched evaluation of single-cell perturbation prediction. The archive includes Replogle evaluation scores, target-level contrasts, sensitivity analyses, scoring scripts, an input inventory and SHA-256 checksums. The included scores support independent summary recalculation. Rescoring from frozen predictions requires separately archived input arrays.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.novelty_zh: 公开单细胞扰动预测匹配评估的派生结果、评分脚本与校验和，以支持独立复算。
llm.summary_zh: PerturbTrust 归档包含 Replogle 评估分数、靶点级对比、敏感性分析、评分脚本、输入清单与 SHA-256 校验和。作者称已有分数支持独立汇总复算，而基于冻结预测的重新评分还需单独归档输入数组。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为扰动预测评估的可复现性提供了实际材料，便于审查评分细节。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要明确指出，基于冻结预测的重新评分需要另行归档输入数组，当前归档不完整。

title: Intermediate files, scores, features and saved predictions for 'Cell number and effect scores in the evaluation of CRISPRi perturbation models'
abstract: Intermediate files, score files, features and saved predictions of the article 'Cell number and effect scores in the evaluation of CRISPRi perturbation models'. With them, the analyses of the code repository (https://github.com/mehrdad-shoeibi/crispri-cell-number-scores, release v1.0.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24489831) can be rerun from their intermediate files, and the reported statistics can be recomputed from the saved predictions without refitting the models. README.md describes the eleven archives, how to unpack them, which commands of the code repository run from them, the differences from the records of the code repository, and the sources of the data with their terms. MANIFEST.tsv lists every file with its size and SHA-256, and ARCHIVES.tsv gives the checksums of the archives. The files derive from the Virtual Cell Challenge 2025 H1 data (Arc Institute, Arc Virtual Cell Atlas, CC0 1.0), the Perturb-seq screens of Replogle and Weissman (2022, CC BY 4.0), DepMap 24Q4 Public (CC BY 4.0) and the GenePT gene vectors (Chen, 2024, CC BY 4.0). Please cite these sources when you use the files. Licence: CC BY 4.0, with one exception. The archive features_stack.tar holds outputs of the Stack model (Stack-Large, Arc Institute). They are passed on under the terms of the Stack model licence for outputs; a copy of that licence is STACK_MODEL_LICENSE.md. As that licence asks, a redistribution of these outputs must carry this citation: Adduri, A. et al. (2025) Predicting cellular responses to perturbation across diverse contexts with Stack. Results computed from Stack features are in predictions.tar and fall under the same citation.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.novelty_zh: 主要发布已有论文的中间文件与评分结果，本身不提出新的建模方法。
llm.summary_zh: 该记录包含论文「Cell number and effect scores in the evaluation of CRISPRi perturbation models」的中间文件、评分、特征与保存的预测结果，可在不重新拟合模型的情况下复现统计量。数据来源包括Virtual Cell Challenge 2025 H1、Replogle等Perturb-seq筛选与DepMap 24Q4。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 使细胞数与效应评分对CRISPRi扰动模型评测的影响可被独立复核。
llm.limitations_zh: 归档内容以复现材料为主，摘要未提及对评分方法本身的新结论。

title: scfm-audit: code and donor-level data for ancestry audits of single-cell foundation models
abstract: Code and donor-level data for the manuscript Cohort design, regularization and readout choice in ancestry audits of single-cell foundation models. The package contains L2-normalised donor centroids for five embeddings (UCE, scGPT, Geneformer, State and a 2,000-gene expression reference) in two cohorts (Randolph, GEO GSE162632, 90 donors; Indonesia, CZ CELLxGENE, 199 donors), the four readouts with permutation-calibrated nulls, donor subsampling confidence intervals, all pairwise model contrasts, dimension-matched and age-adjusted sensitivity analyses, and the code that reproduces Table 1 of the manuscript. Readouts: leave-one-donor-out kNN accuracy, unregularized and Ledoit-Wolf linear discriminant, cell-type-conditioned PERMANOVA excess R-squared with 2,000 donor-label permutations, and an uncalibrated top-PC variance share. Code: code/readouts.py, code/run_benchmark.py. Data: data/donor_centroids.npz with data/donor_centroids_index.json. See README.md for reproduction instructions.
affiliations: West China Hospital of Sichuan University
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: "Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease" - Logical Review & Gap Analysis
abstract: This report is an independent review of the paper "Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease" (Amrute, Lee, Eres, Yamawaki et al., to Stitziel; corresponding authors Amrute and Stitziel). The paper was published online in "Nature" on 25 November 2026 (per the Nature page; see 0.6), DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-11275-z. No print issue was seen. The report sets out 15 claims, consolidates 11 author-stated limitations, adds 11 Gaps in the reasoning structure and 17 checking notes, and analyses how the limitations and Gaps affect each claim. It then assigns a provisional confidence level to each scientific claim, using the method and templates of the Section Zero system (Scientific Knowledge Trust Governance). The paper's central claims have three parts: - 11,269 chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) in four cell types of human coronary arteries, including smooth muscle cell (SMC)-specific caQTLs that intersect disease variants (C4, C6). - A mechanism for rs658956, rs4887091 and AMOTL2 linking variants to enhancers and genes through Hi-C, ChIP and CRISPRi (C7, C13–C15). - Enhancer perturbation by Perturb–seq converging on an extracellular matrix remodelling program (C11, C12). The report finds the paper presents a novel cell-type-level map. Multiome data from 44 coronary arteries, cell-type-specific caQTLs, Hi-C from 15 arteries and enhancer perturbation in HCASMC are placed in a single variant → enhancer → gene framework. The paper does not appear to state that this is the first such map. The main Gaps are: - The lead variant differs from the variant selected at the FGGY-DT locus (G1). - The FMC score and "dynamic" inference drawn from a static snapshot (G2). - No GWAS–caQTL colocalization (G3). - "Specificity" inferred from unequal statistical power (G4). - Scope of human samples and cultured-cell background (G5). - A convergence program measured in one experiment, with replicates split from cells (G6). - Inferential design of bulk-tissue Hi-C (G7). - Batch control and technical noise (G8). - Data integrity across text, figures, tables and the Reporting Summary in the CRISPRi, proliferation, CTCF and AMOTL2 chains, broken down into G9.1–G9.8 (G9). For same-context reproducibility, the relevant Gaps are G1–G4 and G6–G9. Extension directions include more cohorts, more cell backgrounds, allele editing and longitudinal data (G1, G2, G5, G9). The report also examines the validity scope of the interpretive framework: scE2G, the FMC score and the "inherent" scale (G10). These Gaps are not meant to refute or diminish the paper. They are directions for further development toward claims of higher confidence, for R&D and applications. The report has limitations. The materials accessed were: - the main paper (41 pages, including Fig. 1–5, Methods, Extended Data figures and supplementary figures); - MOESM1 (Supplementary Information; 14 pages); - the Reporting Summary (MOESM2; 8 pages); - Supplementary Tables 1–50 (MOESM3; a compressed archive of tables). No Peer Review File was among the materials, and the article page has no link to a Peer Review File or to Source Data. The GEO and dbGaP data repositories and the GitHub code repository were not read (CN17). The Reviewer is not a narrow-field specialist. AI was used to lay out content, cross-check the full text, recompute numbers from the Supplementary Tables and help detect logical gaps; the Reviewer checked and decided the content (details in 0.8, Re_L2). The Reviewer's own confidence is Medium. Keywords: coronary artery disease; GWAS; chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL); single-nucleus multiome; enhancer–gene linking (scE2G); CRISPRi; Perturb–seq; Hi-C; CTCF; AMOTL2; logical review; gap analysis; provisional confidence; Section Zero
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.novelty_zh: 新意在于对一篇 Nature 论文（冠心病单细胞 variant→enhancer→gene 图谱）做结构化逻辑审阅与缺口分析，并给出分claim的临时置信度，方法论（Section Zero 模板）有一定新颖性，但并非新的科学数据或建模方法。
llm.summary_zh: 本文是对论文 "Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease" 的独立逻辑审阅报告，梳理了15条主张、11条作者自述局限和11个推理缺口，并为各主张给出临时置信度。被审论文涉及冠状动脉 caQTL、Hi-C、CRISPRi 与 Perturb-seq 的增强子-基因连接分析。报告的重点是评估证据链与可复现性，而非提出新的建模或数据。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该报告系统指出了单细胞增强子-基因连接研究中常见的推理跳跃（如静态快照推断动态、统计功效差异被解读为特异性），对评估类似 GWAS-caQTL-enhancer 研究的证据强度有参考价值。与虚拟细胞主线的直接关联较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 报告仅基于被审论文的正文、补充材料和 Reporting Summary，未读取 GEO、dbGaP 与 GitHub 代码仓库，且未获得 Peer Review File 与 Source Data；作者自称部分内容经 AI 辅助生成，审阅者自评置信度为中等。

title: Do single-cell foundation models annotate immune cells less accurately for donors of African ancestry?
abstract: Analysis code for a preregistered evaluation of four single-cell foundation models (Geneformer, scGPT, UCE, scFoundation) and three baselines (PCA, scVI, CellTypist) on African American and European American donors. Includes the preprocessing, embedding, classification, statistics and figure scripts, conda environment files, the preregistration and the deviations log
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.novelty_zh: 将单细胞基础模型（Geneformer、scGPT、UCE、scFoundation）与经典基线并置，专门检验免疫细胞注释在非洲裔与欧洲裔供体间的准确性差异，即从人群公平性角度评测细胞基础模型。
llm.summary_zh: 该条目是一项预注册评测的分析代码发布，比较四个单细胞基础模型（Geneformer、scGPT、UCE、scFoundation）与三个基线（PCA、scVI、CellTypist）在非洲裔美国人与欧洲裔美国人供体上的免疫细胞注释表现。材料包括预处理、嵌入、分类、统计与绘图脚本、conda 环境文件、预注册文档和偏离记录。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 这是少见的从人群祖源公平性角度系统审视细胞基础模型的工作，提示模型表征可能对不同祖源供体存在偏差，对临床与泛人群应用有现实意义。预注册与偏离日志也提升了评测的可信度。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要仅描述代码与材料发布，未给出具体数据集规模、准确率数值或统计结论，因此无法判断偏差的大小与显著性；摘要未提及所用数据集名称。

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Graph-Structured Small-Molecule Drug Discovery and Development with Deep Learning
abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery remains a cornerstone of modern therapeutics, yet traditional development pipelines are often limited by high costs, long timelines, and low success rates. Recent advances in graph-structured deep learning have significantly transformed the modeling of molecular structures, biological interactions, and pharmacological responses. By naturally representing molecules as graphs, these approaches provide an effective framework for capturing structural, geometric, and physicochemical information across multiple biological scales. In this survey, we present a comprehensive review of recent advances in graph-structured small-molecule drug discovery and development. To provide a unified perspective, we organize the literature into a four-layer framework covering data resources, representation learning, task formulation, and downstream applications. We first summarize the evolution of molecular representations from molecular sequences and topological graphs to geometric structures, molecular dynamics, and electronic field representations. We then introduce a unified task formulation covering six major tasks: molecular property prediction, drug-target interaction and affinity prediction, drug response and perturbation prediction, drug-drug interaction prediction, molecular generation, and molecular optimization. Building upon this framework, we review recent developments in graph neural networks, geometric learning, diffusion models, and foundation models. Finally, we summarize representative benchmark datasets and evaluation resources, and discuss several key challenges, such as out-of-distribution generalization and data scarcity, together with promising directions for future research.
affiliations: Agency for Science, Technology and Research
venue: Transactions on Graph Intelligence and Network Applications
published_venue: Transactions on Graph Intelligence and Network Applications

llm.novelty_zh: 系统综述基于图结构的小分子药物发现深度学习方法，并按数据、表征、任务和应用四层组织。
llm.summary_zh: 综述梳理了分子表征从序列、拓扑图到几何结构的演进，并将小分子任务划分为六类，包括性质预测、药物靶标相互作用、药物响应与扰动预测、分子生成和分子优化。作者还总结了图神经网络、扩散模型和基础模型在这些任务中的进展。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该综述为图学习在小分子设计中的应用提供了统一框架，其中的药物响应与扰动预测部分与虚拟细胞方向有交叉。
llm.limitations_zh: 作为综述，摘要未提供各方法在统一基准上的定量比较。

title: Artificial Intelligence Assistance with CRISPR to Optimize Drug Development
abstract: Drug development remains a costly and time-consuming process since identifying therapeutic targets that are both biologically relevant and clinically effective remains challenging. New technologies including bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, CRISPR screens and AI are enabling new target discovery opportunities, but there are still a number of challenges in bringing the heterogeneous data sets together. This paper describes how AI-assisted integration of these three technologies can improve drug development. This paper explains in detail how Bulk RNA sequencing can detect differentially expressed genes, how Single-cell RNA sequencing can uncover cell-specific expression patterns, how CRISPR screening can identify dependencies of genes in disease-related phenotypes, and how AI models can recognize complex molecular patterns and prioritize targets for therapeutic intervention using these complementary datasets. With AI support and current technologies, researchers could decrease false-positive target identification and enhance drug sensitivity forecasting. This paper suggest a way to improve the precision-drug-discovery strategies. But there are still issues with data heterogeneity and with model interpretability. To address the remaining challenges, interpretable AI models that combine multi-omics, functional genomic, and patient-derived data should be developed in the future.

llm.novelty_zh: 概述性论文，讨论AI辅助整合批量RNA测序、单细胞测序与CRISPR筛选以发现药物靶点，未给出具体方法或实验。
llm.summary_zh: 文章讨论批量转录组、单细胞转录组与CRISPR筛选数据在药物开发中的作用，并说明异质数据整合的难点。作者认为AI模型可以识别复杂分子模式并排序治疗靶点。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 概括了多组学与CRISPR结合的药物靶点发现思路，但缺少实证支持。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Research Progress of Single-Cell Transcriptome Sequencing Biotechnology
abstract: Traditional bulk transcriptome sequencing can only obtain the average expression signal of a cell population, cannot resolve cellular heterogeneity within tissues, and has difficulty revealing the mechanisms of dynamic changes in cell states and interactions with the microenvironment. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology can resolve whole-transcriptome expression profiles at single-cell resolution, breaking through the technical bottleneck of population averaging, and has become a core disruptive biotechnology in the life sciences. This paper systematically sorts out the technical principles, mainstream experimental platforms, and microfluidic supporting technologies of scRNA-seq, and summarizes the core bioinformatics analysis methods and tool platforms such as single-cell data preprocessing, cellular heterogeneity resolution, and differentiation trajectory reconstruction; it focuses on the application progress of this technology in the construction of the human cell atlas, the resolution of the tumor microenvironment, the tracking of development and differentiation, cell communication analysis, and disease biomarker screening; it summarizes frontier technology directions such as single-cell multi-omics integration, spatial transcriptomics fusion, and CRISPR functional screening, and analyzes the current bottleneck problems of cost, throughput, and data analysis. Finally, combined with the trend of technological iteration, it looks forward to the future development directions of high throughput, low cost, multi-dimensional integration, and clinical translation, aiming to provide a systematic reference for the basic research and biomedical applications of single-cell sequencing technology.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述scRNA-seq实验平台与生物信息学分析的研究进展，本身未提出新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 综述介绍了scRNA-seq的技术原理、主流实验平台与微流控支持技术，并概述预处理、异质性解析与轨迹重建等分析方法。文章进一步讨论了人类细胞图谱、肿瘤微环境、多组学与空间转录组融合等应用，以及成本与通量等瓶颈。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该综述对了解scRNA-seq技术体系与应用现状具有入门参考价值。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要以概述为主，未提供新的定量比较。

title: Machine Learning for Transcription Factor Target Discovery and Drug Intervention: Progress, Challenges and Outlook
abstract: Machine learning now reaches every stage of transcription factor (TF) drug discovery, but its contribution falls sharply along the evidence hierarchy. This review works through five tiers of evidence, from sequence and transcriptome through protein structure, cellular phenotype and chemical matter to clinical validation, and examines recent progress and the strength of evidence at each. Unified models can now predict binding, accessibility and expression within a single framework, and the definition of a ligandable site has widened from a static cavity to a transient conformational state, so disordered regions are no longer excluded a priori. The downstream tiers are far thinner. Molecular generation keeps improving geometric plausibility, but a unified benchmark shows that such metrics do not track the ability to produce active molecules, and no clinical intervention to date can be traced to substantive machine learning input. Missing trivial baselines and information leakage also make retrospective evaluation systematically optimistic. What limits machine learning at each tier appears to be the supply of verifiable labels more than model capacity. TFs sit upstream of regulation, so a single successful intervention may correct an entire downstream expression programme, which keeps them attractive for diseases that still lack usable targets and demanding as a test of algorithmic prediction. On this reading, further gains for TFs and other undruggable targets depend more on what each tier can be made to measure than on new architectures.

llm.novelty_zh: 以证据层级为框架，对转录因子药物发现中的机器学习进展进行分级评估，无新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述按五级证据层级考察机器学习在转录因子药物发现中的应用，涵盖序列、结构、表型、化学物质与临床验证。作者指出分子生成的几何指标与生成活性分子的能力并不一致，且回顾性评估常因缺失基线和信息泄漏而偏乐观。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 指出下游证据层级薄弱，有助于判断AI预测能否转化为转录因子靶向干预。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要提及：可验证标签供给不足，而非模型容量，是各层级的主要限制。

title: Multimodal single-cell analyses reveal distinct fusion-regulated transcriptional programs in Ewing sarcoma
abstract: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is a fusion-driven malignancy, peaking in adolescence. Although EwS tumors are driven uniquely by EWS::FLI1 and related fusions, patient outcomes vary greatly. If and how tumor plasticity of EWS::FLI1-regulated transcriptional signatures contributes to disease progression is not known. To address this, we utilized a single-cell co-assay of RNA and chromatin accessibility (ATAC) sequencing to identify gene regulatory networks in EwS. By comprehensively characterizing regulatory elements across cell lines, we identified multiple unique modules of gene regulation. Differential usage and prevalence of these modules was evident across cell lines, associated with distinct epigenetic and transcriptomic signatures, and in specific cases, modifiable by exogenous TGF-β. When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks. Our findings demonstrate that multiple, co-existing transcriptional programs shape the phenotypic diversity of EwS and suggest that the balance between these networks may have important implications for clinical outcomes and targeted therapy development.

llm.novelty_zh: 在尤文肉瘤细胞系中用单细胞 RNA 与染色质可及性共检测，鉴定多个 EWS::FLI1 相关调控模块。
llm.summary_zh: 作者利用单细胞 RNA 与 ATAC 共检测方法，在尤文肉瘤细胞系中识别出多个基因调控模块。这些模块的使用与丰度在不同细胞系间存在差异，部分可被外源 TGF-β 调节，并且在患者肿瘤的肿瘤内与肿瘤间均有分布。研究提示多种并存的转录程序塑造了肿瘤表型多样性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提示肿瘤内调控异质性可能与临床结局及靶向治疗相关。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

Direct lineage conversion of postnatal mouse cortical astrocytes to oligodendrocyte lineage cells.
abstract: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells (OLCs) are lost in many central nervous system (CNS) diseases. Here, we investigate the generation of new OLCs via ectopic expression of Sox10 , Olig2, or Nkx6.2 in mouse postnatal astrocytes. Using stringent analyses, including Aldh1l1-astrocyte fate mapping and live-cell imaging, we confirm that Sox10 and Olig2 , but not Nkx6.2 , convert Aldh1l1 pos astrocytes to induced OLCs (iOLCs). With single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we uncover the molecular signatures of iOLCs. Transcriptomic analysis of Sox10 - and control cultures over time reveals a clear trajectory from astrocytes to iOLCs. Finally, perturbation models CellOracle and Fatecode support the idea that Sox10 drives cells toward a terminal iOLC fate. Altogether, this multidimensional analysis shows bona fide conversion of astrocytes to iOLCs using Sox10 or Olig2 and provides a foundation for astrocyte direct lineage reprogramming (DLR) strategies to promote OLC repair.

title: Adaptation of a graph enhanced deep learning framework for perturbation response modelling informed by head and neck squamous cell carcinoma data
abstract: Background: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterised by substantial genomic and transcriptional heterogeneity. Single cell RNA sequencing can identify malignant programmes but does not directly predict how these programmes will respond to single or multigene changes (perturbations). Aim: This thesis developed and evaluated a reproducible HNSCC adaptation of the Graph Enhanced gene Activation and Repression Simulator (GEARS). Experimentally observed perturbation-response relationships were learned from a non-malignant, non-squamous RPE-1 Perturb-seq dataset, while HNSCC single cell transcriptomic data supplied coexpression structure and programme definitions. The model was informed and interpreted using HNSCC data but was not trained or evaluated using perturbed HNSCC cells. Methods: A fixed panel of 4000 of the 8749 source genes (45.7%) defined the expression data, graph inputs and model outputs; excluded genes could not be modelled. Four graph prior conditions combined either a self-loop or HNSCC-derived coexpression gene graph with the Gene Ontology derived perturbation graph enabled or disabled. Each condition was trained across ten random seeds using matched data splits, producing 40 model checkpoints. Held out RPE-1 performance was evaluated across all genes and condition specific top 20 differentially expressed genes. Programme space analysis then evaluated 11 held out single gene perturbations across all 40 checkpoints, producing 440 perturbation-checkpoint results. G1/S, G2/M, and EMT/invasion were analysed as separate primary transcriptional outcomes. Results: Across graph conditions, test mean squared error (MSE) across all genes ranged from 0.014998 to 0.015058 and mean Pearson correlation from 0.980421 to 0.980480. Performance was weaker for the top 20 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with MSE ranging from 0.096537 to 0.098474 and Pearson correlation from 0.728370 to 0.730569. None of the held out performance or programme level differences between graph conditions was statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. All 11 perturbations had negative mean G1/S and G2/M scores, and 439 of 440 individual scores were negative on each cell cycle axis. The five primary candidates (MRPS26, MPHOSPH10, EIF4A1, INO80C and SNRPE) had negative G1/S and G2/M scores in every checkpoint evaluation. However, all 11 perturbations had positive mean EMT/invasion scores. G1/S and G2/M scores were strongly associated with global predicted transcriptional response magnitude (Pearson r = -0.998 and -0.997, respectively). These associations were largely unchanged after the retained primary programme markers were excluded from the global response calculation. Conclusion: This thesis established a reproducible and audited framework for generating programme-level hypotheses from epithelial perturbation-response predictions. The cell-cycle scores largely tracked overall predicted response magnitude and did not distinguish the five primary candidates by programme-specific effects. Training and evaluation used only RPE-1 responses, leaving HNSCC predictive accuracy untested. The findings do not establish selective cell-cycle modulation, reduced proliferation or therapeutic efficacy. Further development requires perturbation-response data from HNSCC or a more closely related malignant squamous epithelial system, together with biologically appropriate positive and negative controls.

title: Do hub-gene rankings point to the cause? A preregistered test of the DEG–STRING–cytoHubba workflow on CRISPRi perturbations with known targets
abstract: Preregistration of a known-answer test of the hub-gene workflow (differentially expressed genes → STRING network → cytoHubba MCC and Degree ranking). In a genome-wide CRISPRi Perturb-seq screen of K562 cells (Replogle et al. 2022), the perturbed gene is the known cause of each expression change; we test whether hub rankings place the cause above prior-matched decoy genes from the same DEG list. Perturbed genes were split 30/70: the 30% exploration split served as a pilot and set the rules; the 70% confirmation split is held out and will be analysed once, after this registration is public. Files: the protocol (PDF), the code, documents and pilot outputs (zip) with a SHA-256 manifest, and the commit log of the analysis repository.

llm.novelty_zh: 以预注册的已知答案检验，评估DEG-STRING-cytoHubba流程能否识别扰动真因基因，本身无新方法。
llm.summary_zh: 该预注册研究在K562 CRISPRi Perturb-seq数据上检验常用的hub基因工作流能否把已知扰动基因排在诱饵基因之上。数据按30%探索集与70%确认集划分，确认集将在注册后只分析一次。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该研究以已知答案检验常见的生物信息学流程，有助于避免把hub排名误作因果证据。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要仅为预注册方案，未报告确认集的分析结果。
